analysis.name: Andrew  Pun
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I like how he uses the whiteboard since it shows everyone a slower process step by step and I appreciated that. Overall a good teacher, he wants to see his students improve. Tests were representative of what he lectured, as well as discussion section hw, and the lecture slides he provides.

Ochem is hard regardless, even attending lectures I was so confused I feel as though he is too smart to be able to dumb it down more. I personally did good in ochem I and was not expecting to feel so lost and behind in ochem II. The format of exams does not allow for partial credit since only the answer is graded, which makes it very difficult too!

This class is difficult, but Prof Pun provides you with all the resources you need to succeed. He only uses the chalkboard during lecture, which really helps with learning why each step of a mechanism happens. Exams are reflective of problem sets and lecture examples. I was nervous going into this class, but genuinely found it to be kinda fun.

Actually goated. I loved the way he taught the class. He made ochem enjoyable and I loved learning it! I did avg (70%s) on the midterms but lowkey popped off on the final and got an A-. Idk if he curved but I'm assuming he did, although the curve wouldn't be much because all his tests were mc. His tests were a fair representation of the content.

Exams were multiple choice which is kinda strange for an ochem class. Because of this i've tanked points for small errors, but averages were 70 on both midterms. No curve since averages were high. He does a good job explaining things, but building intuition for mechanisms is challenging regardless. Spam practice problems and ur probably fine

analysis.name: Matilde Córdoba Azcárate
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is a clear and engaging lecturer who explains concepts in an easy-to-understand way. Her teaching style is organized and discussion-based, and she encourages participation. She is knowledgeable and makes the material feel accessible to students.

it's literally week 2 and I'm writing this! I'm rating her this early, bc I KNOW she's going to continue to be an amazing prof this fall quarter!!
Work is manageable, and her lectures are entertaining. From what I know... no midterms or finals; just homework!
She's a good professor. Makes class fun and intriguing every time. This class can be an easy elective class for anyone to take fyi

Easy and interesting class that's definitely gonna be a GPA booster
Not a lot of stress for this class
No midterm or final
Lots of readings, but again, it's easy

(ohhhh don't take this profff, she's BADDDD) 
NAHHHH- just leave room for ME so I could take MOREE OF HER CLASSES BEFORE IT GETS WAITLISTED!!

analysis.name: Andreya Perez Silva
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: super sweet and caring professor! participation is graded so definitely show up to class. the midterm and final exams are pretty difficult so be prepared to study a lot. but you get a cheat sheet and she's a lenient grader. also you can redeem your midterm score with your final exam score. overall, take this class but be prepared to put in the work
She's really caring and definitely very easy to talk to! Definitely take her. The ta was also so nice, absolutely loved her.

I love her! She made accounting interesting and gave us multiple opportunities to practice (weekly homework and quizzes). It was a bit of a pain to do it every week, but it really helped the concepts sink in. 15% of the grade was participation so speak in every class! She's so receptive, caring and a great motivator. Would 100% recommend her!!!

This was her first quarter at UCSD and she made a great effort to assist our learning in the class. She wanted to learn all of our names and was accessible for office hours. I bombed my midterm and got a 67% and did all my homework, ending up with a B+ which was amazing. She offers extra credit during class if you go and it really boosted my grade.
The best professor I have had at UCSD. Weekly quizzes and homework that help with midterm and final. She is literally my idol.

analysis.name: Ash Merryman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Merryman is a great professor who is enthusiastic, approachable, and cares about her class environment! The attendance policy is generous, the homework is easily manageable, and all homework can be redone for full credi, although that will likely be unnecessary because of how kind and lenient she is. She's amazing!

CCE 1 was easy and Professor Merryman was so kind and devoted to the course. Participation is semi mandatory (can miss 3 classes max). Lots of assignments and some projects, but they were not difficult, and often my group was able to finish early. We had lots of in class work time. Professor gave great feedback and very accessible outside class.

Prof Merryman is so sweet and understanding, and wants the best for you. She is very lenient (to any extensions) and provides great feedback. Most CCE classes teach the same thing, but she makes the content more enjoyable. They only thing is that I think she makes the students do more in-class discussions/activities compared to the other teachers.

Ash was so kind and caring. I would highly recommend them. Since CCE is regulated by 8th College most of the classes will be similar, but Ash approached CCE 1 with much care and willingness to help. Ash provides amazing feedback on everything and is lovely to work with, especially in this small class setting. Ash is so knowledgeable and it shows

analysis.name: Amina Schartup
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Schartup is a very organized and knowledgeable lecturer who's passionate about what the material. Class is split between exams, homework (which is easy to do), and discussion attendance. She wanted every student to succeed and offered extra credit and a curve for the class. She is also clear about what information will be tested on exams.

Prof. Shartup is very passionate about what she teaches while also caring for her students. She tries her best to make sure everyone does well in the class and is relatively accessible. While she does require a textbook, readings weren't required and midterm questions could be answered without reading the textbook.

Shes a nice person and her slides are very organized and clean. When it comes to answering questions, she doesn't answer and tells you to go watch the lecture. That quickly changed tho when a lot of students complained. She is nice and always willing to listen and adapt to students needs

She has organized lectures and provides non-graded quizzes at the end of some of the lectures. A majority of the questions appearing on the final exam and she goes over them after. Homework is easy and straightforward. Lectures are recorded and slides are posted.

analysis.name: Jon Aycock
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Every single lecture thought nothing.Went too slow at the start and gave no examples then went really fast and didn't explain. Practice exams are nothing like the test, and the tests are nothing like the examples in lectures or textbooks. If you are taking him, read the textbook all by yourself, and even then you might get caught off-guard on tests

My whole friend group failed the class. We got the average grade above on both midterms since we focused on study guides and practice problems. When we got to the final we had the same strategy and got a completely different test that was never on the homework, practice problems, or any past midterms (with the exception of 2 questions).NEVER AGAIN.

professor did not give any relevant review material, always stated that we should "use the textbook & hw problems" as practice, yet the exam was nothing like the questions that we did on the homework. rushed during lecture only to get nowhere and put concepts he covered the lecture before the midterm (didn't even complete the topic) on the midterm

Never again. His policies do not help you succeed at all and on top of that everything is messy and unorganized with most of his sources being ripped from other teachers. i literally saw another midterm for a diff teacher and it was exactly like our practice exam. he makes the exams 10x harder and makes u be prepared for other teachers exams

No cheatsheets, no curve, no calculators. Lectures are confusing, talks about theorems all the time and barely gave examples. Talks about 20A and 20B before gets to 20C and runs out of time. Skips parts of sections, ended up learning almost everything by myself. Exams were difficult, practice exams has nothing to do with the actual one.

analysis.name: Kim Albizati
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 232 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He's highly overrated.  He's somewhat approachable, you just have to remember that he wont answer questions during class time but you can see him after class.  Doesn't really explain mechanisms in detail, teaches it more like a Biology class with memorizing reactions and a general mechanism.  This makes it very hard to understand what's going on.

He is all hype; his curve makes it impossible to get an A (you need to be at least 80 points above average) and he never reveals his grading criteria (his TAs don't know either). Didn't show up for the final review session or the final exam. Exam averages are pretty low but he makes the exams consistently harder. Tells you to try every book problem

hardest curve of all the ochem profs (need at least 80 points above average for an A), very secretive about grading criteria. Gives very few practice problems, no extra credit, no HW, so grade based entirely on exams. Tells you to try every book problem but they are unrelated and not helpful for his class since his question style is so different.

Here are the hard facts: his curve is EXTREMELY difficult; you need to get at least 80 points above average in order to get an A. Never posts grades until AFTER the final so you are left wondering all quarter. Grade based entirely on exams (which are not easy). He puts challenge questions on exams over topics he never covered in class. Overrated.

I think Albizati is kinda overrated. I mean he is funny but sometimes he skips over basic knowledge but expects you to know how to do it on the homework. The material that he does teach is taught very well though. The TAs' quizzes were the hardest part of the class. Albizati doesn't have the best office hours nor does he extend them for finals.

analysis.name: Adam Bowers
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 275 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Yo I don't even need to say much. Can't describe in words besides "if professor Judy Kim was the worst, HE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR IN THE UNIVERSE". Wow, he's such a nice person, he posts all his lecture notes in the website. His notes very understandable. He has that skill to summarize all the complicated math concepts in textbook in his own words concisely so that students get easy time understanding the whole concepts. Exams? Don't worry. As long as you know the basic concepts, you'll pass. Oh

Bowers does not care for your well being at all. I've never been so destroyed by any class in my life. I look around at the faces of the students around me and I can see we are all under a common suffering that bonds us. If there is punishment in the afterlife, it is taking this class for eternity. The midterms hurt more than a broken heart.

Bowers has easy lectures, but his actual exams and homework are much harder than his lecture content. This is because he explains the bare minimum of each concept in class and expects us to show full concept mastery at a high level on the test. Like training kids to walk a 12 minute mile and then making them run a marathon for the final.

The examples he uses in his lectures are like 1+12. However, when it was time to do the homework or the exam, it was totally different than what was expected. I thought I was the only one struggling in the class, but I noticed others around me were too. "We're all in this together..." 50% average for passing on midterms and no curve...
he is the best but the  final was too dificult

analysis.name: Anne Yilmaz
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Yilmaz clearly knows the subject (she keeps reminding you of her expert status). But often questions felt like they were met with annoyance or sarcasm, so it was hard to feel comfortable asking for help. It honestly felt like the class was harder than it needed to be because of the way she communicates. The slides were well made though.

Interesting topic but the class is unnecessarily difficult. Exams are extremely concept-based and require very precise answers that often feel trickier than what is emphasized in lecture. She talks a lot about her own research and can come across as annoyed when students ask questions, which makes the class feel intimidating. Avoid the class.

Exams don't correspond with lecture material. They are significantly more difficult and feel as if she did not teach what appears on exams. Along with her condescending attitude toward students' questions, it feels intentional, as if she does not want students to succeed. The most unrelated exam questions to lectures I have experienced.

I do not recommend taking her class. She goes on personal tangents about her career and "expertise" in eye witness testimony. The textbook readings do not align with the lectures that are for that particular week. Her exams are confusing and not based on lectures or readings. She is unable to answer student questions on material presented.

Avoid this class, this class is heavy on material. TA's didn't know much of the material, student's would ask questions and would often say "I'm not sure" or would look it up in their computer. Honestly if you miss points for HW your grade goes down heavily. I asked professor for help and she direct me to the TA's which didn't help.

analysis.name: Eli Berman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It's the responsibility of a professor to write exams that are balanced enough in difficulty to make a reasonable curve. Berman made the final too easy, then had to curve the class so that a 93 overall grade was a B. Got over 100 on the midterm, over 90 on the final, did homework, still not enough for an A. Awful.

Much harder than other professors teaching 120B. Test questions are designed to confuse and twist concepts around, half the problem is understanding what he's asking. During the first class, he mentioned that he'd give an automatic recommendation to anyone who gets an A in the class--now I see why. Also, not good at explaining concepts.
homework is very lengthy and difficult. exams are almost nothing like the practice exams. pretty sure he also doesn't curve…

He lets you bring a cheat sheet for midterm and final so the exams aren't that hard. Homework is pretty hard but don't weigh as much as exams. Don't really need to go to class since he doesn't explain stuff that well in my opinion. Studying his lecture notes is useful. .

Berman is no slouch, that's for sure. Still, he's a fairly pretentious guy who isn't much help in office hours. Lectures are straightforward; exams aren't. He doesn't deal with the homeworks and half the TAs were only marginally above useless. He also thinks of himself as a comedian. Take him if you want a challenge and/or are a masochist.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Butler
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took the class for a GE, would not recommend. You would think an online class would be easy but no. The weekly reflections do not have clear prompts and the TA does not give helpful feedback either. Seems like there is no communication made between the professor and the TA.When asked for more feedback, they refer you to the writing hub. So helpful.

Definitely the worst class I've taken at UCSD. If you thought this would be an easy GE, think again. Butler has the worst grading system I've ever seen and if you miss a single class you will drop a whole letter grade. She gets too deep about the subject and needs to realize she grades too hard. Do not take this class!!!!!

This is not an easy A class. You need to have your camera on and participate consistently or you'll get called out. Success in the class depends heavily on attendance and engagement. Grading is extremely strict, and lectures can feel very understimulating. Overall, it was one of the worst classes I've taken here.

Genuinely one of the worst professors Ive had here at UCSD. she grades on a scale of 4. readings due everyday before lecture, and a content quiz for every lecture. it is almost impossible to get a 4/4 on ANY assignment without going to the writing hub. if you miss even one lecture the highest grade you can get is a B.

The grading system is not good, and you have to attend every lecture, or your grade automatically drops. The exams are graded very harshly, where you have to give a detailed response while having a strict word limit. It is not an easy online class to take for gen ed, which you would think it is.

analysis.name: Andrew Cooper
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 210 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He's a good professor, but his grading criteria is way too hard. Our exams are all free-response questions, but if you do not mention all things in detail, you would lose score. There are 6 assignments that count for 10% of the total grade, but we cannot drop the lowest one and he still expects us to reach 93% to get an A.

He has a different setup on his syllabus than to what he expects you to do in class. His attendance is unfair. He is a good biology teacher but very restrictive about grading. If you don't answer it like he did he doesn't give you points.

His tests are not fair, while the questions seem simple, he has a very specific set of criteria that you must match to get the questions correct. His grading criteria is unreasonable, and he doesn't take feedback. You may know the subject well but unless you write the test in the specific way he wants you to you will not get points.

Professor Cooper has amazing lectures and has funny comments/thoughts, and doesn't assign reading. However unlike other BILD 1 professors, he does free response exams instead of multiple choice. Moreover, you must know the material and concisely write your answer to get full points. But if you pay attention and study, you'll do great with him.

The criticism is not justified imo, just wait for upper div bio. Grading is generous, especially because extra credit and exam question redos are offered. Prof. Cooper explains concepts well and is a fair grader, my advice is to word things like he does in the lectures.

analysis.name: Quang Bach
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 219 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Terrible professor. His Vietnamese (?) accent makes it hard to understand lectures so dont even bother going to class. There is no cheatsheet on exams and his exam problems are tough. Also no extra credit. He is assuming a lot of previous background on trigs and calc. Expect to read the book if you want to understand lectures.

Bach is objectively friendly but I struggled to understand a lot of what he would say during lecture. Very strong accent! Material reviewed during class or HW didn't correlate to the exam. Posts class notes but doesn't podcast lectures. Independent math learners will thrive but I struggled & will probably have to re-take 20D with another professor.

Bach taught the material well, but his exam questions felt like they were intentionally trying to trick you. When I took this course in fall, it was combined with the other MATH18 classes. I don't know about the other professors, but I liked Anzaldo's lectures better. If you have the opportunity, take her.

If you want to destroy your GPA, take his class. No guidance whatsoever on the exams. You just have to memorize everything from the textbook or squeeze them all in your cheat sheet. His lecture notes are filled with errors. Also, questions on exams are totally different from what we learnt so studying is useless because you're gonna fail anyway.

The professor teaches well if you actually pay attention but his class is a lot of work. We had HW due every week with 20 questions for each HW and no the questions weren't easy. Exams are tough but grading is a bit lenient. Overall, I'd say he's a tough professor since he could make the class easier with less HW and assignments but oh well.

analysis.name: Brian Zid
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 122 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: If you have little/no background in chem (like me) and are scared to jump straight into the Chem 6 series, try taking Chem 6A with this professor! Incredibly kind, fair exams, and he holds a review session before every test emphasizing key topics. Use that info + the extra problems + the crib sheet he posts to make practice tests, it really helps!

Awesome chem prof. chem 6a does have a lot of content, can be hard but he is really helpful during office hours, lectures where useful but confusing at times on certain topics that took me a sec to learn, just do the practice reviews and GO TO DISCUSSION, its not required but no one goes and I treated it as a tutoring session which helped me a lot.

Zid is amazing. He tells you exactly what is going to be on each midterm and the final, and tells you exactly what to study. People who got a bad grade just didn't go to the lecture. Go to the lecture and follow along, and this will be a very good Chem 6A class. The discussion worksheets are also very good and actually helpful. Lecture podcasted.

Brian is, overall, a good professor, but sometimes he explains things in an overcomplicated way or out of order. His lectures are podcasted, and attendance isn't mandatory for the lecture or section (though you do have to do a discussion sheet graded on completion). He gives a practice midterm for the first midterm, but not the second one.

Professor Zid was great!! Very clear slides that make the material pretty simple to understand. Sometimes he goes a bit fast. Two Midterms that are both fairly easy if you study a decent amount. There are no surprise questions, he tells you pretty much everything that will be on the exams. Discussion sections and lectures are not mandatory; podcast

analysis.name: Timothy Brady
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 60 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Nice guy with really great teaching methods. The slides are really informative and, in my opinion, super interesting. 3 Exams were pretty easy, weekly quizzes were very easy, and the weekly experiments are SUPER easy and fun! I definitely recommend this class. Easy A, cool topic, nice professor

This professor is the epitome of giggles and sunshine. He sees light in everything. He laughs at least 500 times a lecture. Super easy exams if you're into psyc content. 10/10 Reccomend. Grade is based on weekly(ish) quizzes, short experiments, and 3 exams. Super simple class

Prof Brady is really nice, and is accommodating if you can't take an exam or assignment for certain reasons and will offer extensions. His lectures are not mandatory but you definitely need to watch the podcast to know what's going on. The only reason why I wouldn't take him again is because his exams are really hard and questions are very long

Best professor I've ever had. His lectures are so so so entertaining and he is really good at explaining very complex concepts. The tests were very predictable and he always emphasized in his lectures exactly what was on the exams. Graded mostly by three exams, but there are easy quizzes and online experiments for another exams worth of points.

Tim is the best professor I have ever had. For the first time, I truly loved going to school. Every lecture had fun experiments. I truly feel like I learned. I barely had to study because I ACTUALLY retained the info. Professor, if you're reading this, you're an inspiration & your students & daughters are so lucky to have a role model like you.

analysis.name: Michele Bigley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very nice and fun prof. Class is basically P/NP. If you meet the minimum requirements on assignments, you will get an A. Super easy class that felt connected and tight-knit. Attendance is mandatory. She also gives lots of feedback to help your writing.

Super sweet and funny prof, grade is based on completion of assignments, and as long as you put in a good amount of effort, you get full credit. If she doesn't think it's finished, you have lots of time to revise and get it turned back in. This class is what you make it

Had her for 3 quarter of CCE (CCE1-CCE3). She's very considerate when it comes to attendance and due dates. She gives a lot of feedback which may seem overwhelming, but it really helps you become a better writer. Definitely recommend her for anyone taking CCE and looking to better their writing! Also, easy class overall. Just do your work.

Super chill professor, easy class with light requirements. You choose what grade you want and complete whats asked of you. Just make sure you follow assignment requirements for the three projects exactly how she wants them. Allowed to miss up to a few classes but shes superrr flexible with people leaving early (I always left 20 mins early).
Very good teacher. Just give a least a little bit of effort and pay attention in class and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Saba Bazargan
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you're an auditory learner, you'll probably benefit a lot from going to lecture. If you're a visual learner, you might have a bit of trouble because his entire lecture is basically a 50 minute long speech on the readings with little to no visual texts or powerpoints.

Prof Saba is wonderful. You can tell how intelligent he is by the way he explains concepts. There were 5 tests total (in class essays), and that's all. None were cumulative. He grades tough but fair, and is willing to discuss it with you and even change it. He is very funny so I enjoyed his lectures, but the content will stretch you. Pay attention.

His class is hard, I'm an A student and barely got an A-. There's so much reading and none of it makes sense unless you go to lecture (he doesn't podcast). Can't miss even one unless you're messed up. He grades hard (5 essay exams are the only grade) and is looking for specific answers that feel like you're being drowned in abstract phil thoughts.

The way Professor Saba lectures is so clear and organized, it's genuinely amazing. Readings were hard sometimes, but he helps you see the structure and the concepts when he lectures. Gives great and detailed feedback on tests.

If you just want to get this GE out of the way, Bazargan is the way to go. He is very clear about what is expected. His 3 "essay" assignments really just ask you to summarize a specific part of the author's arguments and to give your opinion. No final, discussion attendance is mandatory, should be easy to get a B with minimal effort.

analysis.name: Brian Leigh
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 133 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Leigh starts every lecture with some chemistry memes pertaining to the material of the day and throws in hilarious quips and puns to keep the class interested. He's very knowledgeable and gives in-depth examples of lab calculations on the class website. Take his class!

Hilarious to listen to + cares for students; bit unclear what is wanted in reports at times; lectures not mandatory + flexible.

Midterm good; barely prepped us for the final so I had to memorize everything and still felt uneasy.

Do not take with other time-consuming classes. Despite going to TA helproom every day, I still got tons of points off.

Very nice and funny professor. 
He tries very hard to curve at the end. 
Lab reports are graded very detailed. Sigfigs can cost you many points. 
He posted videos about past midterms and the midterms questions are exactly like those in the video. 
Final exam pretty hard, full of lecture and detailed experimental questions. 
Go to office hours.

I should have been warned about this class a little more and my grade would have been way better. GO TO HIS LECTURES. The sig fig grading is so insane (double check graphs, data, calculations, and write ups). The final is evil but he does curve. Is very witty and wants everyone to succeed. This class requires a lot of effort so keep that in mind.

Chem 7L is a beast especially because prelabs and lab reports are so time consuming, but the labs themselves were very fun and Prof. Leigh made it so much better. He is super funny and really cares about his students. His lectures are very through on how to complete each experiment and even gives tips on how to not get dinged on the lab report!

analysis.name: Michael Burg
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 152 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Awesome professor, awesome guy! He really really (really) cares about his students and gives every opportunity to do well in his class. Lectures are a bit confusing, but if you go over your notes and review the lecture slides, he explains concepts very well. Tests are very fair and are an accurate representation of what was learned in class.

Dr. Burg is a great professor and down-to-earth guy and I would recommend taking him! This course has been my favorite class I've taken and has made me truly enjoy bio. He can be all over the place when teaching, but he breaks up the material very clearly and makes lecture fun! There are no podcasts and 3 exams, lots of USEFUL EC, and no curve.

Very enthusiastic about what he teaches. No textbook needed/ no podcasts, so you need to go to his lectures. Everything he writes on the board/ discusses will be on the test. He usually reviews the last lecture before to know the most important topics. Always smiling/wants people participating. Would love to take his class again!

Professor Burg has a great sense of humor and a passion for all things biology. You will learn how to design your own experiments and investigate different hypotheses. Note of caution: TA's can vary in quality. Make sure that you ask your TA for their SPECIFIC grading criteria, otherwise you may be disappointed with how your lab reports are graded.

I love his humor, and his voice is audible and catching. Also, he is so good at explaining and, especially, at simplifying; he is not afraid to use the colloquialism.  The first two chapters consist quite a few videos, and the tests have the most basic questions that check if you had watched. I learn that way, but I also heard complaints about that

analysis.name: Christine Harris
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Disrespectful towards students and has no passion for teaching. Almost seems like she's looking for ways to fail students. She has a history of saying she heard about a cheat circle and blasts the class to come forward to admit they have cheated. Her tests are written to confuse students and it seems apparent she is incredibly angry. AVOID HER.

This professor is probably the worst professor I've ever had. She genuinely got the entire class against her & called out students by name when asked about grading. She isn't willing to listen to students' concerns, but instead calls them something that doesn't meet the site guidelines. She claims we don't study and just complain. DON'T RECOMMEND.

I can care less about giving reviews on rate my professor. However, the amount of students giving false claims about the difficulty and professionality of the course is the epitome of groupthink. I currently have an A in the class just by skimming through the readings. There's a high chance everyone that left a bad review didn't even start.

She does a good job of covering it up most of the time, but she is unstable af. And not as smart as she thinks she is. Don't even think about doing your 199 or thesis with her. the stories about her treatment of students are crazy disturbing and her research is pretty boring. Not worth it. Be especially careful if you're an international student.

DONT take her class. She struggles to take valid criticism, oddly punitive to students who obv need help, and doesn't care bc she alrdy has tenure. She and TAs were very passive aggressive in announcements. First time I've ever disliked a prof. There's better classes to take by profs who rlly want to help students. not a groupthink issue, just her

analysis.name: Hsiao-Bing Cheng
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 93 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Unless your only goal is to become more proficient in your prayer life, do not take this class!!! If you see his name on webreg, waitlist another professor instead and if you already have him, just drop the class. He told us to drop since Day 1 and I wish I listened. Take literally any other professor, his class is incredibly unfair in comparison.

Self study class mostly no clear outline. No cheat sheets no study guides so it'll be more difficult. Tests are mostly based on homework but require a deeper understanding of the material to be applied to similar problems. Exam averages in 40s-50s while other profs are 80s. Not a big deal since there will be a big curve later on.

He constantly makes mistakes like forgetting minus signs, denominators, and forgets to add all relevant information needed to solve a problem. The hw was not as hard as the exams but takes 6+ hours a week. He assigned quizzes (2 hours each) on the same week as midterms. 0/10 Professor. He said 63% (F) was a very good score for our first midterm.

Very frustrating in every aspect. 10+ hours being spent on homework per week and I don't even get full credit most of the time. He does a very bad job preparing us for homework, quizzes, and tests. You HAVE to teach yourself everything. His lectures are a mess....just spare yourself from the headaches and take this course elsewhere.

He goes though lectures very quickly and expects you to absorb everything the minute he says something. He will do 1-2 examples on the topic but then the homework and test will have complex variations that you barely know how to do. I can see that he likes his job and knows the content, but he is not that good at explaining things well or in depth.

analysis.name: Caren Walker
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Walker is one of the best professors I've had. Her lectures are really good and her slides are helpful if you actually listen and take your own notes. Her exams are fair and based on lecture. I definitely recommend her, just know it's an upper division class so it will be reasonably challenging. (PS. best way to study is to watch record..

Professor Walker is great. Her class was easy. 2 midterms and a final that is cumulative. If you do better on a midterm section of the final, she replaces your midterm grade. She was extremely clear and only tested on things from her slides. People complaining are likely the problem themselves. I was taking 4 classes and hers was a breeze.

Her exams are way too difficult and content dense for the material she covers in lecture as it is directly lecture related yet she does not put enough information on her slides. Exams make up most of the grade with other assignments not making a dent in your grade. Avoid unless you want a GPA tank for a course that should be easy not this difficult

This was my favorite class this year...maybe ever. Professor Walker's lectures are super engaging and makes you feel like she is in conversation with you. She is really funny and open. The exams can be hard, but they are fair, and she gives credit back when too many students get a question incorrect. If you pay attention in class, you'll be fine!

One of my favorite professors so far at UCSD. Great lecturer who cares about keeping her students engaged and involved with the material. Super organized Canvas, manageable workload, exams are based off slides which are also well organized. Exams are usually curved a few points, SONA is extra credit. Podcasts lectures too. Highly recommended!

analysis.name: Geoffrey Cook
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely one of the best professors I have had so far. He knows his material well and is very passionate about his subject. He is nice and always helpful. Lectures are interesting and informative. The lab portion of the class has a lot of worksheet like excersises that can add up and take time, but are not a big deal. BEST CLASS!

TAKE THIS CLASS. Professor Cook is the best professor I have had at UCSD. He is so kind and genuinely cares about his students. He is actually passionate about what he teaches and who he is teaching it to. Take this class if you want to have a fun time, learn some pretty cool things about volcanoes, and leave with some friends.

YOU MUST TAKE THIS CLASS! This class was really chill and attendance is not required, lectures are not recorded but the slides are clear to review and learn. He really passionate in his own study field. Exams are all MCQs really easy less time consuming.

Genuinely the best professor ive ever had the joy of taken. Extremely passionate in his work, made every single lecture interesting and engaging, wonderful funny and kind guy, labs were kind of tedious with the work but was feasible every time. I miss this guy. Take him if possible.

I took his GS(global seminar) class when studying abroad this summer. He 100% meets the expectations that r written everywhere in any ratings students give him. He made Switzerland fun; I recommend it for students to go there! iI happy I'll still have close ties with him/his wife- they r AMAZING PPL!!

analysis.name: Nathaniel Chapman
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Chapman is amazing. His lectures are thoughtful, he is funny but also professional, and he starts every class by playing music (which is awesome). Keep up with his online textbook assignments. They will usually require you to access them more than once before the due date to complete them (which actually helps content stick). 10/10. Easy A.

Loved Dr Chapman. Lectures are fairly informative but the real value is in Dr Chapman's professional insight. He is clearly very experienced and has an answer for everything and is not afraid to dispel false information. Endless opportunities to engage with the lectures which I appreciated. Very easy class, most points are essentially free.
Dr. Chapman is very blunt and has a dry sense of humor, which I grew to really enjoy. I learned so much in his classes. He's SO intelligent and passionate about psych.

Dr. Chapman was my favorite professor throughout my tenure at UCSD. I took 3 courses with him and would have taken more if I could! He genuinely cares about the relevance, relatability, and understanding of his courses. You can tell he is passionate about what he does and excited about impacting the next generation of psychologists. Funny too!

Dr Chapman was my favorite professor during my time at UCSD, I took multiple classes with him and enjoyed learning under his guidance. Just make sure to stay organized and on top of deadlines, also class attendance is mandatory as he does class codes to input into attendance quizzes.

analysis.name: Paul Cao
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Definition of average teacher. Lectures feel random sometimes. Programming HW is painful, taking 6+ hours weekly, literally left me with sore fingers. Small accent and monotone speaker. Requires iClicker participation (~$25) Literally made me reconsider CS and life as a whole multiple times. Tests are fair but don't take with another hard class

Professor Cao gives very light lectures and then gives EXTREMELY difficult assignments. Prepare to spend the entire week dedicated to this class and no other class. You will spend most of your time with tutors if you take Paul Cao. If you are taking any other difficult course, expect to see your grades drop from the time commitment in this course.

Good prof who knows the content. PAs are most of your grade and can take a long time, but they do help you learn the data structures. 3 quizzes with redos, a midterm, and a final. Lots of previous tests to study with. Only scary part is needing above 55% for the coding portion of the final. If you study well, it is a breeze. Mandatory attendance

Definitely knows what he's doing. He lectures from a note outline, which he fills out during the lectures, which honestly isn't my cup of tea, but it's alright. Attendance is graded, but two weeks of attendance are dropped, so there's room for error. He provides past midterms, finals, and quizzes, which are really useful for study and practice.

Cao is a great teacher. His lectures were very easy to follow, and you can tell he cares about his students learning. Practice exams were very similar to real tests. The class teaches you a lot, and is very fair.

analysis.name: Raymond Chou
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 81 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great prof, I failed badly but don't regret taking him. He really pushes us to tackle combinatorics and encourages office hours (I don't recommend going in-person since students keep asking about research giving no time to ask about hw). Curved generously and is aware that his hw and tests are difficult, and is willing to give partial credit!

This man might actually be one of the greatest professors of all time. I will truly miss his enthusiasm and humor. He is the John Keating of the modern day. I have such high respect for this man. This course is otherwise dreadful, however, this guy somehow makes every topic conceptually and practically feasible to understand. Truly, an inspiration.

Professor Raymond is sincerely very passionate and engaging with the material. He cares about you understanding the material, and his lectures are very dynamic and interesting. Can't recommend him enough. He's the GOAT.

Lectures are very fun, enjoyable, and covers a lot of what would be on the exams. Had Discord, so super easy to ask anything inside and outside of class, and get help from the prof himself as well as TA's. Provided practice problems and held extra office hours before exams. Genuinely cares and helps students succeed. Best prof I've ever had. GOAT.

Ahhh... Professor Raymond Chou. How I adore you. If you have the opportunity... TAKE THIS GUY. He's legit hilarious, kind, and inspirational. He explains concepts so well although 20B is the hardest 20 series IMO and when he teaches I feel like I'm being taught by that cool cousin who's a few years older than me. Down to earth. awesome.

analysis.name: Celeste Pilegard
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 88 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Workload is intense every week. Participation for lectures and discussions matter a lot. The only reason why I'm writing this review is because she is deciding to have midterms the day after Halloween. Nobody can go out ON Halloween as Midterm is a 9am. How fun...

Her content is honestly so hard to undestand and her tests are difficult for no reason. Her midterm was so difficult to complete in 50 minutes I was struggling and now her final short answer questions make no sense either. Why are there so many questions in such a short period of time like bffr.

AMAZING PROFESSOR!! Graded by online labs (google form questions), self-explanations (questions about lecture and graded on completion), 2 midterms, and a final. And there's extra credit. An incredibly fair class, and learned so many interesting things. 100/10 would recommend this class.

Assignments are easy, just watch some vid lectures and you'll do fine. What is taught is interesting and is taught in an engaging manner. Only thing that made me get an A- rather than an A were the tests, which I feel were quite a bit of a step up from the video lectures and assignments (especially since there is quite a bit of info that is taught)

psyc 3r has one lecture a week, and she always does a good job at keeping everyones attention and teaching the content in an invigorating way. There are only a few assignments a week and they can be done pretty quick, but the online lectures are usually an hour long so taking notes takes a while. There are a bunch of extra credit opportunities

analysis.name: Dave Stegman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is such a kind teacher.. Although I know nothing about geography, I still get a high grade through hardworking. There are extra credit exercises. He is willing to solve problems for students, and cares about students' feelings. He rescued my GPA!  I'm sorry that I was a little afraid about his low RMP score before. Don't be effect by that!

pretty good for a GE. No exams but  6 pop quizzes throughout and a final project. The quizzes are pretty hard and based on his lectures (he does post slides and notes) but he drops one and the weekly activities and project check ins make up lots of your grade. The weekly stuff can be complicated but office hours can be helpful, with TA or prof.

No final exam but rather a final project, and he mentions how there are 6 quizzes scattered throughout the quarter. He's quite straightforward with his expectations, so please, please, please don't use AI and try to listen. That's all he really wants from his students.

Genuinely such a sweet professor. He cares about his students grades and wants you to pass. I thought taking a geology class would be boring but he made it a very interesting topic. Attend his classes please. The more you attend the more you understand the material.

Was a very interesting class that was taken an as GE. If you attended lectures, or at least look at the slides every day, the class should be very easy. He was funny and a very nice professor that truly cares about teaching his students.

analysis.name: Denise Rava
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 111 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, not amazing, but okay. A lot of students struggled probably because it's their second quarter, and this class was harder than what most expected. I felt that the lectures, homework, and past exams provided was enough to do good in the class. Slight curve of A -> A+. Should have a decent math background to succeed

Stats itself is not hard to understand, but the way she teaches it is insanely confusing. Labs and homework are so time consuming and no proper feedback on why answers are wrong. None of our assignments are dropped and no late work is accepted. Absolutely no accommodations for students during the pandemic. Has no empathy for her students.

If your class average for both midterms is close to 48%, its time to stop being a professor and find a new job. Majority of the other math department staff average around 60-70% btw. Read the other reviews posted about her and just know that for an intro level class, there were people outside the lecture hall praying on their knees before the final

For such a simple introductory subject, she makes content harder in everything we do outside of lecture. No easy to access reviews that reflect content, no notes posted after lecture, heavy amounts of coding that would be difficult for people with no experience in R. This professor is vague and questions during exams are tricky. Not recommended.

The mean score of one of the midterms was 63%. If that doesn't say enough, I don't know what else will. The examples she provides in class are also so simplified in comparison to the homework and test questions. She is also insanely strict with her tests, as thinks everyone is trying to cheat.

analysis.name: Olga Dudko
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She's nice, funny, and explains things very well. However, I never took physics before, so this class was hard. Because of that, I dropped it. One needs to put in the effort to do the ungraded homework problems in order to do well on her quizzes. I would've like to have her in other physics classes. I-clicker questions are good checkpoints and EC.

Amazing professor. I enjoyed coming to lecture every single time. She has a deep understanding of physics, along with much enthusiasm. She is also very funny as well. Makes physics understandable, clear, and interesting. Do your HW, go to lecture, and the quizzes will be fair. The final is based off of quiz questions and clicker questions.

Passionate lecturer but gives out tough quizzes. Homework did not reflect some questions on the quiz especially with simple questions. Skip the simple questions and go straight for the medium and challenging questions and review lecture notes. I had to predict which question type would appear on the quiz. Overall, tough class but doable.

Professor Dudko's class is really great! She goes through examples and explains everything pretty well. She has a sense of humor, but it's best not to mess with her. Do well on the quizzes and the final should be no issue. Extra credit is offered through clicker questions. Grading scale is fair.

If you've either never taken or seen little of classical mechanics, Professor  Dudko's class is for you. She knows how to effectively explain concepts and is very open to questions from students. Reading the textbook and doing practice problems are very helpful. If you study the concepts and algorithms from the quizzes, the final should be fine.

analysis.name: Douglas Smith
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 202 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I took him for physics IB and he is great. He curves to a B+ which is rare at UCSD and he tests only from his slides. However he does not know how to drive nor can he park but he does have a nice BMW :)

Dougie is such an awesome guy! He is very monotoned but has a sense of humor if you get to know him. The guy is also a genius! Class is difficult and he doesnt lecture well, but is slides are super helpful and he quizzes from his slides. Also curves the class to a B+, so as long as you do better than the average youll get an A. Final is brutal tho

I don't know why Smith has such a low score. I took the risk of taking his class over Paddock, and he's a great professor in my book! I get how he can sound monotone in some lecture, but really funny in most of them. He makes physics concepts simple. Quizzes are representative of his slides and are quite easy if you review just those slides alone.

Prof smith is such a dad character!! Hes a genuinely kind professor and has pretty dry humor that makes lectures entertaining at times. he does his best to make a rather dull subject relatable and I always appreciated that he connected the material to real life applications. Very generous curve, quizzes easier than hw that are directly from slides!

i used to hate physics before this professor. he should have a higher rating. he doesn't try and trick students by giving overly complicated problems. his exam questions are super similar to the homework and practice problems. lectures are great too. definitely try taking him if you can. i loved this professor.

analysis.name: Ricardo Dominguez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 60 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: My only complaint about this class is that I had the joy of experiencing it for only one brief quarter. The assignments will push you out of your comfort zone (in a good way!) - be prepared to do performances live and participate in short critiques every class session.  Ricardo is a wonderful professor and this class is a hidden gem in VisArts!

Brilliant, but violent and out-of-control. Has a bizarre obsession with bathrooms, verbally abuses (mostly women) for interuppting his amazing masculine lecture to go to the bathroom. Also has the most childish temper tantrums about phones (instead of asking people to turn them off) and undermines the TAs (they undermine him back, hilariously).

We had one crazy quarter with all the media buzzing around this course. We all banded together and had a beautiful, wonderful time. This class is such a confidence builder, and Ricardo is an amazing professor who made this space a safe and comfortable one to bare one's soul.

Professor Ricardo is so caring and supportive professor that I can easily ask any questions. He really encourages students to expand their hidden creative and artistic energy in any form. In this class, you can build and explore your own virtual spaces freely without any restrictions. This class is amazing. I strongly recommend this class.

He's a great professor. Real genuine,very knowledgable, and tells great stories. I've had 3 classes with him and they NEVER got boring.  The risks you have to take in his class are well worth it in my opinion. Because of that man, I've gained a lot of self confidence and I am very honored to have had him as a professor.

analysis.name: Daisuke Miyao
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is the best. Took him for 2 Japanese Film classes and enjoyed every single second! Cares about his student so much, can't find a better professor to talk about Japanese Film to! Waitlist is long but that can't be a reason to give him bad rating. Be reasonable, he deserves 5 stars.

Professor Miyao is one of the kindest and most caring professors at UCSD. You can tell that he enjoys teaching and is not just at UCSD for research. His lectures are always interesting and he engages his students by asking for responses. His class required two essays. The first is 600 words and the second is 1000 words. Definitely take him!
If you couldn't get an A in this class, what else can you do? He is sooooo nice. I mean soooooo nice. BEST professor I have ever seen.

I really enjoyed being in his class! The discussions we had on Japanese films will be something I will always look back on. Professor Miyao creates a safe space for everyone to voice their own opinions and allows people to have presentations on the films they want to talk about in more depth. I highly recommend this professor!

If you don't believe the good reviews and trust the bad reviews, I highly recommend you just look up his classes on CAPE, stats say it all! You will never regret taking his course and don't drop out before week 2 so that whoever gave him bad reviews trying to get into his class will never succeed.

analysis.name: Gordon Dahl
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Awful . Heavy homework for having stata questions. Using stata software is required without giving instruction, have to figure it out by yourself. Based on research in class the average hours for finishing the homework is about 5 hours. Super abstract test that is not even close to the sample exam or homework. worst econ class experience ever.

honestly i don't understand why there are a lot of comments about how good he is. At least based on the experience of me and my classmate it is obvious that he has the lecture that is just "OK", with material presented but somehow dry. Super difficult midterm which is not related to any of his homework or sample exams. Avoid him if you can

He seems like a nice professor until i went to his OH. i went to the OH, no one was there. after i asked him the questions that i came in with, i was going through my notebook to find other things that i needed him to clearify. but he told me to "go home and make a list so i wouldnt be wasting his time." rude.

Very dry lecturer. Props if you can actually stay awake in his class. He is engaging and works hard to teach and make sure you understand. His tests however are incredibly hard and have nothing to do with anything useful or the stuff he taught. They focus more on the proofs then the actual doing of stats, which is useless unless your a stat major

If you want to learn a bunch of material very well, and not even be tested on it, and instead, get tested on things you've never seen before or have barely heard him say for about 90% of the exam, go for it buddy. I'd rather take a prof that actually tests you on important material and not 3 questions of wtf that account for 40% of your grade.

analysis.name: Debashis Sahoo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Low-effort teaching." or "Not very engaged as an instructor.. Makes his class artificially hard by using the minimum grading schema. Doesn't even give a full 3 hour final window like every other professor in the school, so good luck trying to finish the final on time. This guy also just copies Niema's material (take it with Niema if you can).

Most atrocious grading system ever. He does not care about students and expects everyone to live perfectly managed lives without ever missing one of his irrelevant, extremely frequent hw quizzes. Miss 3 hw quizzes because life happens sometimes, and you're capped to a B. He gives 0 exceptions no matter the situation. Most inconsiderate professor.

Incredibly harsh grading scheme which takes the minimum of your reading quiz average, exam average and programming assignments average and makes that your final grade. That too, there are no drops. So if you mess up on one thing, you're cooked for the class. Also assigned a very long, tedious project the week before finals.

Grading is rigid, with full exam score, missing 2/26 quizzes gives an A-, 3 gives a B. Teaching quality is very poor. Course relies on YouTube videos. He never replies my email. This course should be redesigned. The grade doesn't reflect real learning. He uses rigid policies to lower grades because the exams are too easy.

Incredibly harsh grading scheme which takes the minimum of your reading quiz average, exam average and programming assignments average and makes that your final grade. That too, there are no drops. So if you mess up on one thing, you're cooked for the class. Also assigned a long, tedious project the week before finals.

analysis.name: Elsa Cleland
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved this class and her lectures, she is super passionate and loves answering questions. Lecture is mandatory with lecture assignments every day, and discussion is also mandatory, but both of these give helpful material to help study for exams. 3 midterms a final but you can drop 1 exam. if you like ecology this class is very interesting

Amazing professor who cares about her students. Her lectures are easy to follow and organized. The exams are very similar to in-class practice questions and what you are expected to know is clearly stated. Spend time studying, I used flashcards due to exams being memory-based, and an A is possible.

I'd recommend this professor! Her lectures were very interesting, and she explained the material well and was always welcoming to questions. Attendance is required. Exams were a fair representation of lectures.

Content is extremely boring and hard to grasp when you have no interest in soils and plants.  Tests were very difficult averaging 60s and the final average was a 50 and they still would not curve the class.  Ended with a 84.97 and they would not round it up to an 85 to receive a B+.  Professors are not looking for students best interest

Fun class! Weekly field trips to places like SIO pier and Elliott Chaparral Reserve. Lots of writing, with about a 5 page paper due weekly, but they really do help your writing for other classes. For EBE majors, this is one of the best classes you can take!

analysis.name: Eric Morgan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's amazing! I've never done coding before and his class was the best intro class I could've taken. There are weekly coding assignments graded on effort + 5 overall assignments, all are easy. He also gives two midterms (2 parts each, all of which can be done at home) and a take home final exam or project, also very easy. Take this class!!

The lectures are easy to follow and engaging. Most Labs and homeworks are guided, so nothing too hard, and online resources are allowed. Midterms and final is take-home and very easy. Easy A with minimal effort. Overall, very beginner-friendly.

He was nice and funny, but sometimes during lectures, he went out of order and I got confused at some points. The midterms are on paper and the first one caught me off guard because his practice tests weren't like the midterm. Final was a take-home project or final, so that's light. Attendance was extra credit. Don't need any coding experiece

His class was a breath of fresh air from my regular pre law major courses. He really wasn't kidding when he claims he can teach python to anyone, he is super beginner friendly. The class already provides pre written notes which you can edit and follow through in class without worrying about writing both notes and coding examples!

I was kinda scared of this class at first but honestly the professor is really passionate and sweet and the material is very accessible outside of class. It's beginner-friendly but it does get increasingly more difficult. I took it for a major requirement but I think it could work decently for a GE, depends on your preferences.

analysis.name: Yen Espiritu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Espiritu is an exceptional professor. She is so passionate and bubbly and really makes you leave the lecture feeling enlightened. This class is really easy and if you attend lecture you are guaranteed an A. Professor Espiritu is easily my favorite professor at UCSD and I want to take every class she offers !

A lot of reading which is kind of insane for a remote and DEI class but pretty much just skimmed through the text and passed. Participate in discussions as chunk of your grade comes from it. Only 3 assignments that were pretty straightforward. Did learn about history often not covered in education curriculum tho.
Pretty easy class, and you'll definitely get something out of it.

Professor Yen is great! She is knowledgeable in her field and makes many valid points in framing our culture. However, if you are not generally interested in the field of ethnic studies/interdisciplinary work, you should not take this class. Many professors in this field require an open mind and interest, not an easy A course.
This class is amazing! Those that are saying otherwise have grown up in close-minded environments and have not been exposed to opinions from those in the peripheries and margins of society.

analysis.name: Emily Windham
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is a great prof!!! I would take her again 100%. She gives great feedback. There are 2 essay and one project. Her class is super fun and I loved how she put us into groups. She is always willing to help with anything!! She is not a tough grader and is there to better your writing. If you want to get a good grade participation is necessary!!!
Professor Windham is so great!!! Very approachable and knows how to organize/structure her class. I wish I could take her for the second portion of WCWP.
Super nice professor that cares about how you feels. Just don't forget to communicate with her on time so that your grade standing is good.

Very sweet, genuine, honest professor. Grading pledge was clear and easy. Cares about her students and genuinely wants you to work on becoming a better writer. Every week 3-5 reading assignments with annotations based on your grading pledge. 2-4 hours of work max per week. I enjoyed going to her office hours just to chit chat just cuz she so cool.

The grading system was contract based so you choose a grade you would like and that determines your workload and how many readings and absences you can have as well. She is a very caring teacher that gives feedback on your writing. You use Persuall so most readings are free, I only needed to buy one for ~30 $. A lot of reading in general.

analysis.name: Eric Steiner
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Awesome professor, lectures are straight from the textbook, but you don't even need to read it. He does assignments in class which helps you connect material and takes a load off having to worry about homework! He makes it really easy to learn and you can tell he cares about his students. Also lowkey hot.

I know my grade might not reflect my rating very well but I enjoyed this professor a lot. I made a doc of questions I had for him and he responded the next day. Everything that's on the exams in on the lecture slides so ONLY pay attention to what's on the slides. Great professor and really wants you to succeed and pass his class.

Pure & insane amounts of memorizing, exams are SUPER specific & its difficult to memorize everything he asks us to. Exams every 2 weeks, with 200+ terms to memorize for each exam. It was incredibly specific exams & he does not grade very generously. Super animal heavy, it felt like a zoology course with all the random animal facts I had to memorize

This class is going to be difficult. The topics are hard to understand and deep explanations will not be given. Grade is almost entirely exam reliant, with three exams and one final exam given and spread out along course. Lectures are also often non-engaging and hard to follow.

rlly nice professor. just go to class and study enough for them midterms. for the research project, he basically holds your hand throughout the entire thing. also basically holds your hand during the labs. rlly easy just put in the work to study bc they're a huge chunk of ur grade. labs are worth 3 points each. have to go to lecture

analysis.name: Emma Geller
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very organized and weekly quizzes help you stay on top of material. Quizzes are easy if you read weekly research articles. Final was not too hard thanks to the weekly quizzes and peer instruction(clicker)questions. Need to attend class. APA paper was annoying but doable and useful for psych majors. Content isnt bad but some topics are harder

Okay, I just gotta be honest here as a student currently taking this course (and not having a bad score), currently an A, but this come at the cost of constant studying. You could cram everything in for the last two days before the exams, but just let me tell you that it's a lot of lectures and notes to cover. It's doable (I did it), just a lot.

There are weekly quizzes which forces you to keep up with the material. She is just GREAT when it comes to questions and clarifications about the material. E-mail her or post on discussion board and she's been willing to explain again. The final was super hard compared to anything else but if you do well throughout the class, you'll be fine.

You can tell she really cares about her students' success! She takes “a flipped classroom” approach, so you watch the lectures before class and do group work during class time to test your knowledge. I learned a lot from this approach, but keep in mind there's lots of material to learn so additional study time is likely needed.

Prof Geller was trying a new layout for this course with a flipped classroom with three lectures due on Sundays and weekly group assignments & quizzes. Honestly didn't love this layout. It was meant to promote collaboration/discussion, but most of the time groups would divide and do work in silence. It seemed like the grading scale changed a lot.

analysis.name: Emmanuel Theodorakis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 97 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's a caring professor but his exams are super hard. The things he teaches in lecture are nothing like his exams. He really expects you to know your stuff just to pass the class. He doesn't use the whole class time for the midterms and for the final only gives 2 hours. I don't recommend taking this professor!!!

Dr. T is a brilliant man. His knowledge of his field and 140B in particular is beyond measure. His truly understands the material on a level that can answer any question students throw at him. The spacing between midterms was weird (one was week 3, the other week 9!) but was doable. Final was super difficult but he gave us freebies towards the end.

Theodorakis is such a great professor! He really cares about his students and their success in his class. Is readily available to help outside of class and does a great job presenting material in a way that is easily understood by students. He is in no way arrogant or intimidating like other chem staff here.

He makes ochem very understandable. Clear and funny lectures,but board problems he did were very general. I wished that he would do more examples on the board, but knowing the general cases is very important too. Otherwise, his tests are similar to his practice exams. Midterm 1 was NMR. Midterm 2 was reactions and 1 mechanism. Final- mechanisms!

Truly horrible professor, his tests are nothing like what he teaches at lectures. I have a good understanding of topics, homework questions but still struggle to understand how he manages to create the hardest exams. His practice tests are also nothing like the actual tests. I don't know how he sleeps at night but he made my life a living hell.

analysis.name: Kristine Ehrich
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Kristine is the best teacher. She explained marketing in a clear and an easy way. Her class is well organized, and the projects are fun and helpful. If you follow her lectures and do the work, it is easy to get a good grade. She really cares about her students and makes the class interesting. I highly recommend her !

She's teaches what you need to learn in the class, mostly from lecture, not from the book. Her grading criteria is clear and I enjoyed her classes. Go to class and participate. It helps you stay engaged. Would definitely take 103 from her.

I loved Professor Ehrich. Lectures were very informative and she is super sweet. The tests are lecture heavy and she will put things said in her lectures in her exams. She warns you about it though at the beginning of the quarter. She gives you everything you need to prepare for the midterm and final in her class. Attendance is mandatory.

People who complain about her have never actually taken a difficult class in their lives. She's an engaged lecturer, all of her guidelines and expectations are very clear from what she says and what's in the syllabus, no false advertising. If you take decent notes during lectures and study for literally an hour before the quizzes you'll be fine.

She makes classes engaging. However, the tests are VERY lecture heavy. She will quote herself from past lectures and will quiz you on that. If you know you won't be attending every class, do not take this professor. She doesn't provide a study guide or assignments to prep for the tests, apart from an in class-review session a class prior.

analysis.name: Jose Fuste
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is amazing. His essay and final exams are not really tough and easy for A+. Although the reading assignments are pretty annoying. You can definitely be absent-minded on his lecture cuz they are not helpful for exams.

AMAZING PROF! He really cares for the students. There was no midterm and 2 "finals" which were really easy (easy A). Attendance is mandatory, but u could easily just write your name in the attendance sheet and leave class. There is a lot of reading, but all readings are interesting and are in Perrusall.

Assigns a lot of reading, and has weekly reflection papers based on the readings but the material is interesting and they help for midterm and final paper. He's a great lecturer, passionate inspirational and funny! Also likes to having discussions which keep lectures interactive. One of my fave profs! Oh and readings are on Ted, no textbook!!

Professor Fusté is amazing, he cares so much about his students and tries to be as accessible as possible to ensure that every student feels prepared in class. The readings he assigns are interesting and his lecturers are great for anyone with ADHD/ADD because he speaks at a pace that is easy to follow. I love his classes!

REALLY HARD, not because the topics covered but because he assigns TOO MUCH work. A lot of readings and papers to write... He is a nice guy but I think he believes that we only have one subject: his. Not enough time to do everything.

analysis.name: Frances Hammock
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 186 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Save yourself. Probably one of the worst teachers I've ever had. And I went to freaking public school. Whenever you make an error on the hw and attempt to email her about a regrade, she basically tells you "that's not my problem". She speeds through her lectures like there's no tomorrow. If you're not there for lectures, good luck on catching up.

The homework assignments are fantastic for studying, and the lectures are clear and concise. The course has MATLAB homework, which is busy work. The class has 2 midterms (the lowest midterm gets dropped) and a final. Yet, Professor Hammock sometimes assumes a condescending attitude, making the learning experience uncomfortable.

Class was a lot of work, most of the learning came from the textbook and important major concepts like Chain Rule were not explained in class. First midterm was easy bc it was copy paste practiceMidtermButSecondOneWas curvedSignificantlyAndWasWay differ(shows howPoorlyTheClassMaterialWasTaughtAndHowHarshly itWasGraded). 30 long hwProblemsPerWeek.

Hammock's amazing, people only complain because they are deflecting their struggle onto her.
