What makes her great is how she gets straight to the point no b.s. she states what is relevant and what isn't. She is relatable and fun. Only complain I see justified would be the homework as they can take a lot of hours to finish, otherwise she's amazing.

Lectures are more base on her solving problems while students asking questions, she goes fast and skip steps assuming you know that step so might be confusing, Exams are harder than HW, HW is super long way to many questions. Gets difficult if not putting in the effort. She is very nice and willing to help. Go to her Office Hours it helps a lot.

analysis.name: Melissa Famulari
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 146 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If you want to have a painful experience in UCSD, take this class

Econ 100A is a tough class (no matter which profs you're gonna take). So, if you can't do well in this course, don't blame Dr. Famulari. She is a great professor who can always explain the materials clearly to students. All the fancy videos she posted online really helped me understand the concepts. Just working hard, go to DI, you can get an A.
crazy class and hard. you read you did
Avoid at all costs. She is very disorganized and honestly not helpful at all. Her tests are not representative of the material taught in class.

She is not helpful at all, although she tends to have TAs work a lot.  She looks nice but not kind from heart.  You should try to avoid this professor as much as you could. TAs or econ tutors seem much more helpful.

analysis.name: Jason Fleischer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Trips over his own lectures in class. He doesn't understand the material he is teaching which is affirmed by his " I don't know Math" comments. Asks the class to explain his own lecture slides to us because he can't even understand his own slides. Super frustrating. Take any other prof or ML sequence if you can.

Terrible professor. Nothing he says connects to anything on his lectures. Says he will do things (change grades, edit slides, etc) but never does it. No communication with TAs and IAs so piazza questions never get answered. Late to get grades back so we cannot use anything to study. GIVES NO STUDY MATERIAL in regards to midterms. Overall god awful

This all builds up to a group project. You spend a lot of time analyzing data so that you can answer a research question in a group, there are periodic check-ins. If you're okay with that, then it should go smoothly. Attendance is mandatory. Otherwise it's just pretty boring programming assignments you can do on autopilot.

His lectures are great, and he's clearly really knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches. It's just that the assignments, each worth 6% of your grade where you lose 50% of your score for tiny errors, have the most confusing, vague, and contradictory) instructions. I get that he expects precision, but I think he should lead by example.

Very simple class if you have an alright understanding of coding. Never went to a lecture, more than plenty of extra credit, Very straightforward work and easy final project. TAs and prof are very slow to respond to any posts and grading is very inconsistent. Ended with well over 100+

analysis.name: Jana Fortier
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She's so knowledgable and a super interesting teacher. There is a lot of reading but if you don't read all of it, she goes over highlights in class anyway. Our grade was based off a midterm, final and some class activities which were pretty fun to do. I definitely recommend her. She cares for all her students and wants everyone to do well.

Very caring and knowledgable. Class was very chill and felt more like a seminar. Overall course structure was very low pressure with no tests. Midterm and final was just completing a UNESCO course to earn a certification, and this can be done on your own time as early as week 1.

While the lectures were pretty interesting, they also pack in a lot of info. Be prepared for some reading. It's great that we get to pick our own final paper topic and give a presentation before its due at the end the term. And the best part is Prof F! She is truly kind, caring, and listens to all our different points of view...really learned a lot

She was very sweet and caring.Always made sure to let us know that she'd be available to get help,answer questions,or anything else we may need. Lectures could get a bit dragged out but it's because she's clearly so passionate and knowledgeable about many topics. Weekly reflections, few worksheets,midterm, and final research paper of our choosing

A good professor, unless you do your project area in something she's knowledgeable about. Many people were nitpicked much more during the project planning process than others. Interesting lectures and manageable content, though. The attendance policy is pretty stringent, but you have opportunities to make it up.

analysis.name: Magnus Felke
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Mr. Magnus is a very good lecturer, and I enjoyed his presentations. He is also very responsive over email, which I appreciate. However, he is an extremely tough grader, and not all assignments include a rubric. Even when one is provided, following it does not guarantee a good grade, making the process feel unclear and unfair.

Works in the industry so he genuinely cares and knows the industry in and out. His lectures were fun and engaging. There are quizzes, reflections, midterm, project, and final which may sound like a lot, but they are spaced evenly and are fairly easy to do. He explains things in a manner that makes it easy to understand.

Professor Felke is awesome! Has vast experience (currently works at BD and has also worked at Kodak/Qualcomm) which he uses to connect to topics we learn during lectures. There is a lot of reading but it's interesting. Quizzes/exams were a bit tough but form a good study group and actively participate in class. Wish he taught more classes at Rady!
Good lecturer, but a very tough grader. Despite enjoying the material, I wouldn't take his course again.

Professor Felke is an absolute delight. Great professor who makes the course fly by. It's an easy class objectively, so come with the intent to take as much as you can out of it without stressing too much about whether you'll pass or not.

analysis.name: Francesco Paesani
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class is sorta difficult even if you have prior knowledge from AP Chem. His lectures are boring and his accent makes it harder to understand. He uploads slides but half the material on the slides is gatekept because he wants to make the lecture "more engaging". Homework can be frustrating sometimes. Generous grading scale. Overall, not bad.

i used to love chem. not anymore after taking his class. took 2 years of chem in hs just for bro to ruin the experience. lectures are EXTREMELY boring and majority of it isn't even based off of AP CHEM. keep in mind, a 5 in AP CHEM clears the CHEM6 series yet half of the stuff taught in his class is not in ap chem. grading scale isn't bad tho.

Dr. Paesani is one of those professors that you should try to take before you graduate. While his entire lecture is on the chalkboard, he does it so that he can explain things clearly. He encourages learning, and wants students to think and succeed. He is also very nice and helpful in office hours, and anyone who has gone would tell you to go.

Peasani is an easy professor,  his tests are all super easy(easier then CHEM 4) and are all multiple choice. The only problem are the lectures, it is easier to understand him when watching podcasts rather than going to his class. Gives a lot of extensions and is super understanding, even let some guy use his phone as a calculator during a test.

Professor Paesani is a really good teacher. I'm still in the process of taking his class but I genuinely enjoy it. I recommend watching his lectures outside of class to help with understanding so you can pause and rewind to take notes as many times as needed. He goes a little faster during lecture. He's just sweet and has a cute italian accent.

analysis.name: Yi Fu
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: A lot of times it feels like she doesn't know what she's doing and is just as confused as the students are and doesn't really explain concepts and how to do things well. It's like watching her do homework problems with little and unclear explanations to why she does something because she tends to skip steps a lot. No practice tests or cheat sheets.

She's an alright lecturer, she sometimes seems just as confused as the students. She goes through unnecessary things really slowly and then speeds through the more important stuff. Other than that, class is just doing practice problems, very boring but not bad for learning. First midterm was incredibly difficult, but second was easy.

At the beginning, she used many helpful examples, but over time lectures became very theory heavy with few explanations of underlying concepts or examples. Questions were often deferred to after class and unanswered. Exams were easier than homework but very test heavy. No Homework was dropped, grading was late, and inconsistent exam grading.

Decent and friendly professor. Was unsure often when asked questions. Often made mistakes in lecture, leading to many revisions in posted slides. Much easier exams than homework, but late grading. Would recommend looking into other sources rather than just her lecture

Makes frequent mistakes in lectures, gave extra credit to students who corrected her. Skipped some steps in examples and went over unnecessary proofs sometimes.However, midterms related to her review slides. Midterm 1 avg was 62, but midterm 2 avg was 85, final avg 85. Lower midterm gets dropped. Lacks confidence teaching but very sweet and caring!

analysis.name: Fernando  Dominguez Rubio
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES. If you're looking for a well-rounded, discussion-stimulating class, this is not it. He argues with students who don't agree with his viewpoints, or even just try to present an alternative argument. He does not give clear instruction on assignments and makes students feel dumb for asking questions.

He is rude to students and made my classmates and I feel stupid for answering his questions in classs. He does not give clear direction, and in most cases does not give any direction, on assignments. All he does in lecture is show maps and bar graphs, which are not helpful. Would not recommend him to anyone under any circumstance. DO NOT TAKE.

Took this class during the fall of 2020. All you had to do was make two group projects, but the kicker is this class had no clear cut grading criteria. I literally went the entire 10 weeks not knowing what my final grade was going to be. Is it based on participation, how good the proposal is? You would never know. Avoid this class or P/NP it.

Just took his Comm 10 last quarter. Short conclusion? Do not take his course. Throughout the quarter there are two projects, you will be forced to work with other 9 students to get the project done. He will grade you only base on the grade of projects instead of your effort. Also you will have no clue what ur grades will be all time, NO CLUE

You could have blessings all the way from Jesus Christ himself to Anu the Mesopotamian god of the heavens, and you'd still get a C. World class neurobiologists can't explain the synapse patterns in his mind. Agitated by lack of participation, telepathic connection is expected. Failure to do so results in fighting with students in 200 person lecture

analysis.name: William Griswold
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: By far the worst professor I've ever had. Professor is a certified embarrassment. Spends every lecture talking about what we already read the night before. Wastes significant amounts of time on simple concepts, gives no help on difficult ones. Frustrating quizzes. Almost everything in the class taught is useless besides the project.
This guy's only work experience is AppFolio and it's the only thing he talks about.

pros: teaches stuff that is legitimately relevant to industry and project dev. cons: extremely unstructured, complicated, hyper convoluted material during lecture, in class quizzes+finals are graded mercilessly on an obscure grading rubric, no solutions to past quizzes/exams provided. You get a good grade if you can manifest his subjective criteria

Really didn't think I would enjoy this class due to the previous reviews. But his rendition of CSE 110 is the best at UCSD. Found his class to be directly relevant to my internship at FAANG last summer. The group project for me was kinda tragic (half of them did nothing), but it is only worth 30% of your grade, and lots can be done to mitigate it.

This is the first time I felt compelled to write a review. Many areas of this course need desperate and drastic changes. The multiple-choice reading quizzes are just a disaster. How are there 11 options and 7 of them are correct and students are expected to do them? The final grades are wrong on the first submission, just fitting.

analysis.name: Geoffrey West
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
Child-like and hard to talk to. He threatened to take back extra credit assignment because someone completed it too fast. 
lectures are bullet points/quotations from book, and then he blabs from there or invites students to speak (he loves to challenge/ argue with the answers he receives). 
final: 2 essays and vocab definitions.

Prof. West's lectures aren't mandatory or podcasted but he covers the key themes/historical context of the readings. Discussion heavily impacts your grade. Essays are graded by your TA, and mine was VERY strict about participation, which I found frustrating since not everyone expresses their ideas by speaking up in section but they don't care.

Lectures and the books we read were interesting. 
DO NOT BE FOOLED FIRST ESSAY WHEN THEY TELL YOU RUBRIC IS "OPTIONAL."
FOLLOW THE RUBRIC. FOLLOW THE RUBRIC. FOLLOW THE RUBRIC.
I had a bad TA that didn't teach essay structure, but as long as you follow canvas modules for writing you'll be fine. You've been warned. Other than that, great class.

Honestly a hilarious and knowledgeable guy, I just had a slightly sour experience because of the TA I got. Spent a full week crafting an essay and was given a 78 with rhetorical questions as comments. The TA felt very nitpicky and it is a TA that is often for this class. Other than that though lecture was fun, readings were manageable.

First, I would like to say that nobody in my class got an A+. My TA graded the first two 5-page papers almost sadistically, and you get tired of the teacher' s/TA's personality quickly. It's hard, but you can get through it. Also, discussions were pointless, yet mandatory, unless you wanted your 15% participation grade lowered.

analysis.name: Fred Rose
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 177 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Does not post his lecture recordings and his slides are insufficient. I attended every lecture and still barely passed because he does not highlight points of focus, or provide any study guide. His advice: "Read the book". The syllabus definitely reflects his character. Good luck

Class was interesting. Book, lecture, and weekly quizzes were all cohesive. We had to read around 300 pages throughout the quarter, and received no specification on what we'd be tested on. Tests were challenging because of this, but questions were straightforward. Very test heavy, so if you can't memorize 300 pages + lecture info DON'T TAKE!!

I'm so disappointed in this class. I was extremely hopeful at the beginning of this course because I really enjoy the content of it and the high reviews for Prof. Rose; however, the amount of reading and not recording lectures was brutal. He doesn't seem to care about his class's sub 70 averages for BOTH midterms and the FINAL. Disappointed.

I studies for this class every single day no exaggeration. I read the entire textbook and took notes on every chapter that we covered. Yet, I still received a failing grade. I have never put so much effort into a class to get so little in return.

I love Professor Fred He's really awesome. His tests are a reflection of everything we learn and he gives us exam practice that actually helps. Also he gives alot of extra credit!! (it helps alot!)

Anyways If youre reading this Prof Fred You da best and keep teaching please and stay at ucsd cause I want to take your other classes.

analysis.name: Gurleen Bal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Does a lot of demos and explains concepts well but goes too slow in lectures. Instead of catching up next lecture or just going faster, she always posts extra videos. Really annoying bc you have to watch 3 other vids (and go to all lectures) to complete the hw. There are clickers and quizzes are pretty simple (cheat sheet, ~9MCQ/~1FRQ).

Imo, gives way too much homework and even assigns us lecture videos outside of class when she's not able to finish in time or it's a school holiday. In lectures, she really feels like a highschool teacher with the way she keeps on telling the class to be quiet. She also does a lot of mistakes like due dates/typos. Needed the class but disliked it.

attendance not mandatory but if you show up and use a clicker you can get extra credit for attendance. Quizzes every other monday in person each worth about 10%. Hard class and material. Homework due every sunday. No midterm.

Lectures are alright, jumps to quickly into practice problems sometimes before covering the conceptual stuff (shows in the 56% avg final and 60% for quizzes),tbh Its phys2A though so be prepared to put in 10-15 hours outside of class regardless of prof but avoid her if you can, could've been a little more forgiving with exam or class curve.

Terrible final, 56% avg. I've taken PHYS2A before & Prof. Bal is enthusiastic, but exams suck. I had a B+ quiz average & class grade before the final, a C+ after ??  Engaging lectures w/very helpful conceptual demos and so many opportunities to get more help in OH. This is an extremely difficult class, expect to take 10-15+ hrs/week outside class!!

analysis.name: Mark Guirguis
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It's a straightforward GE class, lecture attendance is not mandatory but discussions are. Be prepared to spend upwards of $200 on stuff for the collage assignments and final projects. Shout-out to the professor and the TAs, they are good people. Probably the best GE I took at UCSD

Professor Guirguis is a very awesome Professor. I really enjoyed his class. He taught me how to precisely use an architect ruler, how to build a mini theater box etc. He has a very chill friendly personality. Someone complained they had to spend $200 for art supplies. I only spent $10 on all my art supplies and still got an A. Take care Mark ~JL

Lectures weren't mandatory attendance until it was one of the 3 quizzes that day. Discussions were mandatory and  final presentations at the end (it wasn't like a presentation just talk about what you made!) But with grading I wouldn't receive till later but just follow the rubric given. I did spend atleast $20+ because of the project/class

Be prepared to spend money. I've lost track but I've spent somewhere in the $75-$100 ballpark. I'm lucky enough to have an income, but idk how other people managed to afford it. The projects were probably a lot easier for people who allocated their time better than I did. Attendance to section is super mandatory.

I took this class as a GE, despite others telling me not to. I enjoyed the class a lot! If you are creative you will definitely like this class. The only downside is having to buy art materials for it, however you can get most, if not all materials at the bookstore. The discussion sections were my favorite part of class. Maricela was awesome!

analysis.name: Ivonne Gonzalez Gamboa
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Kinda a bit of work for 2 units, labs are a drag sometimes, but most things as long as you do it, you will get an A. Writing works are kinda sad, lecture is mandatory with points (I took virtual for lecture, in person for lab). The lectures are kinda an information dump, but you can lowk go into lab with 0 previous knowledge. Overall, better BILD4.

The professor was nice, but your grade depends more on the TA you get. There's one lecture and one lab a week. The lectures are boring and not that helpful. The lab notebook entries are due the night of the lab, which is pretty much busywork. Doable prelabs/quizzes. The class is easy and definitely doable, just heavy on the busywork.

The professor is sweet and very understanding but the lectures weren't that helpful. Grades are mostly dependent on the content learned from what's done in lab. If you get a good TA and lab partners, like I did, the class is not hard at all. As long as you go to lab and keep up with the assignments, you will do fine. :)

Class was easy but professor didnt teach much. You have to sign up to go to her office hours which is a 15 minute slot on Calendy and filled up really fast and I had to wait months to see her even for a mandatory accommodations meeting because she didnt respond to my email. My TA was amazing though, shout out to Mikkey, definitely reccommend.

The TA will make or break your experience (and grade) for the class. The Professor herself is very nice and has office hours that you can schedule to talk with her. There is 3 quizzes and 4 writing assignments and the writing assignments definitely take at least 2-3 hours. Can miss up to 2 lectures. Final is a group research poster presentation.

analysis.name: Karthik Ganapathy
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Ganapathy is a caring and helpful teacher. He sometimes skips steps in lectures but clarifies in office hours, email, or Piazza. His exams are fair, and he gave a generous curve. I believe this is his first time teaching, and he's already pretty good. I only see him improving and would definitely recommend him as a professor.

He actively ensured students had resources to excel but was a bit disorganized due to graduation. Quizzes were super easy I studied for around 10-20 minutes for each and completed them in ~10-20/50 minutes allotted. Final was also easy with no studying. Overall the material is easy and he taught in a digestible manner in the classes i did attend.

do not bother watching lectures or showing up to class,just read the textbook and do practice problems. his handwriting is borderline illegible at times which made his attempts at explaining his thought process even more convoluted. ive spoke to other students about this and its not just me who feels like this. try taking with other instructor

It is much more useful to teach yourself than to go to his lectures.  Luckily, homework assignments and quizzes were easy. The final was a little harder, but doable. Also took a while to respond on Piazza or through email. He was also rude sometimes to students

He made this class unnecessarily hard and tedious. He often came to lecture unprepared and made a lot of mistakes. Self study is definitely recommended over watching lectures/going to class. Try to take this class with a different professor.

analysis.name: Jennifer  Haase
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The people whining on here are acting like they have never taken a class before. Easy midterms, HW is long but based on textbook. One of the most caring professors I've ever had. Created a field trip to engage students, tries to learn names, added "career" info by mentioning ongoing SIO research opportunities. Easy class, nice prof

Expected MUCH worse given reviews. Yes attendance is mandatory for quizzes, yes there is alot of homework assigned, but her grading scheme is designed so that one of these categories is dropped if you do well on the midterms (very ez, open note. if you can do basic algebra and interpret a graph ur fine.) Prof Skrentny is an amazing professor! He's super funny and everything you need to know to do good on the exams is covered in lecture. Lecture attendance is optional, section is mandatory, but highly recommend going to both. Readings for hw but you don't really have to do them.

Such a great class! Although it was a 3 hours he kept it interesting. Hes very smart and definitely knows what he is talking about. Great at presenting the material. There are readings and two exams. If you just show up and take notes, you'll get a good grade. He goes over all the readings in lecture, and not to mention he's super hot ;)

SOCI 50: the BEST teacher I've ever had, and I'm a second-year here. Lecture isn't mandatory, but he doesn't post lecture slides or anything from class. I found this incredibly engaging because, as long as you take good notes and go to the discussion, you should be set. Discussion is mandatory (2 points each show up to class and participating)

analysis.name: Kuiyi Shen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He has a bit of a thick accent, but you get used to it if you attend class regularly. It helps to reference the textbook and what he says in lecture when studying for exams. As of my taking it, the exams are not cumulative, so they're more like unit tests. Super easy if you study and attend lecture. Tons of extra credit too! Textbook provided!

Absolutely loving him. The only downside is his heavy accent. But exams are super easy with many extra credits. No homework. Readings are helpful but you can still get a good grade not doing them. He knows a lot in his field and if you pay attention, the lectures have quite interesting contents. Attendance for both LE and DI are mandatary tho.

It's obvious that Shen knows what he's talking about but he's very boring.  His accent can be a little tough to understand, but it's not super bad.  The class itself is easy, and you can get up to 20 pts of extra credit on exams so over 100%s is pretty doable.  Textbook is NOT necessary and super expensive.

He is a professor who cares a lot about what he teaches. He provides exam review powerpoints so you don't have to study every single image presented. His accent is a little strong, but nothing that most people can't handle. The exams are easy, and the content is actually pretty interesting.

Thick accent but he's the sweetest prof. Mando attendance but I did not pay attention in class and did other hw instead. Some ppl take lectures v seriously and take detailed notes- it's really not necessary. Two exams where you explain the details and meaning of the art shown- he gives a study guide with just 30 pieces. 8 of 30 will be on the exam.

analysis.name: Reem Khojah
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: BENG2; Teacher barely taught, everything was handled by the TA; for a two credit class the amount of work given was absurd, labs and hw every week, questions were hard, only got help going to the TA, even then still got points off on it; mid term and final was fine, just review her mcqs, the study guide wasn't helpful; gave flipped classroom vibes

She didn't have a syllabus ready at the start of the class and only created one midway through the quarter. She would show up to lectures for about 15 minutes before leaving the TA to handle the rest. Overall, she was disengaged and uncaring. Wasn't responsive to emails. TA was good. Thanks Dennis!

If you do the work you will be very well prepared for all the tests. TA office hours were VERY useful. She would go through stuff before/after the tests for people who were paying attention and is a pretty lenient grader.
took beng 277. class was easy but prof was never there and dgaf. ta was helpful. she kept asking "do you feel abandoned" like every class lol. weird.

beng1 is incredibly easy to pass - basically the only way to fail is to have 2 unexcused lab absences (you get 1 grace absence). everything is pretty much just graded for participation, so even if you end up with a bad lab group, it doesn't matter. labs are very straightforward - they tell you what to do and you do it

analysis.name: Kathy Lacefield
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Lacefield is great! She's super nice and a very clear lecturer! Her tests are not crazy specific as some other professors! Print out her slides  before lecture and fill them out during class, and you're good to go! A BUNCH of ec is offered, have to show up to class to earn them tho! Took her during summer and it was doable!

Course is only graded by 3/4 exams. The class is easy, and the textbook isn't needed to do well on exams. She is extremely kind and caring, but something about the class lacked the ability to really engage me. I found myself disinterested in otherwise interesting material. Good class to grade bump your psyc electives, but a lot of it got lost to me

4 exams (final is included) and drops lowest one. exams are straightforward and aligns with the material during lectures. sometimes, she used some terms from the textbook that wasnt mentioned at all during lectures so keep an eye out for that on exams. she allows a double sided printed or handwritten cheat sheet which is a plus

Prof. Lacefield  was nice and I found her class fun and engaging. I feel I deepened my knowledge of psychology. She does require a textbook, but it is findable if you look enough online. Quizzes were your entire grade, but they were fair and she drops the lowest score. If you read the book, you can succeed even without paying attention in lecture.

Attendance not mandatory. Don't recommend if Thomas Morton is the TA. Exams are extremely specific. Allowed cheat sheets every exam. No required textbook. Professor is nice but mocks people with substance use disorders

analysis.name: Clifford Kubiak
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's a nice guy but his lectures are not at all engaging nor helpful, basically you self learn the entire course. Doesn't post lecture slides, speeds through content and spends more time making side comments than doing examples or explaining them clearly. Graded on 2 midterms, final, and weekly hw (achieve). I'd say avoid him if you can.

I hate this class. Surprisingly he talks super slow but zooms through the lecture. I hate that we don't get cheat sheets or at least one midterm dropped. This class is way too hard and I have to teach myself since he doesn't post the slides. TAs just sit and flirt with each other all lecture they're lowkey careless but hey I get it

He's nice but only knows how to teach 6CH. Lecture was him reading off the slides. The first midterm was bad because no one (including the professor and TAs) knew the right answers until 4 weeks after. A lot of midterm scores dropped by more than a letter grade after they got the key straight. Would be cool to talk to outside class

Try to avoid him if you can. During his lectures, he zooms past slides without fully explaining them. I believe this happens because he has taught the honors section of Chem 6C and other higher-level chemistry classes. He expects you to have some knowledge going into his lectures, and he does not release the lecture slides.

Professor definitely understand the content, but he assumes we just finished getting our PhDs and speeds through the lecture slides. Content isn't easy, tests are incredibly difficult, averaging 60%, discussion helps a LOT though, but overall: Do not recommend unless you have to (hes a nice guy though)

analysis.name: Ryan Kastner
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Poor study materials & unhelpful in OH. We were given practice exams using a different framework and told to translate between them before using them to study without an answer key. If you have accommodations, be prepared for a lot of back and forth and indifference to your disability specialist's recommendations. Piazza is neglected for Discord.

The course felt very unorganized overall, and the exams were quite difficult, PA submission issues came up repeatedly and often took several days to get resolved. In lecture, concepts were sometimes explained in a very abstract way without enough concrete examples, which made the class much harder to follow. This was a very frustrating experience.

Cool and funny guy. Very responsive outside of class. He's a good lecturer if you consider that the content of the class is intrinsically difficult to teach. Some PAs were fun, while other PAs were shaky due to instructor-side issues. PAs have leaderboards you get to compete for if you want extra points. Exam questions are confusing to decipher.
One of the most fun CSE class and prof, you run code on the GPU and compete for leaderboard positions for extra credit. Also funny and cool, material could be a bit hard though.
Most unenjoyable content I've learned about of all time. Not the teachers fault but don't take this class as an “easy system” because it's not worth it

analysis.name: Kimberly Schurmeier
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 260 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT take this professor!! Her lectures are nothing like the exams. She gives you a little bit of time to complete the exams and her exams are really hard. She grades every detail and a small mistake lowers your exam grade by a lot.
All those positive reviews below this one were very likely written by Kimberly herself or a teachers pet. Take them with a grain of salt. Hardass class with a hardass professor. Steer clear.

100% agree with the others on this page who claims her grading policy is on the stricter side. She isn't the most accessible outside of class; it takes her anywhere from 5-7 BUSINESS days to get back(so if there are any urgent issues you might have, I would keep this in mind). I think her lectures oversimplify the material of what you're tested on.

Not a huge fan of her grading policy. She is more on the stricter side with grading and can be quite picky with answers. However, I dislike how exam questions can be as much as 30 points each. If you get one part of the question incorrect, the rest of the question is messed up as well with large point deductions. She simplifies content as well.

Good lectures that are straight to the point and well explained (both synchronous and asynchronous). However, the homework, practice problems, and exam reviews do not prepare you for the exam: the type of questions is completely different, questions are awkwardly worded and if you don't include EVERY definition in the lecture you won't pass.

analysis.name: Kyle Kehrer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lots of extra credit. Very clear & organised slides. Lecture mainly teaches concepts & how to approach different types of problems. Possible to self-study because all details are clearly shown in slides, which makes mandatory attendance a bit annoying. Overall still highly recommends him.

his class might be a little boring, but i think every physics class is just boring in its own way. His grading scale is very nice and the quizzes are very similar to the final. 4 quizzes, 1 final, lowerst can count lower if ur final is higher than it. overall pretty good

As someone who has never taken a physics course prior, his lectures, grading rubric, and opportunities for office hours/test corrections over summer session made it very easy to feel reassured that you can succeed with the right effort. Overall, he is also very understanding and easy to talk to when confused about new material. Highly recommend!

I don't think you can get a better professor than him tbh for this class. Lectures covered relevant material for quizzes and hw (though mandatory attendance). He also has a very generous grading policy.

analysis.name: Karen Dobkins
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great class, great prof! Definitely recommend. She is super enthusiastic and explains the material very well. 2 midterms, 1 final all non-cumulative (multiple choice + short answer). No papers. No clickers. You should go to class if you want an A, only seeing the slides isn't good enough because a lot of what she says ends up on the exams.

Exams are worth 85% of ur grade. There are 3 exams and they were all 60-65 questions long. Unlucky for me, it was an 8am class. Lectures are super dense. Try not to take other lecture heavy classes along with this one. I wouldn't take her again. Exams were super hard and class average is low!!!
Great teacher. Meditates with the class which I found initially unnecessary, but ended up very grateful with. A very good woman and a wonderful teacher. Thanks Karen Dobkins! I wish you all the best.
Tests were worth 85% of our grade (no cheat sheet). Despite the mindful moments every morning, they didn't work the morning she said she should curve down because the average was a B.

The problem with her class is that there's no consistency. She would often ask questions about things she only briefly mentioned and were ignored by the book and her own powerpoints, her TAs would discuss topics that she would go on later to say should be ignored. Questions are also terribly worded. (She removed 20% of the first exam's questions)

analysis.name: S. Leutgeb
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He focus on the important concept you need to know. Midterms consist of 5 Free responses and come DIRECTLY from the lecture. Reading the book was a plus. He's crystal clear on what you need to know and I thought he was VERY good. 3 midterms + 1 final and drop one lowest score.( No need to take final if you do well on MTs)&10% extra credit. takehim

There are 3 midterms (lowest score dropped) and 1 final. Reading is required, and there are short iClicker reading quizzes each lecture. iClicker responses are worth 10% extra credit, which is VERY GENEROUS. Exams are straightforward and representative of the lecture material. Dr. Leutgeb is very clear and dedicated. Definitely recommend!

We had 2 midterms (1st 50pts, 2nd100pts), clicker quizzes (+10% pts if you score well), and a final (200pts). His exams & final for us were all multiple choice and were still fairly difficult (10-20%calculations, restconceptual). Don't take if you are busy. Podcasts and TA are reliable. I could've done WAY better if I had more time.

One of the best professors I have ever taken a class with, although your grade is entirely made up of midterms and the final exam (which can be dropped if you do well enough on the midterms), the exams are super super fair and publishes a study guide which tells you EXACTLY what will be on the exams. Offers 7% extra credit if you go to lecture.

Class content was enjoyable and the content in slides and lectures were actually all covered on exams w no random stuff. I thought study guide and review sessions told you exactly what you need to know. Exams were mcq and tricky. lowest exam dropped (even final) prof was great and it was very clear what was expected of you. 10-12% EC offered.

analysis.name: Wade Lindenberger
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Hands down one of few best professors at UCSD. Take him without any doubts.

Professor Lindenberger is definitely the best Professor I have ever met in UCSD. Tests are open notes, open book. You can even bring a computer when taking the test. Not very much workload. And Professor Lindenberger is really caring, considerable, and humorous. Take him if you have the choice!

Very good prof, relaxed teacher, always friendly, makes grading criteria clear. He's super nice and helpful and will always explain things to you if you need any help. I would recommend him for sure; he only gives a few assignments too and they're pretty fair. He is always calm and you will have a chill class with him.

Lindenberger treats his students like friends and clearly knows his subject material. Reading quizzes done in class once per week or so. Occasionally asks for short responses via CourseKey. The two papers aren't difficult if you get started early. Lectures aren't really him talking; instead it is heavily multi-media based.

Best professor I've ever had at UCSD! The class has many components, which helps you earn points towards your final grade. The midterm is worth as much as the final, which is not cumulative. The group project was fun and useful. He gives extensive quiz and exam guidance, which really helps guide your studying. He is so nice and caring as well!

analysis.name: Marina Langlois
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 121 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Looooooots of Homework!! Her class goes so fast. The homework, the lectures, and the tests are three different worlds!!
toooooooooo much homework!!! too much!!! you will know if u choose her. trust me!

A good professor; but I would not recommend to take her lectures regarding her pointless lecturing style. Although she instructs so fast, she still cannot finish all the content based on the syllabus. Again, she is a very nice professor but poor in lecturing skills
Marina is a very good professor showing caring to every student but I wish she could slow down the speed of instruction so that we could follow

Dont recommend this professor. Talking extremely fast during lecture; 40 seconds on average for each clicker question (how could students respond to a question with 40 seconds????); always giving bad examples to demonstrate ideas and making things worse!

analysis.name: Tin Lam
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Lam made learning chemistry a lot more easier than expected. In comparison to other chemistry classes, her quizzes, midterm and final seemed relatively easier. You must go to every lecture as she does do clicker questions but she drops the lowest quiz if you attend 80% of the lectures and lowest test at the end of the quarter.

Lam speaks super fast, she mumbles, she is never clear. She uses every minute of lecture to "teach". She is a professor who barely scratches the material in lecture but on the exams expects you to know the material so much more in depth. There is no clear grading scale but basically a 60% was a C-. The quizzes are too long for the time given.

Literally speeds through everything and snatches papers away faster than the projector can keep up with. I find it much easier to watch podcasts from other professors and go to the chem help room than try to understand what she is doing. When I leave her class i am frustrated and feel like I can't do stem. Only positive is the homework extra credit

Professor Lam doesn't put surprises on her tests. They are all very representative of lecture material and homework. As long as you study her notes and homework word for word you will definitely get an A. She really knows how to break down the concepts. Just make sure you attend all the lectures because it is hard to get those performance points.

After having a traumatizing experience with AP Chem, I came into Lam's class expecting the worst - I was quite mistaken. Her tests are very fair and similar to her examples from lecture; clicker quizzes are straightforward; there is a ton of extra credit on the hw; her accent does not impede on your comprehension; and she gives out crib sheets!

analysis.name: Lisa Cartwright
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Slides and lectures were disorganized in structure. Also, for a course focused on visual culture, her slides sure were designed in a way that made it unnecessarily hard to read (so much for accessibility..) Her assignments had no clear criteria. Thankfully, my TA was super capable so I didn't leave the class with nothing at all.

graded on participation and 6 “reflections”, but none of the homework has a clear outline and you kinda just have to go based on what your TA chooses. attendance was mandatory but the way they checked depended on TA. lectures were unclear, she talks like a chat gpt bot. fairly easy but she isn't lenient, textbook is overly expensive and unnecessary

The entire class was essentially the prof teaching content from book she co-authored. 4 absences (justified or not)= fail. Unclear grading criteria, overly wordy and vague prompts. You can tell the prof is passionate about her content. Easy credits as long as you are punctual about attendance. You won't know your grade is until the end of the qtr.

She is clearly passionate about art. Gave the option to attend her class in person or via Zoom. Grades based on attendance, 3 projects, and 3 writing assignments. However, all components are very TA-dependent. The textbook isn't necessary to succeed; luckily, you aren't forced to purchase it.

made us buy a textbook around $50 that we didn't use at all. She wrote the textbook so maybe thats a reason why its nessecary. Other than that she was caring and nice, had zoom as an option to join in on class which was very considerate of her.  Hard to reach outside of class tho. Only 6 assignments, 3 mini essays and 3 art projects no exams.

analysis.name: Megan Strom
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Keep devices away until attendance question at end, don't talk while she is, and at least try to discuss content w/ partner when it's time - you won't have a problem in lecture. I found her lectures to be helpful in understanding readings, and readings are interesting if you're willing to engage w/ it. Midterm and final were writing on demand.

Very easy class, just the reading is annoying. Her lectures do cover enough of the information needed so you don't have to read closely; a light skim should be fine. Attendance for lectures and discussion sessions are mandatory. There is a no technology policy for the DOC program. She has gotten mad at people for being late or not taking notes.

Great lecturer and is super passionate about the subject, but she is a bit cold and standoffish when speaking to her one-on-one. Your grade honestly depends on what TA you get, but the midterm and final are pretty straightforward, and they prep you the whole quarter for both. The bad part is that it's very anti-tech, and there is a LOT of reading.

She is a great and strict lecturer, she would kick students out of the lecture hall if they are late for 5 minutes or take their phone out of their bag, however, she does this for people to focus on the course material. The grading is 100% based on your TA. Just join all the sections and go through all the readings, and you will get a fair score.

Fine lecturer. Not the most outwardly nice person, but good at teaching the course content. Hard on no technology/gen AI/cheating policies. Tended to rush the end of lecture due to lots of content and not enough time to go over it all. Will kick you out if you're later than 5 mins to class, sees you're not prepared for class, will call you out.

analysis.name: Simeon Man
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The class is really easy material. A lot of the stuff that was tested on was not part of the readings so you have to go to lecture to get that information, but the tests are really easy. There was a final paper based off of an interview which was obnoxious but overall the class was super easy and a good choice for GEs.

Lectures are organized and recorded but can be pretty slow. Midterm is not bad if you watch the lectures and memorize the words he provides. Final is a take home essay. There is a lot of reading and participation is mandatory for discussions, although it is very dependent on your TA.
Not too hard to score well on this. Good way to finish off your GEs
Very understanding professor. Understands people's living situations and gives them grace when it comes to homework submissions

Nice guy overall but the contents and how he lectures could use much improvements. The 103 class is just a repetition of how bad militarism (especially the US) is with examples taken out of full context. Mainly narrates the lectures and examples with bias and basically repeats that until the end of the quarter.

analysis.name: Steve Levkoff
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 362 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The combination of his condescending demeanor and his rudeness when answering questions made this class a bad experience. Furthermore, he fell way behind, had to cram most of 100c into 3 weeks, and assigned outside-class lectures to be tested on. He loves to test on info he failed to teach, so if you like surprises on exams be sure to take him.

Since he spent a lot of time on materials relevant to 120B, he was behind the schedule for both midterms and final exam. On both 2nd midterm and final, he put questions which he definitely didnt teach them. I dont know how he does normally, but this quarter he was very inefficient, and I highly do not recommend him.

Questions on tests were confusing. He intentionally tries to word test questions abstractly, so students have struggle with questions. A class with this much of material is hard enough, so there is no need to be more confusing.
Just take his class, and you will know the definitions of a good professor.

Pros: He's very funny (dry humor) and connects his class to present day news and topics. No attendance is taken for either discussion or lecture. He podcasts all of his lectures. Cons: Overall grade is mostly dependent on midterm and final. Both the midterm and final is all free response. Doesn't use canvas and have to pay for his ai website.

analysis.name: Achinta Nandi
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He skips lectures without prior announcement. He also says he'll post the lectures he missed but never posts them. The midterm also had two whole problems with wrong numbers that left me confused.

The exams were not particularly difficult and were mostly based on the material we had learned in class. There were also bonus points available on the test. The professor is very sociable and clearly very knowledgeable. Attendance is not required for in-person lectures, as all classes are recorded and made available for later viewing.

Often went on tangents during lecture, commonly moved class to online with short notice or canceled class, saying there would be a posted lecture but it never happened. Handwriting is not legible, only writes on chalkboard. Homework was never graded in a timely manner and midterm reviews had no posted keys. Overall grade curve was generous

Its a proofs class. You pretty much need to understand everything. It gets hard around chapter 14 or week 7. Has a bad time with releasing recorded lectures on time and has a hard time explaining harder subjects. Overall, would still take if doing pass no pass, but not sure about letter grade. I believe he will curve though

The professor cares about the student's understanding when he explains things in class and explains concepts/train of thought mostly clearly. Sometimes goes on side tangents which are unrelated to course material, and occasionally makes mistakes on the board. Also, as one review said, he promises video lectures but ends up not recording them.

analysis.name: Neil Gong
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Can't speak to how he was for other classes but 140A was an excellent class with a lot of interesting guest speakers, lectures, and topics covered. Not an easy class, mandatory attendance, and the exam was a lot of writing but if you're interested in the incarceration system it's a really good class. I learned a lot

he's nice but his lectures were boring. he relied on group discussion and would cold call on people from each group like we were in high school. he didn't post our grades until week seven and grades the midterms harshly. only gave us an hour and 20 mins to answer multiple choice questions, two short answer questions, an essay. don't recommend him

Professor was pretentious when it came to grading. If you're not used to writing 1,400 words in person in about an hour and 20 minutes for midterms don't take this class. Also grades were posted week 7 and I'm not sure if that was intentional so more people didn't drop the class. If you're taking for upper div. credit as a non writing major don't

reading assignments due before class and weekly team quizzes (open note). harsh grader on midterm/final: all writing on blue book, 3 short answers (2 paragraphs) and one long essay (4-5 paragraphs), cheat sheet allowed. grades weren't posted till week 7 unfortunately.

Prof Gong was nice but sometimes inconsistent with grading criteria and expectations. Course was graded on weekly group quizzes (open-note) and a midterm and final which were handwritten essays and will make your entire arm ache. My class was able to advocate for the use of cheat sheets on our exams but he might not do the same for others.

analysis.name: Maysa Nichter
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Nichter gives a lot of pre-law opportunities, but if that's not your thing, there's nothing for you here. It's easy in that there's not much you could do to guarantee that you meet all the vague criteria that the course grades by, so it's pretty much up to luck. This course was not rigorous at all, and I felt like I gained nothing.

If you are interested in pursuing law, I HIGHLY recommend taking one of Professor Nichter's classes. I was lucky enough to take her legal reasoning course. She taught us how to thoroughly analyze cases via the IRAC method and write legal memos, client advice letters, and demand letters. TA's may strictly grade though and write minimal feedback.

I took her for both 104J and 104U this winter quarter.104J is writing-heavy with three papers, one being six pages, another being four, and the final being six pages (released the day before it's due). The papers were time-consuming and tedious, but if you pay attention, you will be fine. Take her class; she's an amazing professor and so helpful.

104U was one of my favorite classes. The midterm paper is released the same day it is due, and if you pay attention, it's very doable and straightforward. The final is a seven-page max paper assigned the night before. Taker her class! It seems intimidating at first, but she makes it easily accessible, and her lectures are very helpful.

Great class with a great professor. Only thing to note is that final paper is 5-6 pages and is released the day before it's due, so you don't get very much time to work on it. Other assignments are usually done in class throughout the week they're due which is helpful+there's very clear instructions with rubrics for each assignment

analysis.name: Richard Norris
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is the best professor I've had at UCSD by far! The class was very enjoyable with 2 fun full-day field trips (they're mandatory but you are going to want to go!). The class was flipped where you watch videos at home then discuss in class but the classes aren't mandatory, only the lab days are. Overall easy grader and assignments too.
Lots of drawing, a field trip, a little confusing canvas page, but overall very sweet and really cares about the students

Prof. Norris is very passionate about this subject and does his best to make sure you are too. This was an EXCELLENT and super fun class - the tests were really hard, but he curves it somehow (he doesn't explain it but I think it's participation-based?) and that takes the sting off. He's also good for one-on-one if you go to OH with questions.

Class is interesting but a lot of work and requires a lot of memorization. During lectures he usually draws pictures which I couldn't learn from, but I guess some people can. He puts his lecture notes online though which have the concepts written out so those are helpful. Don't bother reading the book for this class.

Excellent professor who knows a lot about the subject and field geology and is a good professor to get you used to paleobiology and field geology in general. Field trips can be tough physically but midterm and final were quite challenging but fair with lots of extra credit opportunities. Strongly recommend!!

analysis.name: Ndapa Nakashole

omg this guy is insane to understand and he really doesn't go in depth in topics at all unless someone asks him a question. go to ur discussions and ur ta's will be extremely helpful. nothing about the homework is explicitly covered in class and he really is all over the place. he says "um" and "uhh" like 10000 times during lecture. sweet guy tho.

no clear grading criteria on problem sets, doing homework on mcgrawhill was extremely frustrating to deal with. course overall is disorganized and prof doesn't explain material clearly, lecture material has little to no correlation with homework problems. please wait another quarter for another genetics prof if possible

analysis.name: Glenn Tesler

He is very rude to students who ask for help! I walked into office hours to find him practically yelling at a student because he did not understand a problem. Aside from that, his final is incredibly hard and will lower your grade dramatically! Would not recommend
Tesler is awkward and mean when it comes to office hours and interacting with him personally. Wastes testing time, hard to finish exam in time frame.

analysis.name: Siddharth Vishwanath

Homework and discussion is really hard, but it will be easier than midterm and finals. If you have the time, go to her office hours, it really helps, definitely choose her.

Very kind but I found doing homework to be more helpful than going to lecture sometimes bc it's very fast paced and not everything is explained well + skips steps. Discussion/lecture not mandatory and discussion sheets are posted on Canvas. Questions asked on the midterm/final are pretty fair but still difficult class.

analysis.name: Mark Young
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Young taught the best class I have taken at UCSD. Initially the syllabus seemed very stressful and threatening, but it seemed a lot nicer after he explained it in the first class. Attendance is a HUGE factor, but he is very understanding. The class is fantastic. A lot of discussion about modern topics like AI and technology. Def recommend

It's GE so I wouldn't have chosen to take this class. But with that said I got way more out of the experience than I would have thought. I'm a better writer and thinker because of the teacher. Definitely worth taking.

I learned more about writing in 10 weeks with Professor Young than in all of my time in high school and community. Really smart and very caring, especially if you are trying to learn. The grading system puts the focus on effort instead of perfect work, so it takes the pressure off and lets you experiment and actual get better. Made me think!
Great professor! No other writing course has explained in such detail the mentality of how to be an effective  researcher. The  content was engaging and the  grading was easy.

Loved Professor Young! This class is literally completion based so its hard to do badly, but he still cares how much effort you put into it. Take it seriously and communicate with professor, but dont stress about getting a bad grade. Easy A.

analysis.name: Pinar Yoldas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There were few readings in this course and most assignments were essays— it was easy although time-consuming but might vary by section. Lectures had a no-devices rule and were mostly about neuroscience, so might not be everybody's right fit. She is very passionate about the material and frequently interacted with students during lecture though, W!

As a neuro. major, I took her in Winter '26 for CAT 2: Art and the Brain. She showed incredible interest in her lecture topics: sensation, perception, synesthesia, art as memory, dreams, emotions, and faces. In lecture, super interesting art pieces shown & 2 fun olfactory sense activities. 

I recommend, going to her lectures with an open mind! :D

Lectures can be boring at times but also interesting really varies on the day. However, there is a clear disconnect between TAs and her because (this may just be my TA) never had a clue about anything due dates prompts concepts etc etc. Focused heavily on neuroscience aspect while TAs are more art based. Made things really wonky.

If u like neuroscience and art, u will like this class. I didn't have much interest in it but the class was super easy--there are only a few assignments. however, your grade is 100% dependent on the TA. Dr. Yoldas tries her best to incorporate references that cater toward our generation's interests so sometimes we watched stuff like slime vids lol

Professor Yoldas CAT 2 class is interesting especially if you love neuroscience and art. Class is super easy and a lot less work compared to CAT 1 despite being 2 units more. While grade is entirely dependent on TA, the lectures were interesting and it is easy to tell she loves what she teaches.

analysis.name: Zachary Brants
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I truly believe Brants is a solid professor. He never fails to be energetic and shows great passion for philosophy. His lectures were fun at the start though it got a little dull near the end. 5 P/NP assignments for the whole quarter. Study guide is provided, easy A for the midterm. Pop quizzes are P/NP and quite easy even w/o doing the reading.

Professor Brant's is an excellent lecturer who makes the content very interesting. The reviews who rate him poorly do not reflect his teaching style. If you do the readings (which are quite lengthy but interesting) you will be fine on pop quizzes. If you are looking for a throw away class and dont care to learn then dont take the course.

I thought this professor was excellent. He was very descriptive in his slides. Gave study guides for exams and easy pop quizzes on readings. If you participate in class discussions you will definitely learn more. Participating in class is a key part of your education so don't listen to the bad reviews it's people who don't do the work.

His passion for philosophy is admirable, but a little too much, as he often goes over time during lectures. Attendance is not considered mandatory, but he does do pop quizzes to ensure students are attending class. The lectures just go over the readings, and they're not engaging. Also, he has a no-technology policy, so come to class with a notebook

The professor is a great, passionate lecturer, and does a good job engaging the class in discussion. There's no attendance, but there are pop quizzes, which are easy to pass if you did the reading, which is interesting and not long. The essays are pass/fail and you get much leeway on how to write them. Midterms and finals are easy.

analysis.name: Avi Yagil
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I have had Professor Yagil for two lab classes now. Obviously not by choice, he writes quizzes that are really difficulty considering the lecture is always behind the lab. I dont comprehend how UCSD decide curriculum for this class, but all I can say is I hope your TA is nice and can help you understand the material.

I never saw this dude the whole quarter but my TA Alessio was chill. Lab reports were kind of annoying but they drop 1 lab and 1 quiz so its alright. Anything above 90% is an A or A+, so generous cutoffs.

We were given biweekly quizzes about physics concepts even though we were already being quizzed on this material in 1c. When it was brought up to him, he purposely ignored anything we had to say and argued that we were just not studying hard enough. Avi Yagil, I don't hold any personal grudges towards you, but I hope u reconsider your career choice

Lecture slides are helpful in the labs, but impossible to follow during lectures. He is  a fast and soft speaker w/ an accent which makes things harder to follow. Homework is cake compared to final exam. Do many extra problems from book to prepare for final, lab material is not covered. TAs were usually confused about how to handle things in labs.

Prof. Yagil and the other two profs "instructing" this course have never shown their faces to the class and have never held office hours. Extremely hard quizzes and the lab reports are graded ridiculously hard. No instruction on how to do things. Instead of trying to teach us, they lower the grading scale and we learn nothing. Incredibly lazy.

analysis.name: Christine Zoumas-Morse
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: One of the most considerate professors. I understand why her courses are always at max capacity. You can apply a lot from this class to real life.

Dr. Zoumas - best prof here! She is so knowledgable in her field and her story is so interesting. Her class was easy and low-commitment, but it was also engaging. Great professor in public health! Interesting and personable lectures and is very caring towards students.

She is the most amazing professor! She is very interesting when she speaks because you can see the amount of care she puts into her lectures and the material. But she is kinda off on her assignments and when they are due! so do all the assignments even if they don't have a due date.
Extremely nice and easy going class, as long as you show up you should receive and A+.

analysis.name: Zhuowen Tu

AWFUL AWFUL AVOID AT ANY COST!

analysis.name: Kenneth Zeger

His midterm was extremely difficult, and from someone who has never gotten a B before, I would be happy with a C. He's clear and I like his lecturing style, but in my opinion the tests are just a huge leap from the material in class.

1 midterm, 1 final (40%, 60% or 100% final) Try to get an A on the midterm to buffer your final score. Final was extremely difficult. Midterm resembled the homework, final was MUCH more math intensive.

He is clearly a smart guy, but the leap in difficulty from what he teaches to what he tests on is gigantic. I mean, what purpose does it serve to make exams THAT difficult? ECE 109 was a hard subject, but I feel that the students should have been better prepared (by him) for what he expected out of us. I wish we could fill out CAPE's after finals.

He is very clear and precise when it comes to explanations however besides that, to get an A/B you need to self study.  His suggested problems don't help at all and you have to be the top 30% in the class just to get a B- or higher.  Good news is that most people don't self study, but if you do, you will be far ahead of the game.

analysis.name: Aaron Rosengren
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I thought he was a great professor that truly cares about his students. Goated professor, exams exactly like practice and HW, very clear expectations, so kind with grading, funny, lowkey beautiful looking

analysis.name: Aaron Drews
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work

review_highlights.comment: Lectures were very useful throughout the course. A little more guidance might have been offered with homework, but it was doable. Took him for CENG 15 during summer session II. Homework can be tough, but he gives out amazing notes and guides us through problem sets. Final exam was a bit tough, but it was similar to the homework.

Very little guidance for lab assignments was provided, but reports were graded as if there had been. Often did not provide adequate answers to questions posed in lab. Be prepared to do almost everything on your own and be marked down for any mistakes you make. I understand the need for self-direction, but am glad that I am done with this class.

Dr. Drews is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is probably my favorite. He is really brilliant and hilarious. Fluids is a tough course but he makes himself available outside of class to help students. Tests are very fair.

Professor's handwriting on the board is amazing, especially with that fancy chalk! Lectures were very clear and helpful for doing the homework. analysis.name: Danna Zhang
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work

She is a really nice professor. She is really patient when answer your questions, and she would like to listen to students concerns. Go to office hours if you need help. She's more than willing to try and assist you. Study hard for midterms/finals since they're heavily weighted.
Very nice and accessible. Exams and homework are a bit tricky.

Danna has a pretty strong academic background. She is pretty good at explaining concepts and materials. She will tell you which part is essential and which part you just have to know. She also offered students with a lot of help during her office hour. So she is a pretty good professor.

analysis.name: Sarah Aarons
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

Dr. Aarons definitely cares about her students and is really sweet. She is okay at explaining things but her exams were fairly difficult. Definitely need to read the textbook and understand concepts pretty well in order to do well in her class.

analysis.name: Aaron Pollack

Overall, a great lecturer. Super nice and willing to help. Homeworks were super manageable, and he gives plenty of hints for tougher problems.

Smart guy but does not listen to the students. Get ready to spend 5 hrs+ per week on his weekly hw and one drop. 2 midterms and does not allow dropping. If you are sick and did poorly in one, you are done. He was teaching new material at the last lecture and expect us to prepare it on the final.

His handwriting is definitely a problem but his lecture is not that bad. With that being said, if I have to review some concepts, I have to watch the videos again or read the textbook. I cannot just read the notes. However, homework is easy and inspirational. Overall an easy class. He could be a better instructor if he had better handwriting.

analysis.name: Eddie Aamari

Oh my goodness, I love this class. I'm not even done yet but I absolutely love him. If he taught all the math classes I'd need for a math minor, I'd do a math minor. Although the materials Prof. Aamari gave are really hard, his notes are helpful and his practice exams are also indicative. Overall, I like this professor, and I have learned a lot! By the way, the homework are tough.

LECTURES ARE SUPER DENSE. but i really appreciated it being organized and easy to follow on PPT. He was very enjoyable and always had savage jokes and replies on piazza. Class is work intensive with labs and hw due every week but doable and prepares you well for exams. read the book for better explanations when u get confused. that really helped

He's a great professor! I really loved this class. He does give a lot of homework, but I found it manageable. He obviously cares about how his students do in his class. I would definitely take him again.

analysis.name: Ron Evans
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work

Prof. doesn't prepare, he is just a brainiac & teaches by ear. The only good thing is that there is a HUGE curve.  I got a 50%, 27%, and who knows, but passed.

He is friendly, but his monotone voice and demeanor can scare you off. But after getting used to his OH, he IS one of the best profs. I have ever had. GENEROUS curve!

he is funny! he makes me think of Mr. Bean! but his tests are much harder than the homework. There are really little homework, which is kind of bad because you don't get as much practice. Sections are mandatory because there is a quiz every week. but the quizzes are simple and my TA even goes over what we need to know for the quiz every week.

Doesn't assign lots of hw; optional, but it helps because the weekly quizzes are exactly like the hw, only numbers change. Go to OH early in the course if you don't understand much. He's pretty good at clarifying. Midterms are HARD = nice curve..but for the final this qtr, he actually told us what kind of question #1 and #2 were going to be!

analysis.name: Aaron Coleman
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Coleman is a really chill guy and is in no way out to get his students or fail them. His midterm was very fair as was the final. Seriously, go to lecture each time, take notes and you will do well on the exams and quizzes. All his tests were very reasonable with some problems showing up directly from the problem sets. Really sweet, clear and chill

This course was not as easy as people made it out to be. The midterm was fairly straight forward but really long for class time given. The final on the other hand was really difficult and long even though it was said it would be shorter. Class was barely curved so my grade drastically fell! Def more Bs and Cs then A. Nice guy, but needs to be clear

Prof C is wonderful! His lectures are super clear, and the class material is straightforward. Dr Coleman was good but his midterm/final was hard. Some quizzes weren't bad but some had very confusing wording. need to go to class to understnad all the material..since it all guest lectures..just study all the slides very closely..and then go clarify the classes material with ta, since it will hlp you..got a B plus..and still tried quite a good effort..midterm hard..but final was esyy.

analysis.name: Julia Adrian
