Dr. Al Ajrawi's teaching method is the best because students are actively involved in the discussion and discussions are always lively and to the point.. Shenever distant herself from the students, even the shyest student participate in critical discussion. I consider myself very fortunate to have a full package to have a professor like you.

analysis.name: Marisa Abrajano
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took her Race and Ethnicity class. Unless you're lazy or plain stupid, there is absolutely no way anyone could fail her class. She posts up her lecture slides on ted and gives you a clear cut final and midterm study guide that is very similar to the actual test. HOWEVER, i'm not going to lie...the class is boring.

Abrajano is very helpful if you go to office hours. She gives a study guide for the midterm and final, so getting an A on those is pretty easy. Don't blow off the critical response paper, it is graded more toughly than the exams. It is refreshing to learn from a young woman.

Great professor.  TA was a fair grader also. I took her Latino politics class.  It is her passion and she taught it well.  Take home midterm. She also was cool enough to provide a study guide. She is easy on the eyes too! I recommend her.

easiest class i have ever taken. i regret taking it pass/no pass. if you go to lecture, u'll find out she basically summarizes the important parts of the book and her final "reviews" are basically a table of contents for her tests. if ur majoring in poli, avoid. but if ur doing it for as area of focus or just want an easy grade, highly recommended.

Classes are all lecture based.. She gives 2 unannounced in-class assignment, each 10% of your grade, and if you miss it, there's no make-ups. Lecture slides are unclear and sparse if you're counting on them. Exams are long essays + she gives study guides based on lecture material. She's monotonous and serious throughout so not a fun lecture either.

analysis.name: Omar Akbari
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. This whole 10-week class is based on 3 super difficult canvas exams. The questions are phrased in a way to intentionally confuse you. He seems like a nice, caring professor, but you can tell he does not care about teaching. Avoid at all costs!!!!

I think the class was okay. I liked that in lectures he would give real-life examples connecting to his research as well as doing a lab tour. This class is only exams so if you aren't a good test taker then this class may not be for you. Also, I felt like the wording on some questions was confusing. Dr Akbari is a nice person in lecture though.

Professor Akbari is amazing! The class was graded on 8 of 9 quizzes, each based on readings. Quizzes had 3-4 questions, were open-note, and easy if you understood the concepts. From Week 1, you join a group to present a paper. He's very caring, knowledgeable, and answers all questions. He even gave us a lab tour! Overall, an incredible class!

With all honesty, don't take this professor. He never replies to the emails sent and he only cares about teaching and getting out of there. His exams are online but in honesty, they are quite unfair. He purposely curves by the smallest point even though averages are horrible so it does not impact the student's grade in any positive way.

His lectures are not reflective of exam material. Exams are not a good measure of how well you understand the information. Other BIMM profs are a lot more understanding and provide a lot more grade improvement opportunities and EC. Take anyone else.

analysis.name: Akos Rona-Tas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Akos is passionate about the films and our ideas - but ultimately he has joined the dots with the sociology and the films we are watching, and classes could get boring when not talking about the films. I thought he was kind, approachable and a generous marker. A good easy(ish) and enjoyable sociology option. I'll remember him more than the course.

This class is definitely sociology, not film. The films are there to illustrate the concepts, not to be analyzed on their own. Pretty easy class, fun & interesting prof. Three exams, all short answer (not essay). The questions are grouped based on lectures, films, & readings. If you pay attention it's very easy.

Grade based on weekly/biweekly assignments (10 total), 1 midterm, 1 final. Very caring, allowed us the chance to try again for a couple assignments that a lot of the class was confused about. Lectures somewhat all over the place. Responds to emails very fast but short responses.

Difficult boring class. Professor does give good examples. Make sure you go to class and get a good TA. If unsure go to TA's office hours for clarification. Book was useful, but also boring. Important to learn material for future classes, since it will apply.

one in class midterm and in class final. watched a film everyday in class. reading topics coordinated with the film topic as well. he seems to know his stuff. okay teacher overall. not too bad of a class, ive had worse.

analysis.name: Faik Akif Tezcan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You'll do well in professor Tezcan class if you do two simple things: attend lecture and do the book problems. Most of his quizzes address concepts or certain types of problems  that are included in the lectures and/or book problems, and if you focus on that you'll be Gucci.

Do not ever judge a chem prof by their 6 series reviews. Tezcan is easily one of the best profs at ucsd, and his course was amazing. He takes time and care to get to know his students, his lectures are interesting and engaging, and he is great at showing students recent research, which most other profs don't. If you can take a class with him, do it

Many questions you are tested on, you have never seen anything like it before. Unreliable at office hours. Terrible book. I wanted to learn but the class made it impossible. I got a D when I was 1% away from a C-, not even a D+? But he let 20% of the class to leave with their cell phones during the final. Avoid if you care about learning/grade.

Nice professor but difficult class. Weekly quizzes do not reflect material in lectures. Quizzes are basically a midterm and final is most of your grade. The only redeeming thing is that he is an EXTREMELY generous grader.

The work load is light but he's an awful lecturer. I had background in Chem already, so I turned out fine but he makes so many mistakes during his recorded lectures that he just never mentioned again or fixed. He's so terrible at explaining new concepts to students...I don't even know how ppl without chemistry background would even pass his class.

analysis.name: Natacha Akshoomoff
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Class was really interesting. The textbook was GREAT. If you read you will get an A for sure. Professor has a lot of knowledge and her stories from the field are interesting. Lecture really isn't mandatory for a good grade. The only negative to the class is that she does not grade with +/-. My GPA went down when because I didn't get the + I earned.

The material was interesting; unfortunately, Professor Akshoomoff put us to sleep just about every day.  She tests based on information in the textbook and on the slides.  There isn't too much variation between the two.  The lecture notes are posted on WebCT, but are difficult to read, due to the small font.  Know EVERYTHING about the disorders!
Make sure to know lecture material and book material . Helpful professor but exams were pretty lengthy and have to know a lot of material.

analysis.name: Andrew Barton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Super chill class and very nice professor. Memory based so I used flash cards to study. Practice questions very similar to exams, and he did have some trick questions on exams but in my opinion they were easy to catch. Discussions had a decent amount of work to do, and attendance for both lecture and discussion was required. Pretty easy A

3 tests and a final. Attendance is mandatory, but he talks extremely fast, so you will barely hear everything. Uses clickers for attendance, which is 10% of the grade. Tests are completely made up of trick questions. If only he had straightforwardly asked questions, a lot more students would have succeeded.

Taught half the class, had really interesting lectures, and explained content well. Lecture and discussion were mandatory and provided good study material. No trick questions on exams but definitely still required a decent amount of studying, and you can drop 1 of the 3 midterms or the final. I found lectures very engaging and loved the topics.

This is one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are super organized and easy to follow. He lays out very clearly what will be on exams and gives in-class practice questions that are extremely similar to the exam questions. You will still need to study & memorize but an A is super achievable.
Exams were overall representative of what was taught in the lecture. The material was often confusing, however, he was always open to answering questions from students. Attendance is mandatory.

analysis.name: Andrew  Chisholm
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: final grade is only on 2 midterms and 1 final (u can drop a midterm). very generous curve (220/300 is an A on the midterms), but with that you dont rlly know ur grade until he puts it into acad. history. lectures were boring but got the content across; he says some random things but they become EC on the final. hw and disc optional.

Grade based on two midterms (one can be dropped) and a final. Not too hard if you study, and has a generous curve. Discussion and lecture attendance isn't mandatory, and neither are weekly practice problems. Gives good idea of concepts on exams, and practice problems are helpful. Overall nice professor, and willing to help.

I just took him this Winter quarter, and I barely learned a single thing, lectures are random and all over the place. Exams are not representative of what we learn in class didn't know my grade because he applies a "curve" at the end. The final was on very specific details mentioned in class. Better to read outside of class.

This might've been the hardest class I've taken. The lectures were a bit hard to understand and sometimes gives unnecessary information that doesn't help us prep for the midterm and tests. Grade is test-based, but gives us a generous curve. The hw assignments are optional but the exams are much more harder than the hw.

Lectures are interesting and straightforward. Practice sets provided but they vaguely represent the midterms. The midterms are about 2x harder then the provided practices. On both midterms I got 200/300 which turned out to be an A. Difficult tests, generous curve. Grading solely based off two midterms and a final.

analysis.name: Anthony C Davis
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The WORST teacher I have ever had at UCSD. Doesn't tell you what he expects until the last min. Extremely disorganized. This professor was so bad that I felt compelled to register and warn others about possibly taking his class.  He grades easy but the class itself is SO frustrating because you never know what is going on. Waste of time.

The lecture and discussion attendance was mandatory, but he would just talk about the opera we were focusing on. Very nice, but there are 5 short essays and a final essay that is seven pages. His TAs were also very helpful and graded the essays easily. Easy class, just do the essays ahead so that it doesn't stress you out.

Wish I could give a better rating but he is disorganized and TA's were AWFUL and rude. However, he is VERY passionate about jazz and connected our lectures with personal accounts which was both interesting and insightful. Midterms/final/assignments were made out to be harder than they looked, though, listening examples were difficult to study for.

I am a musician and have been since I was young. Even knowing many (if not all) of the terms and techniques, the class was still hard to follow for me. It was not nearly structured enough and Professor Davis is SO passionate about the subject that he tries to impart as much knowledge as possible which just muddies up the content in general.
An easy class, no midterms, consists of five short essays and one final essay. But the short essays are graded pretty easy. But attendence is required not discussions though.

analysis.name: Andrea Mendoza
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I LOVE her she is so nice and the way this class was structured was through a grading contract and you can negotiate it for your final grade. She understands if you dont do all the readings. And you can speak in english or spanish. makes the class very nice open space
GOAT we talked abt yaoi once. just do all the assignments and try to participate in lecture and you're golden

Bro just write one paragraph a week on whatever movie is assigned that week, only 300 words. I stopped watching the movies after a few weeks, I just wrote the paragraph on whatever scene I skipped to. She's a great professor.

Professor Mendoza was super chill and accomodating this quarter! Course material was very engaging and interesting, and her discussion sections always felt welcoming and friendly. All assignments were basically graded on completion, so as long as you put in the effort you will definitely get an A.

analysis.name: Andrew deWaard
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Quite literally, one of the blandest professors I've had the opportunity to meet. The class consists of exams, and although they say it isn't based on memorization, it does really only test you on your ability to memorize the assigned readings. He drones on in lectures reading directly from the slideshow with no elaboration and is very down putting

If I could give him a negative score, I would. He's nice, but Professor deWaard is one of the worst professors/instructors I've had. His class consists of only three assignments worth 5% each, and the rest of your points come from 3 closed-book exams only testing how well you can memorize course content. Take ANY other professor if you can.

1. EXTREMELY off-putting right from the start-- his syllabus states that if you get a "C" in his course, your work indicates "no room for professional achievement".
2. Reads off an ipad in lecture--often from lengthy quotes and makes lecture difficult to follow and take notes on.
3. Completely lies about his exam expectations

In-person class 3 times a week, long boring lectures that you don't even know what to study and are surprised by the midterm questions. Just reads off the slides and doesn't elaborate. My biggest concern is the midterm exams. Unfair grading, and weirdly worded exams that were barley covered in class. DO NOT TAKE HIM
Forces liberal political views on students, tests are overly difficult.

analysis.name: Amna Salam
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: for 104V, love her, she's very cool. Easy hw assignments, the midterm and final were relatively easy because of the study guides she provided. I didn't read the textbook because everything we needed to know was on her slides, she made that clear from day 1. I'm not a fan of group presentations but overall the class was easy, I also learned a lot!

Little to no homework (I spent ten hours or less of working outside of lecture), which is a lot less than my other poli sci classes), just doing 3 memos and preparing for one group presentation. Midterm and final are straightforward and easy to study for. The lectures could be more interesting though. Her outfits eat and she is a cool person!

No podcasts but slides are fairly one to one with what she is saying if you miss lecture. Graded by 3 assignments, midterm, and final. Provides feedback and help if you're ever confused on the material. She also made some lectures very interactive and fun, playing little games that coincide with what we're learning for the week.

Class is straight to the point. Grade consists of three memos, group presentations and closed book midterm/final. Downside; rude and has yelled at the class for talking before a presentation, but not many people talking. Could've approached it differently. Regardless, if you're ok with group presentations & closed book exams, take her, its doable.

I really like her; she is like a diva. Her tests are just like the study guide; you would end up with an A if you study it. Group presentations are not as bad as people make it seem. she is actually nice yes she yelled at the class but for a valid reason no one likes to be talked over.

analysis.name: Leesa Anzaldo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 113 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Her lectures are based textbook, there are a lot of theorems but she explains them, and she is willing to answer questions about the theorems and how they work. She goes through practice problems too. Tests have true/false section about theorems and a practical section where you apply equations. Homework helps you practice, BUT it costs $100.

10/10 professor. Exams are very similar to practice tests. Final is "cumulative" but more than 3/4 is represented of post midterm 2. HW is guaranteed 100%, infinite tries. 6/9 discussions are mandatory for full credit. Study discussions. Watch 3Blue1Brown linear algebra. PLEASE read the textbook and do the problems. Watch out for polynomials!

Honestly, she is an amazing professor. She teaches through examples, which was a much more effective approach (for me). She listens to the topics that students struggle with and prepare questions for the entire class to do together. Her tests reflect on the topics covered in class, and grading is fair.

She is genuinely one of the best teachers you will ever have! She's super kind, genuine, and helps you prepare for tests very well. All you have to do is attend class, do the practice exams, and put time into the homeworks and you will be good. Definitely do the discussion worksheets (will help you a LOT).

She's a very nice and respectable professor with lectures that are SEMI-mandatory (You can miss 6-7) and same with discussions (You can also miss 2-3) and still receive full credit for attendance. Grading wise, very easy on everything BUT midterms and finals as they weigh about 80% of your grade. Stay caught up and this class will be light :P

analysis.name: Amy Kennemore
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is pretty easy and she employs a very flexible attendance system (plus one day of lecture is asynchronous) in addition to flexible turn in dates. The TAs grade way more strictly that what I expected considering how flexible the rest of the curriculum is, but there is options for regrades so it didn't matter too much, just annoying

The class was pretty easy for me. A lot of assigned media, but I lowkey barely read anything and was fine. Tuesday's are asynchronous, and discussion attendance is optional starting after week 5. There is no midterm/ final, just a media project (can be indiv. or group) and there are weekly assignments (2 small write ups and a discussion post)

Professor Kennemore has really flexible policies that are super understanding of students and their time. No exams and final was a group project. Class was a nice light GE and wasn't super time consuming. Class was scheduled for Tues/Thurs, with asynchronous work on Tuesdays, optional attendance, and lots of extra credit opportunities.

prof. kennemore is extremely caring and demonstrates her passion for what she teaches effortlessly.. it made this class very enjoyable! her class can be content/reading heavy at times but she does a great job at making sure material is understandable during lecture

She was a great professor. Almost weekly discussion boards which are not hard at all. You dont necessarily have to read, you can get away with skimming. Weekly portfolios. Attendance and discussion are not mandatory. Super easy and fun class. She is passionate about what she teaches. Looking to take her again for another course!

analysis.name: Amy Non
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I would suggest taking her only if you're heavily into research, specifically on biology and genetics. Most assignments consists of reading, writing, and critiquing research articles. Midterm was multiple choice. In my opinion I think her field is very niche but also very useful to know about, especially with the current political climate today.

She is very intelligent and considerate of her students. No quizzes, but there will be essays, student-led discussions (in groups) through presentations, and lots of dense readings (also some easy ones) weekly. She shows you how to read the dense articles so it's not really big deal. She also offers plenty of extra credit outside of class.

Such a caring person and incredible professor. She does important work at UCSD and is passionate about it. She offers interesting courses with exciting content and is always willing to work with students. I highly recommend taking her courses, especially those who are interested in bio anthropology/ epigeneticsLove her!

The material is very interesting and Non promoted open discussion within class. There were no exams but discussion boards and papers. Many extra credit opportunities were given. I would say there was not a clear prompt for the papers so you could have trouble with what to write and what not to write. However, overall easy DEI class!

analysis.name: Amanda Solomon
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: It is the worst class I've ever taken! This woman is not respected at all.
The lecture is sooooo boring. I cannot force myself not to sleep. While it is mandatory, non sense! I don't understand her logic.

I LOVE DR. SOLOMON! I took her for DOC 2 and 3 and do not regret it. She made lectures enjoyable and she was like a mom. Before lecture started, she would turn on some music and then would start the class. She is very knowledgeable and I'm grateful that I had the opportunity to take DOC with her!

Rated on her teaching style and attitudes overall against other professors because there's only 3 options for DOC. She goes over all relevant content very well, lectures are a little on the boring side, can be a little demeaning and passive aggressive. About as professional as a Karen can be. Overall good for getting an A in DOC.

She is very passionate about what she teaches, and you can tell she cares. The course is very passable if you put the effort to try, tho there's a lot of reading. Attendance is mandatory for both lectures & discussions, but u get some free skips. She's great, just don't be late (you'll be locked out after 5 min.) & do not whip out any electronics.

analysis.name: Amy Fox
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor is nice + topics were interesting but I didn't feel the prof conveyed ideas clearly. HW readings were long + confusing. Quizzes are take-home + graded on participation. Exams were difficult. No explicit grading rubric (esp for saqs). Grades are hidden the whole quarter. Tested on guest lectures that was confusing + outside scope of course

Lectures were not mandatory. Discussions were only mandatory Week 6 and beyond. Two simple projects. Weekly readings were long... but you can get away with not reading them if you attend lectures. Professor is very kind and considerate :) Class structure was definitely chaotic at times given Fox's freshness as an instructor. Easy midterm and final!

Very sweet prof, seems like she truly cares and takes student feedback. Lectures and readings get a bit repetitive but ngl I did no readings, went to a few lectures and it was fine, discussions are only sometimes mandatory +many ways to make up points +extra credit. Group projects were a little annoying. If you read the syllabus you'll do fine!

i honestly liked her lectures, and as long as you attended and read the (really long) weekly readings, then it wasn't hard to get a good grade. the exams are worded kinda specifically so the first one was hard to me but the final exam was reasonable. just go to lecture and pay attention. every quiz was designed to help u and was for completion only

She was inconsistent with her lectures and what was applied on test. She lack a structure of her course, and was often more confusing then informative. Lacks attention and focus which causes unnecessary strain as student, she also lacks being able to decipher when a student is wrong or right, she cant fully answer a question furthering confusion.

analysis.name: Amarnath Gupta
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: In 4 years of (very difficult) Math and CS coursework at UCSD, this guy is the worst prof I've ever had. Constantly condescending to students in every lecture, exams are ridiculously unachievable within the time constraint and cover things NEVER mentioned in lecture or homework. Zero practice problems or guidelines for exam content. AVOID!

his class is unbelievably unorganized. he's making up the structure as he goes, which in turn, leads to a mess.

homeworks were given extensions which was nice, but what was on the homework doesn't reflect on the exams. difficult relational algebra stuff covered in class was not on the exams.

everything is chaotic. don't take

awful af. do not take. wants very specific things in his assigned project assignments but when you try to ask questions about what he wants, he says "you are asking for answers now" if the project is not as open-ended as you claim it to be, then give us specific directions like bffr
oh my god this was the worst experience that I could ever have in UCSD.................................like PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF for real

This is the worst professor I have ever met at UCSD. His class actually teaches nothing and he constantly changed his requirements to students. Very chaotic unstructured class content and homework. Sometimes he can't even remember what he said as homework requirement. This is my first time to give a bad thumb on a professor. DONT TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

analysis.name: Amy Pasquinelli
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: No solutions provided for problem sets, threatened students w "video evidence" of students cheating with clickers, hinted that it's probably in our best interest NOT to ask for a regrade since she regrades entire exam and you'll probably LOSE points, impossible exams. Final destroyed me. Oh, and no curve. I've never taken a more unreasonable class.

When most of her class is failing and her excitement after her students studied for days straight is "There were more right answers than wrong answers" because she's overall happy with a C- average. Then comes the final, which was out of box, barely having anything to do with a majority of the lecture content. You sit there, destroyed and ask why

Class was 40% midterm and 60% final.  Midterm was reasonable and her lectures prepared me for it.  Final was incredibly conceptual and experiment-based, which I was not prepared for at all.  iCLICKER questions and assignments for the second half of the quarter did not match the type of questions she had asked in the final.  Would not recommend.

She needs to SLOW DOWN AND TAKE A BREATH. It can be frustrating how she zips through a ton of material without ever  pausing on a subject and elaborating. Just feels like shes throwing a ton of information at you at once, and you try to do your best to take all of it in.

40% midterm. 60% final. 5% extra credit added to your grade for attendance. Up to 1% EC on top of that for CAPES if your whole class does them. Midterm was reflective of the practice midterm and assignments but the final was ridiculously difficult and didn't really match up with the assignments (post midterm)/practice final. Wouldn't recommend.

analysis.name: Alina Schimpf
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Insanely organized lectures slides and discussions, every lecture seems to be planned down the minute. Inorganic chemistry as a subject is not easy but Dr. Schimpf does her best to simplify tough concepts. Her slides are the most organized I've seen and you can understand most concepts covered in class just by reviewing the slide. My goat.

I really enjoyed Prof Schimpf's class! She is very approachable and will happily answer any questions during lecture and in office hours. The exams feel fair, and she is very clear about what will be tested. The homework and practice exam problems are pretty good preparation for tests, and she goes through practice problems in lecture.

Professor Schimpf gives good lectures with helpful explanations and lots of examples. The older reviews aren't, in my opinion, a good representation of her teaching now because I found that she was very organized, knowledgeable, and answered questions in a helpful and encouraging way.

Worst teacher I've ever had. Uses another Prof's slides and I swear she reads them for the first time when she reads them out loud in her first lecture. Literally knows nothing about the material. Students ask basic questions during lectures that she can't answer. She does not know the material. Not enough space to rant abt more

Very fast when lecturing. The pace and questions she lectured assumed the topics were immediately understood after being taught. Knowledge checks asked questions not always covered in lecture and were worth a lot grading wise. 

There was no curve on the final or final grading scale. 
2.37 class GPA for my section

analysis.name: Alex Chaim
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Chaim's lectures were really helpful and he made it easy to understand the content. The exams also had buffer questions which made it easier to get an A even if you didn't know every little detail. The class is memorization heavy in general, but Chaim and the IA's made it easier :)
Professor is clear about what will be tested. Participation points can be gained in discussion section. All tests have buffer questions, which makes the exam and studying less stressful.
One of the most compassionate professors I've had at UCSD. He genuinely wants to see you succeed and will do what he can to support you when things get tough.10/10 would take again

Very clear lecturer, explains what parts of mechanisms you need to know, and problem sets are a very clear reflection of the exams. Class is entirely memorization but exams have buffer questions so getting answers wrong can still get you an A. 10% of grade was participation in class or through video recordings, but pretty easy to earn. A nice prof!

The class was distributed between 2 midterms, a final, and 10 part points. 
It was his first time teaching the course and I felt he did amazing, was clear during lectures, often ended early (huge plus)clear study guide, midterms were reflective of the material taught. 
The final was a little tougher, but if you do the study guides you will be fine

analysis.name: Amitabha Sinha
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Difficult class and often no one raised their hand to ask questions. Professor sometimes would assume we already knew things or didn't explain too well in class, but he answered everything during office hours. He's definitely very knowledgeable about quantum chemistry and very articulate. You will likely spend a lot of time on this class.

The only bad thing about this class was the TA, Zhiyuan Yin. The professor, though, was really nice. Sometimes he has a hard time grasping what students questions are about the content, but he does a good job explaining topics. My advice is to NOT study the proofs he does in class, just focus on their implications. Study hard for the quizzes.

HW 10%, Midterm 40%, Final 50%. A lot of HW and tough grading for 10%, and mostly Diff Eq. Read chapters and you will see it's the same as lectures, but lectures are clear and helpful; show up to lectures and sessions, and ask questions! Check exams for re-grade: Graders make a lot of mistakes, and short re-grade period... it messed up my grade!

When I first started the class, I thought he was going to be an unhelpful jerk. But he is actually very kind and willing to help, so long as you show him that you are trying. His lectures are extremely clear. At first you will think you will not have to go to class, but GO! Midterm directly reflected class. Offers multiple review sessions too.

I did not like this class. I've taken related courses and have interest and experience with spectroscopy (I wanted to learn more). This class was an advanced mathematics course with little insight on concepts or techniques. It doesn't seem useful, and I was disappointed; also, the HW seemed ridiculous and it was not interesting. Buy the book!

analysis.name: Alexis Komor
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Komor is a humorous and knowledgeable instructor. She provides detailed lecture notes and problem sets that represent the exam materials. Recommend her class.

Lectures had a lot of information and she goes super fast so it's easy to fall behind. The midterms were 25 questions in 45 minutes, so it was easy to make silly mistakes going so fast through it. Do all the book problems and practice a lot for the midterms. She was alright at explaining concepts, chemistry can just be hard to understand in general

Prof Komor is a new but excellent instructor. She's fairly young so she can connect well with her students, especially with her sense of humor. Her lectures include lots of examples to help reinforce and practice concepts.

Although one feels like she cares for her students, she doesn't do the best job of teaching the material. Lots of practice examples but runs through bad. Her tests are not difficult, but the time constraint sucks because she gives you 25 questions in 50 minutes. Multiple choice Conceptual and problem based, totally based on her lecture slides.

Had her for CHEM 114A, and she explains concepts really well. The class is relatively easy, and it is a flipped classroom. Exams make up a huge portion of your grade, but the practice problems she gives are a good reflection of the actual exam. However, there weren't really as many application problems.

analysis.name: Alexandra Jazz Dickinson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: SO AMAZING! Hated ochem but loved bibc bc of her(no memorizing mechanisms). She's so real and tells u what will/won't be on 3 exams + 1 final. Lectures can be boring but useful for exam prep. Problem set graded on effort, and it helps to go to discussion for clarity. Gave EC for SETs even tho we didnt reach threshold #goat (+20pt EC asgmt week6)

best biochem prof. Lectures are engaging, exams are memorization-based but she clearly outlines what you need to know, they are exactly like the practice material, and there are many extra credit opportunities. Homework is graded on completion, and discussion is not mandatory. she is very sweet and this was the easy A if u put in the effort

One of the best professors I've had at UCSD so far. Very caring about her students, passionate about what she teaches, and very clear about what material will get tested on the exam. Metabolic biochemistry is a hard topic to grasp, but Jazz makes the topic significantly easier and less stressful to understand.

She is a really kind and straightforward professor. Her lectures match the exam questions and there is extra credit at the end of each exam. A lot of memorizing like Aminos and enzymes and such but she makes the class really interesting and enjoyable tbh. Also a 20pt ec assignment that was like week 6.

BEST PROFESSOR at UCSD! This class should be your number priority on that schedule of yours. Exam 2 averaged at 90%, she's pretty hip and teaches really well. I was intimidated by biochem but ended up being the most interesting and easiest class because of the way she teaches.

analysis.name: Alex Snoeren
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: really good lectures, assignments are tough but extremely educational. the midterm was too easy so he ended up turning the final's difficulty upwards, which ended up being too much. however, the curve is generous enough that most people could get a decent grade

Pretty difficult class especially the 3 PAs and the final exam but with a fair curve. 

His lectures were amazing though, might be one of the best at UCSD (outside of Sanjoy Dasgupta). I'm going to audit his CSE 223B course just to attend his lectures.

One of the best classes I have had at UCSD! The lectures are joyful, an experience in their own right. Professor Snoeren wonderfully highlights the key systems concepts in the papers, enabling a deep understanding of the topic. The class requires a lot of effort, but its definitely worth it. You come out of this class as a different person.

A great professor whose passion for the subject really comes through in his lectures. Projects and exams are tough so you really have to put in the work, but it is extremely rewarding when you come out the other side.

4 projects due over the quarter, 2 big ones and 2 small ones. You code a router packaging TCP packets, congestion control and then router topology forwarding IP and ICMP packets. 2 midterms and 1 final. class is taught an engaging way tho there's a lot of content covered. have to make sure you don't fall off

analysis.name: Guillermo Algaze
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 75 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Your grade COMPLETELY depends on your TA. His lectures are very helpful for his final essay, so you should listen to the podcasts if you do not want to attend class. In Fall 2015, our grades were based off of two essays only (I don't know if the 15% participation was included . . .probably not). If you have the TA Jena then I wish you luck. . .

Prof. Algaze is a super nice guy and is very knowledgeable of the material. Your grade is dependent on the weekly readings (usually 3 or 4 articles a week, but you don't “have to” read them all). Homework is annotating one article of your choosing. In discussion, you write a paragraph based on the common themes of the readings. Easiest A ever!

The professor is sweet and knowledgable but make sure to not have Manoj as your TA, he is a tough grader. If you don't want to spend all your time engulfed in the content of this course, I'd pass and take a dif CAT 1!

Attendance required like any other CAT courses. I'd say we had less work compared to other profs. One-page paragraph/essay per week done during discussion. Prompts are already on the syllabus at the beginning of the quarter, so just read some articles and prepare some evidence for that week's writing. Grades solely depend on TA.

Prof. Algaze is really nice and passionate about the lecture material. Attendance was mandatory for lecture and section, but you could miss up to 4 with no effect on your grade. The 2 weekly assignments were super easy. Your grade depends mostly on your TA and I was blessed with a very generous one (Cristina). Easy A if you know how to write.

analysis.name: Alicia Munoz Sanchez
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Only 2 midterms and final research report. Content/midterm questions were based on daily readings, so get ready to read. Professor genuinely cares about her students, always answers her emails, and is really sweet. Linguistics background is very useful, not impossible without it tho!

These classes  were extremely stressful. Your put into classes with people of all different levels so advanced people guide the class and true beginners are left behind, humiliated and given poor grades for not raising your hand. Very discouraging way to try and learn. Also dependent on TA entirely. You don't get a professor.  Avoid if you can.

Professor Munoz is a very kind professor. She's very caring and is always there to hear what you need to say. Her work is very easy and most is done with groups. It's a very interesting course that I would recommend taking!

Taking this class as an Education Minor. Tbh, being a linguistic major will make this class 10x easier, but any non-linguistics majors will have to do extra work trying to understand linguistic concepts. She gives complicated research articles, but she always explains them in lecture slides so reading isn't impossible. Thought-provoking concepts.
Love the Professor! So Caring and a sweetheart! Fun and Super Interesting Linguistics class!

analysis.name: Aobo Li
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Love bro, would take his class again. Although he read straight from the slides, it helped me make sense of the concepts thru hearing him say it aloud. Perfect lecture speed. Requires mildly solid background in basic math. Bare minimum is taking notes and understanding clicker questions. Study hard and you'll definitely succeed :3

He was really caring and passionate about this class. His grading scale is very forgiving and geared towards students. Two midterms, all multiple choice, with a 12/15 being 100%. Final is two parts and can replace midterm grades if higher. Lectures and slides are excellent and convey material well. Hope he offers 1C, would love to take him again!

Makes physics actually understandable and his exam questions are lifted straight from iClicker and online homework. Just keep track of all the equations thrown at you and make sure you know how to do iClickers and you'll get an A. Super funny lecture slides also, he tries to make it fun.

Professor Li is amazing. His grading system is super fair and actually gives you a bit of wiggle room. He does do iClicker, but you're allowed to miss 5 classes. I would still encourage you to attend as much as possible because a good chunk of midterm/final content is taken from the lecture slides (he posts them as well) and from the homework.

Professor Li is amazing! He has a very forgiving grading policy (two midterms, final is two parts and can replace either midterm if you are unhappy with your score). His tests were very representative of the hw and in class questions, and his lectures are engaging! You can tell he has a genuine love for physics and wants his students to learn!!!

analysis.name: Anthony Aportela
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If need the grade, absolutely take prof tony. Was going to be a hater but the quizzes/final are so ridiculously easy (I'm talking EC on literally everything). Yes, very conceptual but this means you can skip grinding problems and just actually understand the content. That being said don't expect to learn in lecture, just use YT vids/Kudu sometimes.

he was really nice and chill but all comm was through discord and his lectures were just tangents and derivations. it got to the point that i gave up on going to lectures even tho they were mandatory and just relied on openstax to teach me. quiz avg was around 60-75% and only 60% iclicker points meant full points tho and final was easy

Took during SS2 and dropped because the class was very disorganized. Quiz averages were ~35% and how he taught physics symbols instead of numbers just didn't make sense for me. Prof Tony is very caring, but he is soft spoken + goes on tangents, so it's easy to fall asleep in lectures (mandatory)... Prepare for a lot of self learning and good luck!

New to teaching, so you will have to do more work. No practice quizzes, but a practice final & good curve. Treat office hours like another lecture. The class wasn't really organized, and the subject is difficult, but he is passionate & made me appreciate & like physics more. Take him if you can put in lots of work & manage a less organized course.

Prof Tony cares about his students and you can tell he wants to help where he can, but his lectures were very hard to follow. IMO, the first couple quizzes were not representative of what we learned in class, and HW did not prepare us. The class was hard because of the disorganized lectures, limited examples in class, but Prof is kind.

analysis.name: April Sutton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Super easy imo. Final was online/not lockdown. Lectures were not mandatory. Mandatory discussions but super chill. There were only 4 HWs, a midterm that I felt was very fair, and a final. Lots of readings but the content is all pretty simple. Sutton is super nice, and gives extra credit just for going to lectures. Highly recommend.

Honestly I thought I was cooked in this class. I got a C on the midterm, and was bogged down by the readings, but class was heavily curved and catered towards students success. The final was significantly easier, open note. 4 assignments to becompleted throughout quarter, that are practical and straightforward.

4 HW assignments, ea/very simple and she said herself she did not give out lower than (I think) a B on each one. Lots of extra credit in lecture and even on the midterm and final (which were a mix of MC, short answer). Her lectures were amazing and thorough, could easily replace the textbook. Section is mandatory, lecture isn't. I loved her class!

Prof Sutton is so sweet and it's really easy to succeed in class. Four hw assignments, a midterm and final made up of multiple choice and short answer questions. Content isn't too difficult either  not much stats, mostly just memorization of terms that'll be useful in life if you plan on doing research. She also gives easy extra credit sometimes.

I think the class is very interesting and informative, Prof is very nice and wants students to succeed. I feel like I learned a lot of was engaged with the material. In this class, you work with a group for some assignments and she gives class time to do so. A fair amount of reading but nothing that isn't manageable.

analysis.name: April Linton
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: By far one of the greatest professors I have ever had. She is really interesting and very helpful. The work load is doable and isnt too difficult. Take her class! You won't regret it.

I took SOCI87 as a freshman seminar class (worth 1 unit) just because it was the only one that fit into my schedule. I had no interest in consumerism whatsoever (didn't care about sweatshops) but her genuine concern for the society and environment rubs off and I ended up learning alot. She handmade a pumpkin cake for us at the last day of class =]

Amazing professor. In fact, best prof I have had at UCSD by far (took 3 classes). She is extremely clear and organized, and makes the topic even more interesting than it already is. The exams are very fair. In class midterm and final take home essay. Prof Linton is also very helpful outside of class. I highly recommend her and all of her classes.

Prof. Linton is a great professor, definitely recommended. This class was harder than I thought due to the amount of demographic data, but interesting. Midterm/Final are both M/C, TF, Short Answer. Some in class writes and either an 8 pg literature review paper or a 3 pg service learning paper/comm. service project. Overall, I enjoyed the class.

Very helpful and sweet.  I realy enjoyed going to her class.  Her lectures are available on powerpoint, but it is more beneficial to go to class.  Her midterm and final are very easy if you keep up with the reading and attend lecture.  There is a lot of reading, so plan accordingly.  She is very fair though.  She is always available to help.

analysis.name: Ashley Juavinett
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I really liked Dr J. She's kind, did well at at simplifying coding and showing us practical uses in bio, and gave us a fun final group project where we really had creative reign. Weekly homeworks, a few quizzes (no midterms), and the TA's were very helpful. I didn't try nearly as much as I should've, think it wouldn't be hard to get an A in here!
Difficult organized class. You learn very little, but put in so much work and time. Very little benefit. Too much unnecessary work and very picky grading.
OH MY GOD!!! NO!!! PLEASE STAY!!! DONT TAKE THIS!!!

Loved this class and this prof! BIPN 145 is my favorite class i've taken at ucsd so far and that's thanks to Dr.J.!! she makes lab interesting and lively, and she's always there if her students need help! Lab reports, midterms and final project were reasonable and fair imo, and Dr. J makes it very clear what she expects from you. 10/10 recommend

Professor Juavinett is amazing! She handled the pandemic so well and is super understanding. The class is lab report heavy but they aren't terrible, try and you'll get at least a B. Labs are done in groups and we do a group grant proposal at the end. I recommend this class! Love the class but hate working in groups so much.

analysis.name: Robert Asaro
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The devil himself. Often talks about evil demons. Makes everyone buy a book that he wont mention after the first class (He wrote it and will make you buy it from a sketchy website). Begins every lecture with a rant about how he is disappointed in attendance. Also does not believe in holidays or getting sick. Cool hat though. Nice sweater vests too.

I had said this before but Robert takes the cake for the worst Professor I've had. He's too old to be teaching anymore, and his lectures can hardly count as "teaching" anyway. His OH are just as bad. All the reviews about him are true. He is a sour mean old man who interrupts you and will not even let you speak if he has his mind made up about you.

Absolutely the worst prof in UCSD, expect everyone to attend his confusing lectures & OHs even tho its optional. Easily get mad over lil thing like attendance & being rude to students for no reason, also he used his lectures to talk about his life stories. Weekly hw, 1 midterm & final. The exams are similar to hw and the same every year. Avoid him

Absolutely one of the worst prof in UCSD, expect u to attend lectures & OHs even tho its not mandatory. Exams are similar to hw and the same every year. Easily get mad over lil thing like attendance or being rude to students for no reason & he used lectures to talk about his life stories. Weekly hw, 1 midterm & final. Avoid him at all costs!
Terrible Professor. Lucky he is retiring soon

analysis.name: Alexander Stewart
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 115 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are basically the readings. This was his first year teaching MMW but he was previously a TA. Grading is pretty weird. People only come for the clicker questions that count. He gives a study guide but his essay questions are pretty ridiculous, some were hypothetical and some asked for 5 sources. Would not recommend for MMW professor

He was my professor for MMW 12 last Winter quarter and thought he was good professor overall as he knows the materials very well. However, I had him as a TA for MMW 14 in Summer Session 1 and he graded writings VERY DIFFICULT. I would skip him as a TA if possible. Good luck to anyone having him as a TA as he required more things than the professor.

I took his MMW 122 class during summer session and I know since it's summer it is more condensed but Jesus he assigned so many articles to read that was not humanly possible. Every lecture you are suppose to ready about 8-12 articles which range in number of pages from 1-30 His lectures are rather boring and monotone although he seems passionate.

The class itself was easy. There was did-you-do-the-readings style assignments, essays, and two exams. The exams were tough because of limited time. The grading was extremely lax and I'd consider this class fairly straightforward. However, lectures did not align with class content/learning objectives. Often made questionable comments.

Class has a moderate amount of busy work but solidly easy. Pay attention to lecture and skim/briefly read the readings and you virtually don't have to study for exams. The exam averages are 90-95% so are the paper averages. He grades pretty lax just give it your all and don't use AI you will do well in this class. He's a super kind and great prof.

analysis.name: Asif Shakeel
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: By far the worst professor I have ever had. Thick accent, ungodly amount of work, mumbles for half the class, goes on tangents when students asks a question then never ends up answering it, speed reads through the slides, messes up setup of the equations, and will ask us to forget what he just said cause it was all wrong. Unacceptable UCSD!!!

He's clueless! We'll get finish an example and he'll say "oh nevermind that was all wrong." His handwriting is IMPOSSIBLE to read and he never clarifies what he is writing even if students ask. He mumbles to himself and sounds like he is trying to learn the material as he is teaching us. I had to teach myself everything... never take his class.

I don't know where to start. This professor seems to be reading the slides for the first time as he's trying to lecture. Notes are incoherent at best. Be prepared, if you ask a question he will likely forget it within 20 seconds of talking himself into a hole. Don't take unless you want to teach yourself everything.

The final was by far the worst final I have ever taken and he had the AUDACITY to not curve it or the class whatsoever. Study maybe two weeks ahead of time for this class if you want anything above a C. I tried hard on all the homeworks and labs. The homeworks are easy but the labs are graded harshly so I  go to office hours to get them checked.

I don't think he has any idea as to what he is actually lecturing his students. His lectures are impossible to follow synchronously. His handwriting is not just reminiscent of Egyptian hieroglyphics; it is the hieroglyphics. The best thing from his class is you learn how to teach yourself the subject. Save yourself and take 20C with Ko Woon or Yin.

analysis.name: Ashley Smith
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: BEST. CAT CLASS. EVER. Hands down. No essays in the traditional sense. Class is based on videos; main project is to make a short film (3-7 mins, though my group went over to 9min) with group which was very fun. Topic of vid was about design fiction of world 100yrs from now. Only essays are just reflection paper on the video. Highly recommend!

Her lectures were all over the place and had no relevance to any assignments that we were doing  for that class. We basically just watch videos that she skips through so we cannot even understand what is going on at all. Also she acts like her class should be everyone's first priority when we all have other, more important classes.
Really did not like her class. It was a lot of work for a writing class and made no sense to me. Her lectures were not engaging and were all over the place. Really glad to finally be done with her

She's nice but doesn't always explain things in a clear way.  She is an artist so maybe that is why she talks using words that are vague or dont really mean anything. But she was good at getting students to participate in conversations during lecture.  Her lectures don't always seem to really have a point though.
Pros: extra credits, interesting topic, enthusiastic, one paper only Cons: pop attendance

analysis.name: Brittany Asaro
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Asaro is amazing! She goes over everything as many times as you ask in order for the you to understand the material. Her tests and quizzes are very fair and overall was a very fun class that I looked forward to. It is a language class so you will need to memorize vocab and conjugations, but if you keep on top of it you'll be fine!

Dr. Asaro is a very intellectual and caring professor. She is available outside of class and wants to help you learn. She has a lot of extra credit opportunities which is really nice! Homework, 2 quizzes, 2 tests, 2 papers and 2 presentations. Pretty clear and solid class. Loved it!
She really cares about students. You do a lot of reading in this class, but not an insane amount. 2 5pg essays, 2 quizzes, 2 projects and final make up your grade. Would def recommend.
Appreciate taking her course. She genuinely works to help her students do well in the course. There's a lot of reading and class discussion is mandatory so I suggest reading.
very helpful, wants you to do well. Recommend taking

analysis.name: Aram Grigoryan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: dry lecturer but very passionate and clear. teaches very well, exams are fair and he prepares you well based w/ practice material. study hard for exams and you'll do well in the class, prob the best econ prof  here. literally a saint compared to the other 100b profs. no curve for an a though, material after exam 2 is the most difficult so study up

He is such a W professor. He gives out practice exams that are very similar to the actual exams. He actually cares about you and wants you to succeed instead of trying to trick you on the exams. Very straight forward questions just like the practice or the examples he did in class. Everything is recorded no attendence for lecture or discussion.

The structure of his class is very clear: 4 homework assignments, 2 lowest are dropped, and the midterms and final study guides you are given are basically what is on the exams (same type of questions, different examples obviously). Make sure to attend lectures and discussions or watch them to understand the material.
Compared to the professor in other class, he's practically an angel. I hope he teaches 100B this fall.
Lecture notes are very clearly written. Aram tells you exactly what's on exams, and as long as you understand how to do the practice exams you will do well.

analysis.name: Jessica Arlett
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is genuinely the worst professor I've had in my three years at UCSD. She does care for the subject but does not care if the students succeed. Our quiz averages are around 60% yet she refuses to do anything about it. Our class averages are so bad but she refuses to acknowledge that is a result of her own teaching.

Although she is a good person, she is NOT a good professor. This class gave me more anxiety than any other class I have taken in my life. So much unnecessary work that amounted nothing to my understanding of the concepts. Tests were poorly made and had many errors that confused me and led loss of points.

The class itself is flawed IMO, not much to do with the prof. Grades weigh heavily on prelab quizzes and reports. Quizzes are 5 Qs but they try to trick you. Reports are VERY repetitive and tedious, and feedback for me was minimal. However, the professors are accessible through piazza and quite accommodating. Still my least favorite class so far.

Professor Arlett really does care about students' success in her class. She gives opportunities for EC (up to 4.5% grade boost for my class). Some of the EC came from answering peers' questions on piazza which she's very active on as well so it's easy to get questions answered. The content is hard but the amount of work and its difficulty is fair.

my fav class, and i learned a lot abt stats. yeah labs take ~10 hours, but theres 3 reports THE WHOLE QUARTER. if you cant manage your time, thats on YOU. i got a 95 having lost 25% on my late 1st lab because she halved the lowest grade's weight—she values improvement. TAs offer ~18 hours OH during lab report weeks; if you want an A, youll get one

analysis.name: John Arroyo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Arroyo is a really inspiring professor. I am not even a USP student but his lectures still were interesting. He cares about teaching and is super knowledgeable. Just be prepared for the group projects since they are a huge part of your grade!
If you want learn something and enjoy your class he is great, definitely take him
One of best professor , who will teach you but also don't pressurize , I would say easy class
He is very inspiring. would recommend.
I love John. Such a caring professor. If you are taking his class go to his office hour and talk to him. It is very therapeutic.

analysis.name: Siavash Arabbaygi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Homework and Labs were not required, but heavily recommended. Quizzes were challenging, with averages hovering like 40-50 percent. The ARM coding language and environment is specific to the class but straight up didn't work on my computer with no real alternatives found online, so tough luck if it doesn't work on yours. The curve was very generous.

class is content heavy. Prof does a good job explaining the concepts and lectures are useful. grade is based solely on quizzes, final, project (all of which are hard) so if you are bad at test prep or takings tests in generally you will probably suffer. otherwise you'll appreciate not having hw, unless you actually do the labs, which are optional.

The workload isn't very crazy for me (6-8 hours), but the lecture and pre-lecture recording is boring and easy to get distracted. Some quizzes and the final are tough, and the study/example problem sets aren't very sufficient to test your knowledge thoroughly. No homework is graded so only quiz, final, and a project contribute to the final score.

Get ready to spend a lot of time on this course. You have to watch around 40 min of pre-lecture before each lecture. Quiz are open notes while online, but not for final. Project is in pairs and if your partner disappeared, you may suffer. This course is hard and the online nature makes it harder. Be prepared to choose this course and spend time.

Good professor, explains concepts well. It is a flipped classroom, where we watch pre-lecture videos to learn the concepts, and then during the lectures, the professor shows examples. There is a lot of work for this class, at least 20 hours per week.

analysis.name: Kristin Arcidiacono
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great instructor! Very professional and passionate about dancing, and also have great personality and teaching method.

The class has a variety of tap styles to experiment with. Your experience doesn't matter because she caters to all levels. Her grading is generous too because it's based on attendance, 2 performances of a routine we learned in class and a paper. I would recommend this class to anyone who wants to raise their GPA by having fun dancing.

Ive taken her several times, so hopefully that tells shes a great teacher. I didnt grow up dancing, but she really devotes her time to help anyone. Shes so patient too! She really wants her students to achieve in her class. However, sometimes she does cater a lot more to the advanced students of the class. 10/10

Kristin is an amazing dance teacher. As a person with a lot of dance background, I can say she is one of the best teachers I have had. Her stretch routines, technique sequences, across the floor exercises, and dance choreography are perfect for growing as a dancer. She is helpful and encouraging.

A great professor who genuinely likes ballet and cares about her students! She takes the time to learn about everyone, and gives feedback tailored to what you need. I've never done ballet before, but she is very easy on beginners. Enjoyable class!

analysis.name: Kam Arnold
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Arnold is def knowledgeable about physics however he is unsuccessful in passing on that knowledge... Lectures are unclear and not helpful for the homework and quizzes. If you actually want to learn from someone you are presumably paying, this is not your prof. If you're all for self-teaching, though, go for it. Averages were veryyy low.
