I regret taking this professor, especially after hearing that friends in MCWP 50 with other instructors are earning A's while I am not because of how rigorous his grading is. Many people say MCWP is difficult, but it doesn't seem that way unless you take a professor like Jason Bartulis.

Dismissive and deflective of all punitive responsibility to the MCWP department. Plays the "good cop" when exacting punishment, acting like his actions were completely out of his own hands– no accountability. Came off as condescending on the first day, which unfortunately never changed. Do not take if you do not absolutely have to.

Couldn't tell if he was making fun of me or not, but always mispronounced my name. Extremely difficult grading criteria. Better off taking another professor as it'd be easier to get an A with anyone else other than Jason Bartulis.

analysis.name: Francesca Balboni
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Weekly workload depend heavily on the articles and essay she gave, for now experiencing like hundred page of reading every week. Minimum time to complete her weekly assignment around 12 hours, attendance taken in iCloud which located your location through GPS.

Nice woman, good intentioned, but holy moly she literally assigns so much reading. In week 8 and it's literally been like this the whole quarter. Really easy assignments but like... not if you didn't do the readings which are like 60 pages every two days. Just too much work, not trying to be lazy but yea. Wouldn't recommend.

I'm taking VIS85A right now, and her lectures are really boring, with a lot of tedious stuff. She assigns a lot of homework, and her attitude toward students when judging their work is disrespectful. Do not take her class. There is a reason why her class is the only one with extra slots among all other GEs.

Media and art isn't for everyone, however, if you are someone interested in this field, the course was interesting and provided historic and relevant context to film, media, video, art, etc. Lectures can get boring, DIs can be interesting, NO Midterm, Final is a straightforward project, discussion boards do matter + readings, and weekly worksheets.

Readings can be a lot, but you can get away with skimming them just enough to answer the canvas discussions and weekly worksheets. There is no midterm or final exam, with only a final project which isn't that hard and are given ample amount of time to do. Not a terrible class if you don't want to stress about an additional midterm or final.

analysis.name: Saharnaz Baghdadchi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If there was an option to pick "Sweetheart", that would be number one choice. Sahar really cares about her students and tries to do her best to let the students succeed. She truly is a GEM and I'm trying to take every single class she teaches at UCSD. As long as you care for her class, you WILL pass and probably with a good grade too.

On everything, I showed up maybe 5 times early in the quarter and skipped the rest, yet still did decent on the final and rode the curve to a B. She even noticed I didn't come to class and questioned me, but I just couldn't sync with her style. She is so sweet and caring. Didn't take ECE 65 and still got it done. Y'all can do it.

Sahra really cares about her students. ECE 65 is hard in general, but she gives lots of extra credit opportunities. She encourages you to go to her office hour. I would definitely take her classes again.

Great lecturer, she really cares about her students and sends out tons of material to give mid-quarter feedback. However, she does let the class average go pretty low before deciding the cutoffs, so the final was quite scary. Regardless, she's one of the best professors in the Electrical Engineering department. Would definitely take again.
Great lectures, clear lab instructions, tests are similar to practice exams. You should expect an A if you work through all the practice exams. One of the best professor I met so far.

analysis.name: Steve Barrera
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 117 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: BEST PROFESSOR AT UCSD. Literally, I've had Prof. Barrera for 3 classes, and he is such a great lecturer! He makes his lectures very clear and easy to understand. I never bought a textbook for his classes (COGS 1, 101A and 101B). and I easily got an A. He also offers EASY extra credit (SONA and section attendence). I would DEFINITELY recommend him!
He's great. This course has guest speakers who put me to sleep, but I love Barrera. Plus he looks like Jason Bateman, really he does.

Best Cognitive Science teacher! Hands down! Very thorough with his lecture and at times may be a lot to handle. This may be due to the nature of the course though. But just go over the study guide and you'll be golden! Has weekly quizzes but you get three attempts. Oh and don't need to buy the book for any of his classes!

Taken fall 2025, this time tests were in person and not on canvas. Memorization heavy because tests aren't open-note, but can get difficult when taking other classes that require you to memorize. Fun professor and genuinely care about his class, I feel like I just have test anxiety no matter how much I study.

Prof. Barrera is very passionate and interacts with students well. His lectures are straightforward and he uses detailed power points (but you still have to attend lectures to get participation credit). His online quizzes are SUPER easy (you get 3 tries and the entire weekend), as well as the exams. Don't need to read the book; lectures cover all.

analysis.name: Bennett Chow
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 85 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures: Often very unorganized, although informative if able to follow along. HW: (20%) Followed mainly from book, and some from lectures. Midterm: (30%) Probs followed HW mainly, some lecture. Final: (50%) Only 1/4 probs followed HW/Lecture, 3/4 DID NOT!!! Most probs overly difficult/not covered directly.  DO NOT rec prof for final alone!!!!!!!!
Chow gives pretty clear exam range. Unlike other professors, chow focuses more on proving and understanding concepts. Hes always passionate during class. Great overall!

So by past finals he posted and the midterm, I expected that most of the problems would be similar to the homework and lecture problems with a few of them being extra difficult.  I'm not sure what happened this time around but the final was ridiculously difficult with only a few similar to class problems. Prof did not prepare us for final at all...

Ben Chow isn't a good professor by any means for math 109, he does have practice exams available but those only help so much. In class he often dwelled on very conceptual proofs which he got lost in. The class introduces a new way of thinking mathematically but Chow does a poor job of delivering these important concepts. A nice guy, but stay away.

Chow is completely lost. He began by reading what the professor before him (also 20C) wrote on the board and said something like "you all get this right? If you get this raise your hand"... then, no one would raise their hand because he hadn't even grazed that topic before... "ok perfect" and began to prove some theorem no other class was taught.

analysis.name: Benjamin Cowan
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His lectures were really interactive, and he is a funny guy altogether, which made it more enjoyable. He has daily readings assigned, but they're not too unreasonable. I had to rent out a lot of the books, but I'm sure you can find them online. Participation and attendance are mandatory but I missed a few days and ended up with an A anyway.

Very engaging and funny lecturer, so the mandatory attendance rarely feels like a chore. Participation is 25% of the grade, but I only participated a handful of times and got an A. There are two essays, each 5 pages and pretty simple.

History of Brazil was one of my GE requirements, I loved his class, attendance was mandatory but lectures were always interesting and professor cowan was pretty funny. Grades were based off basically the midterm essay and the final essay. You have tons of time to prepare so I wouldn't worry at all. Definitely take this class if it satisfies credits

2nd class with Cowan and he is so great! Lectures are mandatory and a part of your grade but he is so funny and knowledgeable so they always fly by. He draws a lot on the readings for class lectures and will call on you to give your opinion. Class grade is based on the midterm and final paper. As long as you start early you'll be good!

I loved taking Brazilian history from Cowan!The class is super interesting & the majority of your grade comes from reading the material & discussing in class. As long as you show that you're engaged & participate, you'll do well! Come to class, do the reading & put effort into the term paper. That's the best advice I can give if you want an A!

analysis.name: Becca Rose
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: She would explain things throughoughly which was appreciated as we went over topics of identity, that many may not have had prior knowledge to. Caring but grading scheme was not for me. Feedback had me constantly feeling like I was not doing good enough. Readings, watch parties, free-writes, discussion boards/responses, essays, projects, peer reviews.

I recommend you take a different professor.

Quizzes every other week that lectures and practice quizzes don't really prepare you for. Grades take a long time to come out and the class can be a bit disorganized at times.
pretty bad. all good ratings you see came from when the quizzes and exams were taken online.

Lectures on complex math concepts by just talking about them, rather than walking through concrete examples. Gives a quiz on a mid-term's worth of material every week. analysis.name: Thomas Bewley

unorganized (no class website, no feedback on homework or midterm, no communication on how the grades are determined), inappropriate lecture material (lectures are based on reading his book, or his research papers), good: available at office hours

analysis.name: Elizabeth Jenkins

she was good...i think she is a theorist...easy to understand

analysis.name: Guy Bertrand

analysis.name: Peter Bjorklund

Dr. B is a good prof. I liked being in his class. There is a lot of work, but he was willing to push back assignments if we needed more time. He is good, just not the best professor I've had. You'll do okay in the class if you do the labs and homework assignments.

Prof. B is an absolutely amazing prof!!! HDS 181 is a lot of work (3 papers+weekly hw & readings), but he makes it manageable and easy to handle. Cannot say enough good things about him

analysis.name: Joe Bigham

The worst class I've taken at UCSD. The whole concept, to learn a musical instrument in 10 weeks and then write a paper on the process of music-learning, is flat out stupid. Grading depends solely on the TAs so count your blessings: some of the TAs take pleasure in speaking down to their students and grading harshly for a dumb and pointless class.

analysis.name: Robert Bitmead
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

review_highlights.comment: Homeworks are dreadful to do, especially the matlab sections. Lectures are useless and the professor berates the class for not answering questions he asks during lecture. This is not an easy course and Pro Rob's approch to the matieral can make it hard(er) to understand.  I had hard time understanding the material when I took it, but things became much more clear after I took the related Math courses.  Good understanding of transfer function (and related math material) can make this course easier.

Tedious homework. Beware - he 100% gives out Fs to students who dont make the cutoff (no curving). Make use of ALL the resources he offers.
I honestly think I could wake up with swine flu and my left nut alone could still be a better professor.

He makes students feel horrible about their education. The class is one of the hardest in Engineering. He does not explain anything during lecture. He spends hours on Matlab and he does not even test you on it. Horrible professor.

analysis.name: Jon Bialecki
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great teacher, very passionate and understanding. Great guy, would 100% take his class again and will miss him after I am done with my final.

He's a very caring and kind professor who is passionate in what he teaches. My fav professor at UCSD. His classes are easy if you put in the effort. Graded by discussion posts, a midterm paper, and a final paper. The discussion posts are graded on if you tried hard enough, he'll give you a 10/10. The midterm and finals you need readings. Love him!
GOOD professor! passionate! care about students, detailed and useful readings! you can learn a lot from his seminars! definitely take it again!

He's a passionate teacher who clearly loves to teach the material. You just have to show you made the effort and tried, and he will be generous with the points. Do the readings for the midterm and final.

His class is pretty similar to any other anthropology class where you just have to read and provide analysis to the readings. Grade determined by 3 papers. If you attend class, he will offer you the "answer" to the rubrics or at least provide you with different approaches you can take to analyze the readings and formulate your argument.

analysis.name: Scott Biering
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload

TAKE HIM

He is amazing, clear on what is expected on the exams, 4 midterms, lowest is dropped. attendance is extra credit. He makes sure you understand the material and he goes over everything that will be on the final. Cheat sheet front and back. I was a little behind on my lectures for the first midterm so I didn't do as well. take him if you can.

Such an iconic professor! He always listened to students' feedback to improve his teaching. Sometimes rushed topics, but overall did amazing at lecturing! Very forgiving course grading systems. Created such a warm class environment and even his TA's were amazing. Exams were pretty representative. Great upper div introduction. Take him if you can!

Probably the best genetics professor at UCSD. He's new and this was his first quarter and compared to the stories my friends have told me about genetics as a subject and overall taking it at UCSD I was expecting torture, but with him he made it fun and understandable and fair! All his exams are extremely fair with cheat sheets and extra credit(15+)

Dr. Scott is kind, silly, inspiring & passionate abt his field. He cares abt his students and does his best to ensure everybody understands the material and he wants everybody to get an A or a B+. He teaches the difficult subject well and grades on a point system. Attendance not mandatory but worth extra credit and lecture heavy. He's cool/chill af

analysis.name: Ethan Bier

no podcasts, and no office hours. good luck trying to ask him a question beforeafter class. He is clearly interested in teaching, but his lectures aren't presented in a logical manner and you often have no idea what will be on the tests.  Go to the review sessions - they will teach you way more than lectures.

He def knows his stuff, but lecture's a bit monotonous and not very stimulating. Your grade is hw, 2 midterms, and 1 final. Exams only have questions off of the hw, so it's an easy A if you're good at memorizing. He never had OH, and some students got an F on the final for no reason and he was MIA when they emailed him. Apathetic but knowledgeable

The tests are exactly the homework questions; this class will require intense and rote memorization just because of that.  Answers to the homework questions are given during discussion, so make sure to attend those. Lectures can be a bit dry, but he will bring guest lecturers towards the end of the semester and I found those to be more fun lol.

analysis.name: Bing Cheng

review_highlights.comment: The only way to pass the class is to teach yourself the content outside of class hours. Lectures are confusing, scattered, and poorly organized. You also only get 2 units for 4C if taken after 3C.

Passionate about the subject but not good at teaching at all. Provides no feedback and 75% of the students were failing before the final. Take this course at community if he's the only professor available here.

Within this class, you are expected to know all topics and have no other way of learning. Other classes give out cheat sheets and give better explanations as to what to do for problems. He'll put the blame on you when he doesn't give enough help as to what to expect. In a class where the average for the midterm was 50%, you'd think he would help.

analysis.name: Bill Geibel

Professor Geibel is a solid choice as a professor and gives a well-outlined agenda on what is required from us. analysis.name: Amy Bintliff

Dr. Bintliff is super accommodating and tries to build genuine relationships with her student. Due to Covid-19, we were not able to participate in person mentoring and tutoring. analysis.name: Brinda Rana
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She had one of the most disorganized canvas modules I never seen, her lectures were so confusing giving lecture on a topic but then say we won't need to know that. I was constantly emailing the TAs and IAs to understand what the quizzes or exams were going to be on and they didn't know the answers. Had an example of past final exam from 2018...

Honestly you know its bad when even the TA and IA say that Professor Rana makes this class so much harder than it has to be and that she is so disorganized and not good at teaching to the point its makes them frustrated as well.

She is not good at teaching all she does is read her slides off do not recommend not even sure allowed to teach UCSD

She is SOOOO incredibly confusing. It may be just me, but the homework is confusing, the tests are confusing, her lectures are confusing, like what we are actually supposed to understand. She doesn't tell you straight facts; it's just a whole bunch of information put everywhere. She keeps giving me headaches fr.

Course had 4 quizzes, weekly HW, a final, and a group project. TAs and IA were not helpful, discussions felt pointless. No calculators allowed on exams. Did not follow syllabus and was disorganized wrong dates, information. Teach yourself.

analysis.name: Marcus Brooks
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Clear grading criteria. The content was pretty hard for me, not sure why. But the lectures were definitely helpful, all exam were take home but proctored (3 total exams). Honestly loved Prof. Brooks, took him previously for MGT 4 and loved him for MGT 131A. Ended with a B-, somehow scored less than average on 2 exams, but felt like I studied a lot

Many of the concepts were pretty tough, but he managed to break it down in manageable steps and was clear about what we had to know for exams. 2 midterms/1 final, and weekly reading/hw (around 4-5 hrs/week). Very understanding and firm about class policies, and I would take him again in the future.
Very well taught class with about 2-3 hours of work each week. Make sure to read the SmartBook chapters on McGraw-Hill and attend lectures for participation points.

analysis.name: Lucas Buzaglo
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Amazing Professor. Very active on piazza and hosts occasional office hours. You can tell that he wants you to succeed and cares for his students. Fair midterms, difficult final. Very generous curve. To succeed in this class, doing his practice finals, homework plus office hours and questions on piazza is good enough to pass exams. Highly recommend

Good Professor and very nice guy! His textbook is my favorite part as it isn't very mathematically savvy compared to other textbooks. Hard Final. Fair Midterms. I'd recommend really studying practice tests the most as most points lost come from missed proof steps, not correct answer. A lot of professor gate-keep exam info, he wants you to do well.

An amazing professor!! He gave amazing lectures and explained everything well, although the course itself is challenging, especially after midterm 2. It is a reasoning math class, so you kinda need to write a short paragraph proof for each question, but the grading is very lenient. Overall, an amazing quarter with him, a very nice professor.

Chefs kiss, he really set the bar high on my expectations for math professor at UCSD. His lectures are amazing, his office hours are spectacular. He really cares about his students; always checking to see if people have questions. He makes sure you are equipped with everything you need to succeed in his class. I cannot recommend him enough.

Literally the best professor I've ever had for math! Gave out review lecture notes and past midterms/finals before every exam. Although class may be very hard, just make sure to ask a lot of questions!!! After mid-term 2 is when this class got super difficult, and he started to pick up the pace dramatically, so be wary of that.

analysis.name: Burritt Demill
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I've had Demill before for other classes and i was disappointed W/ 103. Demill still has his incredible and engaging lecture style, but the class formatting could use work. Lecture material is outdated due to the rising use of social media. Class content is difficult unless you read the textbook. Read the book as 103 is much harder than 162 or 16.

This class was a lot of fun, and people of all sorts can find it useful. Very interesting lectures, 2 group projects or homework, and the final is a large negotiation. The lecture was mostly taught through random videos, but what he said afterward was interesting. Grading I found to be harsh in this class, barely anyone gets A's, but overall fun.

chill class and prof is very passionate and charismatic about the topic. it's clear he cares about his students succeeding as well as his TA. some assignments can be a bit unclear paired with the rubric. i wish they took more time to explain why some points got deducted. i also didnt like how half the class was based on videos

Professor Demill really cares about his students and gives super inspirational lectures. He teaches a lot of applicable material in the real world. It's a great class to take even if you're not a business minor because what you learn really sticks with you.

He is a very nice guy and his lectures are interesting but I found that his grading rubric was often unclear, and instructions on assignments were difficult to understand at times. Additionally, there are sometimes random pop quizzes which can be scary.

analysis.name: Jose Burgos
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor is one of the best I've had! He is very fair in grading. Midterm and Final are all online. There is one group presentation (about 15 min). It is definitely possible to earn an A if you attend most of the lectures and complete all the discussions and assignments.

The fact you are even at UCSD will get you an A in this class. Very easy class Burgos is a very nice guy wants his students to do well. Midterm and final are take home. One discussion post a week. Very manageable. There's no negatives to taking this class take it for an easy A

joke of a class. I had over 200 responses on the pollev and didn't get out of the final bc it was only 60% rate but when I asked the TA he said we need a 60 to 70% participation rate. so you literally need over 300 responses on the pollev SICK JOKE!! further pushing my hatred to this school. thank you im dropping out

Weekly discussions & quizzes, attendance is mandatory through I-clicker (phone). One group project that was easy, he cared more on discussions during a presentation with one shared paper to complete. If you participate in Pollev, and you have a 96%+ you do not need to take the final exam. One midterm that is online, not in class. Fun class

Besides mandatory attendance the class is very chill. Easy A!! You're able to be exempted from the final if you have a 96%+, 100% in attendance (via iClicker or paper attendance), and a good participation grade. The average for the final was like a 95%!

analysis.name: Leonid Butov
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very easy class, final was a challenge but doable. Leonid has a very dry sense of humor which makes lecture entertaining. Only real challenge in the class is walking down the very steep path to Blacks beach to collect data for the first lab.

Don't need to bother going to lectures, they are pretty useless. Just read everything on what he posts or look at old lab presentations from ucsd. Homework is 1-2 questions per week. Lab reports can be confusing but just go to the extra lab sections and ask a lot of questions, then you'll be fine. Make sure to read old homework/labs for final;

Not really sure what we learned in this class but you don't really need to and you'll still be fine. HW is just like 1-2 textbook questions every 2 weeks and theres only 4 lab reports. His lectures weren't really helpful it was just going over 2 math problems and the experiments but that was about it, nothing new learned in this course.

He's a very knowledgeable professor and teaches in a clear and structured manner. The course is difficult starting with a base of only basic quantum mechanics, but grading is based on homeworks (graded real easily) and on a project and a written paper, which isn't too heavy.

Absolutely time-consuming course. Material pretty easy. However, if you think deep over some pattern using latex.. it will be hard, for example, if you derive Bohr's model with the exact atomic number. Or if you use the biot-savart law to derive the Helmholtz coil.

analysis.name: Harold Buchanan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 106 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The class was overall enjoyable. The professor does step-by-step demonstrations of how to solve problems that will be on the homework and eventually on the tests. There are weekly homework assignments which are fairly easy. You don't have to read the book but if you do it helps a lot during the midterm and the final.

Class is common sense: show up, participate, and do the assignments for an easy A. Attendance is mandatory and checked, only few assignments that are no longer than 2 pages and are self-reflective. Participation is very mandatory, which can be the only intimidating part but Buchanan is very welcoming to all ideas and is super funny.

An old-fashioned and very stubborn professor. He has a very strict class policy that does not allow people to use phones and be late. He does not respect or care about students. You won't be able to get a full participation grade since he only calls the people who sit in the front. The grade is not arguable since he only thinks he is right.

He's not the friendliest guy when I asked him questions in person. Wouldn't even give me eye contact. I like that we get chances to work with classmates. I'm tired of going to classes and not getting the opportunity to make friends. 5% extra credit from quizzes and answering questions in class. 3 exams. Read the textbook for conceptual!

Good professor! sometimes speeds through the material though. Lecture is not mandatory but helpful because he offers extra credit with iClickers. The class itself was hard for me since I'm not good when it comes to financing, however, he offers lots of extra credit opportunities to raise your grade and curves generously with each test.

analysis.name: Anthony Burr
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you're great at "guess the song", you're going to do well in this class. Interesting history into hip-hop. Basic quizzes after lectures covering core concepts. As he puts it: "If you listen to the songs and study the lecture slides, you'll be just fine." In general, any class that blasts Chief Keef in Peterson Hall is great imo.

The class was overall easy, but more studying goes into than you think! Make sure to go to lecture, listen to required songs, and study the lectures a day or two before the midterm and final, and you will do well.   P.S: Don't waste your money on the required book. You don't need it to do well in the class.

I can tell Prof Burr is enthusiastic about his lecture but his lectures are just a snooze fest because he speaks in a very boring tone and the class is just honestly very easy. All the exams are all multiple choice questions and 60% of it are "guess the song" questions. Take him for that easy 4.0, but do not take him if u wanna stay awake in class.

The professor himself is great. Super nice guy that understands that people don't really care about the class. The 3 hour lectures are a joke though. There's weekly quizzes that are meant to encourage attendance but he posts the slides so you can just take the notes without going. Also there was an annoying amount of work required for the papers.

He is super nice, very passionate, and knowledgeable. He posts lecture slides, discussion attendance is mandatory. Exams were kind of difficult but he provides everything you need to know. He cares about students and MUS17 is a fun class. Would definitely recommend.

analysis.name: Byung Kang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Awesome professor, took ANSC 148 with him. This was his first time teaching the course and was incredibly open to student feedback. Lectures are interesting and he really cares that you learn the material.

Professor Byung made sure lectures were super fun to attend and I looked forward to class every week. Although most assignments were group projects, he does give students the option to submit individual assignments as well. Would take his class again 10/10

Such a great professor! SO caring for his students. Assignments were group projects, but the project and materials were very fun and educational. Readings and lectures were great and educational as well. Super great if you need a fun easy class!
Very kind professor who's assignments are pretty easy to understand. Most of it done in groups, which is fun but there are also individual alternatives as well
Professor Kang is very nice and all the TAs are very helpful. Was taking to fulfill the requirement but loved it.

analysis.name: Byungkook Lim
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Lim is research faculty and only teaches this one class every Spring quarter. His class size is small by choice. He goes through lecture material very fast and it is very dense, but he tries to be specific. He cares about the lecture material and although teaching isn't his focus, he does a good job trying to get feedback from students.

Professor Lim is very transparent about the difficulty level of his class. This course has helped me grow as a researcher more than any course at UCSD. If you attend class, read the papers, and go to OH you can succeed. The first exam was definitely a shock, but if you learn how to take them it'll be ok. It's worth it to grow and be challenged.

He is the type of professor that blames his students rather than take accountability for his own actions.  He showed us how poorly the previous year's class did in trying to scare us to drop.  You really think if the averages for midterms are in the D-F range, it is the student's fault? He does statistics in Neurobiology but can't comprehend this

Dr. Lim is honestly one of the best professors at UCSD.  He is actually a genius!  BIPN 154 is 90% going over papers from researchers and his lab and telling the class what they found.  The class is super interesting as you learn so much about how the brain is wired.  Tests are actually fairly difficult but if you study, you will be fine.

Prof Lim spent the 1st lecture saying how everyone fails his class, even showing horrifying statistics. When entire classes are consistently failing, the professor should reconsider their teaching ability, not blame the students for being dumb. Teachers are supposed to inspire, not flaunt how impossible it is for someone to succeed in their course.

analysis.name: Kathryne Byrne
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Byrne showed no enthusiasm towards the course and was only present to read her PowerPoint. She struggled to give clear answers to her own Iclicker questions, and lacked a clear grading scale. Her exams tested on content she did not instruct/ expand on and would test content she instructed not to study. She did have weekly quizzes that were rela

The worst professor I've had in college. Talks incredibly slowly and only reads off her powerpoint. When she doesn't know what she's talking about she will mumble and trail off. It would be faster to stay home and look at the slides yourself but clicker participation is necessary and based off of questions that she doesn't teach in class.

Ruined Bio for me ... This class was supposed to be an easy lower div but this prof made it the worst class I've ever taken in college. Only thing she does in lecture is reading off her ppt (in extremely slow pace). Specifically told us not to read the book and tested us on materials in the book and barely included anything on her lecture slide.

You'd be better off reading the textbook (which isn't mandatory) or the slides yourself than going to lecture but clicker questions are a part of your grade. Her weekly quizzes are TOO easy compared to her exams. She's very hard to reach outside of class, she'll either respond to your emails too late or not at all. Be prepared to teach yourself.
Take her class as letter grade, fat curve in the beginning, fat curve in the end. More than half the class got A's

analysis.name: Sarah Bynum
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's one of the best professors i've had. She's really interested and involved with her students, and yes, while she does have work, it's fairly easy, and as long as you do it (it's just papers, 2-3 pages each of fiction! come on you writers!) you'll get an A.

She is a great professor, really cares about her students and has an honest and invigorating love for writing. She is so supportive of everyone's work, is welcoming to new ideas, and just has just a passion for the written word. Definitely recommend her.

Bynum was fun, in every sense of the word.  The assignments were good, the reading fun, the writing fun ,and the lectures fun.  You can tell she's honestly passionate about her field, and it rubs off on her students.  Loved her mannerisms, too!

It's a treat to learn writing from Sarah Bynum, a passionate and profound writer. Her teaching style nurtures both structured and subversive writing styles, which helped me discover my "voice" in a natural way.

best teacher in the ucsd writing dept hands down!! she is so adorable and really cares about her students. class is easy and fun. she makes you want to be a better writer. you're lucky if you get the chance to take her

analysis.name: Jennifer Carr
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Direct professor discussing very, very dense and complex material in a clear way. The class is outlined very effectively: complete readings, post each week, turn in your (x2) papers. Luckily, all of the readings were posted online, and she was always accessible - and eager - to answer any questions about class material. Do Read! She cold-calls c:

This was the hardest class ever. DONT TAKE HER. She uses so many excessive words in her lectures which confused me half of the time. She's also super monotoned. She makes this class harder than it needs to be. If you can understand logic then this is the class for you, otherwise, get ready to fail. Her average class GPA was 2.4!

this class is way too time-consuming for a lower-division course. It honestly felt harder than my upper-division classes. Save yourself the stress and take it at a community college—same material, way less wasted time.

prof. carr is ridiculously smart and an excellent teacher. she expects you to keep up and participate, but she's supportive if you don't get something. even if you feel intimidated, she is super nice once you approach her personally. PS: she'll totally be a renowned philosopher soon, so take advantage of her help while you can!! :)

Don't listen to bad reviews! She comes off as intimidating at first but she's the coolest. I've never heard someone talk with such sophistication and it actually makes sense. Very easy to understand but some ideas take time to process. She's passionate about everything she says. She takes this course very seriously. You'll get an A if you do too.

analysis.name: Catalina Reyes-Gonzalez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 110 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is a great prof. But her accent is strong, I'm having a hard time to understand what she is talking about even with 0.8x on podcast. Her first exam is extremely hard and mostly focus on week 1 and 2. Most of the class didn't finish the exam on time. She teaches too much details and the slides only have pictures, no explanation.

Caring professor. However, the lecture slides are narrow with only photos and her strong accent made it even harder to understand. There was little work to do in this class, so your grade depends on the 3 exams. The exams weren't difficult though since we had an extra hour to complete it.

Professor Reyes is a funny, caring, and attentive professor. Her lectures are easy to follow and her teaching style is consistent, content is also very consistent with homework. Homework is required like every other week in canvas quiz format. Exams are easy if you spend an appropriate amount of studying. Which is not alot tbh. Overall 10/10 prof!

I would not recommend taking Catalina for BILD 2. Lectures are too fast & confusing, must rewatch them to understand all the material; not all of the info is on the slides. Midterms are difficult even if you study a lot. Lots of hypothetical questions. Study guide/ problem sets do not help prep you for exam. Must study every detail from lecture.

Overall this class is one of the harder bio lower div classes, but she makes the process of learning all this material so much more complicated. The accent she has is not bad as other reviews say it is, but rather the speed at which she goes through content. Also the tests are hard and grading is unclear as the average on midterm 2 was a D.

analysis.name: Thomas Bussey
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 207 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Bussey is a great chem prof, he'll deconstruct complex topics and make sure you really understand everything. His tests are very specific and often more concept based than math, however the hw is math intensive. He's a great lecturer and very helpful during office hours. If you're stuck between Bussey and Johnson I'd say go for Bussey, less work.
Tests are all free response, 9 pages each midterm and 14 pages final and he sometimes grades unfairly. If you don't mind that then go ahead and take him, his lectures are good.

He is a literal god sent from the heavens to UCSD, a godless place in need of enlightenment. Never have I heard ideas expressed so clearly and with such grace. If you value your education or your life, take Dr. Bussey.

I loved Bussey because if you attended his lectures and rewatched the podcasts, you would get a good grade. Compared to Johnson, Bussey is a lot easier and he is so much more thorough in the way he teaches. Bussey will go over a concept many times in order for you to understand and he really cares about his students. Take him!

DO NOT TAKE HIM IF YOU WANT TO DO WELL!!! I love chemistry and this is nothing against the professor but rather the class. we have to do readings, discussion activities, reading quizzes, and problem sets but the kicker is that NONE of these even prepare you for the material on the exams which are every other week. be prepared to teach yourself.

analysis.name: Michael Caldwell
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Caldwell as a TA is both great and not so great. He's great at explaining the finer points of lectures in an relatable & funny way. But he is a crazy grader. If you're not overconfident in your writing abilities and care a lot about your grade, then don't take him, because it's hit or miss with him; it's hard to figure out what he wants.
There should be a rating for how nice or mean a teacher is. Sure, using helpfulness clarity and easiness are important..but some teachers are just jerks.

very intimitating. does not hesitate to mock you. calls on you when you look like you're clueless. sarcastic. 15% participation grades. couldn't he accept that some of us aren't as smart as the others?

Lectures and discussions were mandatory but I found his lectures engaging. His assigned readings were interesting and not super unreasonable I would say. Grade was made up of 2 essays (20% each), 2 in-section writes, class participation, and the final. The final was incredibly chill as well if you were familiar with the readings and paid attention.

Overall, his character was extremely energetic and lectures were somewhat engaging, but a lack of overall organization and sometimes confusing to follow. Only main things were lots of reading, mandatory attendance (quizzes/participation), 2 essays (20%/e) and final 2 informal essays (30%) . Class depends on TA, but overall, I would take him again!

analysis.name: Carrie Wastal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Overall this prof is nice and sincere. However, you are not taught how to write up to their standard, but its rather expected of you.  Insane amount of work to do for just a graduation requirement class. The grading is rather ambiguous, you don't really know any right or wrong answers, so its easy to do poorly if you are not constantly seeking help

I highly recommend Dr. Wastal for any MCWP! Writing a 13 page research paper seemed impossible coming from a CC but she was very supportive and her class helped me improve my writing skills tremendously. She's also very nice, approachable, cares about her students and just overall amazing. Take her if you can!

You'll never meet the actual professor, all taught by TA. Wouldn't risk gambling on getting a good TA check others out first. My TA was pretty good, however he did seem to hold a grudge because I missed a couple classes, graded harsher after. Other than that I enjoyed this class. AI topic was just too repetitive.

It is heavily dependent on your TA, you will never interact with the professor. That being said, my TA was absolutely fantastic and clearly cared about all of his students. I cannot give this professor a 4 or 5 due to the class being entirely taught by a TA. I would recommend looking at other professors before gambling on this one.

When I took this course it was managed by the professor and led by my TA, who was fantastic. It truly helped me grow as a writer. I'm not a great writer and took it during a time of incredible hardship, but I still did well. The program is strict on deadlines, but if you're honest, extensions are granted. Do the work, and an A is achievable.

analysis.name: Robert Campbell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 135 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Campbell is an excellent professor  great jokes, good lectures, and course content that applies to your life as well as in a business. His exams involve a lot of memorization and *anything* he says is fair game for an exam question, but the exams are open notes and open book which alleviates this. Take good notes and read the book and it's easy.

By far one of the best professors at UCSD. Lectures are engaging and materials are reasonable and are graded fairly. He is a very funny professor and those who gave a low rating are just mad at the fact that they can't accept any opinion outside of their liberal agenda. It is truly sad to see liberals so angered by a conservative professor.

This is only my second quarter, but I think Professor Campbell will be one of my favorites throughout my college journey. His lectures are very engaging. I do wish there were more opportunities to get participation points besides raising your hand to answer questions. His tests are open note too! I hope to take more classes from him in the future.

Just no! I don't believe these positive reviews are real, and my classmates said the same. He should be fired for the things he has said in class. He admits having been reported for his political rants. The class is easy pass but hard to get above a C because exam Q refers to very specific words he has said in class. Loves to talk RW politics.

If I could describe a perfect day, it would be called a Robert Campbell day. In the first lecture, he made it clear his goal is to make this the best class in UCSD, and he has gone beyond what I had expected. He is one of the few remaining conservative professors, but he challenges both sides of the arguments, which helps our intellect grow.

analysis.name: John Cena
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Even though people say he's a great professor, I haven't seen him a single time in lecture he always cancels lecture last minute. Haven't seen this dude at all, personally class was not bad but it just wasn't the vibe him not being in the class when 90+ kids shows up to his class. Not very respectful

Great professor, a ton of resources. His lectures were pretty much hybrid (guy prefers zoom, and in-person lectures only happen for group projects and presentation). Pretty engaging and inspirational; be prepared to practice the material a lot!\
Greatest Proffesor I have ever had. Didn't see him much but he was great.
I took this class to get my thuganomics degree, and Professor Cena did a great job. However, I often had trouble knowing where he was. The board and chair were great lecturerers as well.

analysis.name: Carolyn Kurle
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 73 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: What a fantastic professor! She gave us an essay for the midterm and a reflective of class materials finals. She doesn't go into the nitty gritty sophisticated models of marine conservation. She teaches what is feasible. I highly recommend

Kurle is amazing! She is very passionate about her work and she loves teaching BILD3. It might be weird to adjust to her way of teaching at first, but once you understand, everything will be fine. Go to class and don't fall asleep (which I doubt you will) and you'll pass with an A. Clicker q's and quizzes are easy and she podcasts! Would take again

I also wanted to add 'Hilarious', 'There For You', 'Would Take Again' tags but only 3 tags were allowed. My BILD3 class had 750 students but she definitely seemed to care about all of us doing well, getting good grades and actually understanding/getting interested in the material. She's so enthusiastic. I don't regret taking her AT ALL this 1st yr.

Kurle is an incredible professor. She's inspired me to change my major and made me ok with getting up at 8 for a class.  It's definitely not the easiest of classes and the material on exams is kind of nitpicky but it's 100% out of lectures (podcasted, and you can miss up to 6 classes) and required readings. Amazing class and would take again.

Dr. Kurle's lecture are very clear-cut. She's great at explaining concepts and takes time to answer questions. She made everything easy to understand. Exams are reflective of lecture material. There is just one midterm and the final.

analysis.name: Ana Celia Zentella
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I did get a decent grade but after all these years, it is clear that what you learned is useless in life and work. This prof. made a lot of noise; now her views are clearly obsolete. Official US English and mainstream culture are the sure thing!

WORST CLASS EVER!! ONLY WAY TO PASS IS TO AGREE WITH HER INSANE BELIEFS...ONLY TRIES TO HARP AND MAKE PEOPLE FEEL GUILTY...I TOOK A W BECAUSE I COULDNT STAND ANOTHER DAY IN HER CLASS....DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!!!!!

THE WORST CLASS AND PROFESSOR EVER! Stutters, harps on the same thing all the time, unorganized, unclear, tests on bizarre, random material. Stay away. Take another class, or at least another professor.
She is the WORST professor EVER! She is not clear or helpful at all. Don't take this professor unless you REALLY have to!
Her class is challenging and she is tough but if you put enough effort forth it will pay off... disagree with her and you better be ready to back yourself up... You need to work for your grade!!!!

analysis.name: Celine Wahl
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is an amazing teacher, especially in regards to introducing the German language to many who have never even tried their hand at learning it. Every class, even when we were doing back-to-back lessons, was super organized and helpful. Herr Wahl is one of a kind, and it really shows.
Languages at UCSD aren't the easiest, but Frau Wahl did an excellent job at organizing her lectures and making the class as interesting as possible.

I took LIGM1B and Frau Wahl was the best. She had a great sense of humor, tried to have engaging lectures, and did her best to explain grammar concepts in a language all of us hardly understood. I'd gladly take her again for the next quarter.

analysis.name: Celeste  Lanuza
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took this class my fall quarter as a gpa booster and did not know what to expect, however, this class turned out to be very easy. Midterm and final were based on a short group performance and teacher was very kind and helpful. Just go to class and participate and you should get an A, class was not as bad as some people are making it seem lol

Overall she was a great professor often it was hard because it was an 8 am class but other than that it was a pretty easy A the midterm was a small performance and the final was an outside performance but honestly it was really easy. She shows a lot of passion to ballet and it is seen through the dances. I loved taking her class.

She does not know how to teach dance. The class was not beginner friendly and she graded harshly on midterms/finals. The final was outside of class time and not scheduled on webreg. I recommend taking literally any other professor for dance. Class was quiet and miserable.

analysis.name: Katharine Cezo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Mandatory discussions and lectures that almost put me to sleep. No test or real quizzes with most your grade being participation based. Never put more than 2 hours a week into this class and was still the easiest A I've ever earned. Realistically, you won't learn much but ig a good class if you want a GPA boost. Really nice and caring person though

EASY A, could not recommend this class more. 2 extra credit opportunities were easy, and a lot of this class is based on common sense. Professor Cezo had caring and engaging lectures. Spent max 1 hour on HW each week. Such a good lecturer though with guest speakers often. Got over 100% in this class because it's just that easy! DO TAKE HER!

Easy A. Attendance for lecture/discussions is mandatory, you get 1 missed discussion and I believe 4 missed lectures before it affects your grade. There is easy extra credit. I got over 100% in this class and never spent more than 2 hours working on it out of the classroom. Lecture is boring, you have online discussions, NO TESTS, easy GPA boost

I absolutely loved professor cezo! she is a sweetheart and you can tell she really cares for all of her students. her class is very light and there are no exams. I learned a lot. TAKE HER CLASS you won't regret it!!

Her class is insanely easy to the point of being dull. Has meaningless, but time consuming assignments. Lots of group discussion boards. No exam. Definitely do not take if you struggle with organization and multiple assignments. The work is really easy, but you have to be comfortable with multiple deadlines. Easy A if you remember to do the work.

analysis.name: Maria Tere Cesena
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was really interesting. We read a couple of books and had to discuss what we found interesting and share it with the class. We watched movies and quizzes weren't really that bad as long as you read and paid attention. The final was a little different since you had to bring 2 guests for a performance you make. Good regional spec for ERC

She is knowledgeable, cares about her students, and is easy going. She IS NOT clear on what she wants for papers, and was extremely controlling over the projects. She kept interrupting student presentations. I stopped doing the readings about 3 weeks into class and still could participate fine. She is very nice though, and an easy grader.

Tere is a very nice teacher and really puts an effort into helping her students become better writers.  If you go to her office hours, she is willing to help you with your essays.  If it weren't for the fact that Muir 40 itself is tedious and seemingly pointless, I would recommend any class she teaches.

I didn't think I had a chance in this class because the writing is so tedious. She's really cool though. She understands her students and as long as you put forth an effort, you should get at least a B. Definitely take her.

Same teacher I had for Muir 40. This time she was a little less clear about what she wanted because I tried to apply what I learned in 40 to this class and it didn't work out well. She's still cool though. Recommended.

analysis.name: Cecil Lytle
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: A very funny an intelligent man. His quizzes and final were very fair and his lectures were very helpful an entertaining. The readings weren't bad either. If your a music or non-music major I suggest him, you will be satisfied in every aspect

Did not learn anything in this class. My class notes consisted of doodling. Lectures do not hold your attention and it's only interesting when he plays the piano, which is maybe once a month. Besides that, he does not explain the material clearly. I didn't know what I was supposed to know. I relied on my music background to get through this class.

This was a fun elective class.    He plays piano in class, which helps you stay awake in lecture.  Go to class b/c most of his notes are not in the book. He only posts skeletons of his lecture notes and song charts online. Midterms were take home, and you could write an 8 page paper (recommended) instead of taking the final -which was not takehome

His lectures can get a little off topic. This makes it hard to sit through but remember he's a jazz musician, don't expect too much structure! Haha. When he uses live musical examples, it can be much more helpful.  Ask for help if you missed anything! He's friendly and caring so he'll try to be helpful. Participate, quizzes, final paper, project.
My favorite Professor. He is funny and witty in his lectures but also very intelligent. A must for music majors or those who need an elective.

analysis.name: Celia Orona
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This teacher is one of the most helpless teacher in the world. She treat you like a high school student. Worst thing is she won't answer your question in class time. Also, she is very forgetive, she lost your homework and blame on you. Her class is very useless. She just keep reading on textbooks and word document instead of having useful activity.

Worst teacher ever. She treats her students like high school kids and expects too much from our essays, forgetting we are not encylopedias. The reason I progressed this quarter is because I did my best to get at least a 3/6 with her. She acts like she is nice but she isn't. Avoid her

She is such a horrible teacher. I got out of her class after having to be in there for a whole two hours writing an essay. And she doesnt teach you how to write effectively. Her essay format is useless; she will make you fail your exam. GET OUT ASAP BEFORE IT'S TOO LATE!! AHHHHHHHHHHH!!

This professor is one of the worst! She is very rude and blunt most of the time, even though she "tries" to act nice. She is very fake and most of the things you do in there are not helpful. Also, she is really strict. I recommend you to never take her unless she is your last result. OASIS writing program helped me pass the exam, not her!

Don't really recommend this teacher to those who is not a native speaker. I know she probably tried her best but she is simply not the 1st choice. I am not a very good student but even I find the homework very easy. That's why I am so not confident in the final exam. I took OASIS too, but that's simply not enough. Writing needs more practises.

analysis.name: Haley Ciborowski
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. C always has the best energy! Assignments were minimal but there was a group paper and project presentation which wasn't too bad if everyone contributed. She brought a lot of guest lecturers and attendance was 2 pts per class. If you ever have questions, she is super kind and responds to her emails pretty fast.

FMPH 130 has been taught by other professors in the past and midterms and the final were online and open notes. Dr. Ciborowski has changed the format to closed notes and in-person, paper style. She expects students to memorize over 600 powerpoint slides meticulously for the cumulative final. It is impossible and sets the student up for failure.

Sign in sheet/participation is a big percentage of your grade, if you miss one class your grade is down 2% and she only excuses covid cases. Tests are based off memorization and she wants super specifics when we already have to remember 9 different 50 page slides, TA's were harsh graders with homework assignments, but she is a super sweet prof

Professor Ciborowski's lectures are very informative and she is very thoughtful and accessible both in class and outside. Throughout the course, she will have multiple guest lectures. There is only one group project in the end of the year, one midterm and a final, both open book and online. Does have homework and reflection every other week.

Study guide was literally posted less than 72 hours prior to the midterm. Study guide was extensively long and was basically straight memorization of information. Midterm was in-person, old-school paper style. No notes, based strictly on dead memorization. Would not recommend, in comparison to Professor Long.

analysis.name: Benjamin Ciotti
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 73 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The quizzes were extremely hard and for most of the quarter, I had to teach myself almost everything. He expected us to know a lot of things, leading him to not go over some "basic" things because he believed we should've known them already. He's a nice guy (had a bit of an attitude sometimes) but his teaching style is not good.

The questions and problems on his hw does not appear on the exams. I wish he would have showed us more examples in the lectures. The lectures are easy to understand; however, textbook is the real source of help. You need to teach yourself most of the time. Tests and quizzes are graded very harshly. DO NOT RECOMMEND!!!

He's the worst teacher I have ever taken. Although he had little control over the contents of the quizzes and exams, his lectures covered very simple conceptual "examples" that gave you background on the foundational knowledge of the subject. He is easily accessible outside of class, I'll give him that. However, I would NEVER choose him ever again.

Professor Ciotti loves math and he is passionate about it but I don't think he should be teaching it. I was forced to drop the class because his lectures didn't cover much of what is expected on the hw. The tests are simple but he uses the "there's not enough time" excuse when you ask for help or for him to show an example. A very self-taught class

Ciotti is a nice guy but not the best teacher. He gives really simple examples in class and difficult, conceptual questions on the exams. He often responds to questions with "I don't know" or something roundabout that makes no sense to students. When solving problems in lectures, he uses methods without explaining his reasoning for using them.

analysis.name: Manmohan Chandraker
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: the GOAT, one of the few professors who give partial credit to a wrong answer. Homework is once every 2 weeks in average. Grading is very lenient, he makes sure we are interested in the subject more than the grades

Amazing. Easily one of the best profs in the CSE department. Lectures are captivating, with a great balance of theoretical/mathematical rigor, and practical applications of the techniques used throughout computer vision (and just AI general). His attitude towards grading also makes the class more fun than stressful. Start the homework early though.

Incredible teacher. You can tell he really cares for his students. Wrote individual feedback after both the midterm and final. Put a big emphasis on learning and having fun over grades. Very approachable and knowledgeable. I would gladly take any course with him teaching.

An absolute gem of ucsd. Professor Chandraker is very caring for students, he cares about if you really learned in his class. Don't worry about your grade as long as you put effort into the class material, try your best to get a grip on what he taught, and always ask questions! Professor is always there for you! One of the best classes at UCSD!
going to go against the grain and say currently i don't feel lectures appropriately convey information to the audience. they have been using many suboptimal teaching methods

analysis.name: Ching Wei Ho
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: he's a good prof. he can teach, good vibes, and midterms are pretty easy if you studied. but prepare for the final. bro made the final more difficult compare to last quarter which is a bummer. not only that, HE DOESN'T CURVE. i repeat. HE DOESN'T CURVE. overall good prof but sadly could be better if he curved.

It is unfortunate for all econ major students that we have to take this class before we can take the major upper-division level courses. But the fortunate part is that if Ching Wei Ho is your professor, you can still manage to get the whole class through with an A! He cares for his students and is always responsive to email. He is a goat!

Professor Ho is the best Calc professor. Goated! Very passionate about teaching, the lectures were easy to understand, and approachable after class. Btw, although lectures are not mandatory and there's recordings, the quality is quite poor. I recommend to just attend the lectures, and that Discussion session is mandatory.

the practice exams are the same as the midterms and final. he lets you bring a cheat sheet to each test (front and back). he's super caring and just wants all his students to pass. attendance to lecture is not mandatory but discussions are (7/10), however lecture is recorded and posted. super chill teacher would so recommend

HW - 20%, Participation - 5%, 2 Midterms (22%), 1 Final (31%). The professor's lectures were clear, and going to lecture will 100% make the tests and studying easier. His attitude and attention to detail are above average. The midterms were easier than the homework and relatively straightforward, but the final is harder but fair. I would recommend!

analysis.name: Clark Gibson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is hands-down the most challenging poli-sci class I've taken to date, in a good way! The quizzes seemed hard at first but after you get a feel for what they're testing on--they're not bad at all. You need to actually put in the effort to do well and there's nothing wrong with that. Prof Gibson is super funny and knowledgable! :)

he does lecture the entire time and tell stories, but its honestly not too bad. memorize key concepts in the weekly readings and you will be fine for quizzes/ tests. he is intimidating at first but does not bite unless you cheat or scheme against him. just show up to a class you signed up for and read

Amazing prof, funny and charismatic. His lectures are truly entertaining, and he always has the most insane/interesting stories ive ever heard. Stay caught up with the readings and you'll be chilling in this class- and he always explains the readings too. random quizzes at times, but only like 4 questions and pretty simple. 10/10 would take again

someone who gets off topic quite a bit but honestly if you do the reading you already understand the concepts. frustrating at times, but both exams and the quizzes are solely on the readings, so its not detrimental to ur grade. for the final he gave us all the questions in advance + gave us the points for two quizzes we didnt have time for. not bad

Great professor. The material was easy to follow and self-explanatory. His stories in class often connected the concepts to real-world situations, which made the content easier to understand. The class was very engaging and the reading materials were interesting. There are occasional pop quizzes, but they're easy if you keep up with the readings.

analysis.name: Cindy Gustafson-Brown
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: 5% are quiz clicker questions (need 72% to get all 5%) 5% are class clicker question (just need to answer 75% of this) Optional 10% are section paper (3 of them) 5% section participation (Show up to section) 20% final section paper optional 15% midterm exam 40%, 50%, or, 65% Final exam depending on the "optionals"

This class isn't hard. It's her ridiculous grading. The real reason people score badly in her classes is that she has so many ways to penalize you for every little thing. She does it to make you artificially lower her average and make you feel stupid. Avoid! Avoid! Avoid!

I've taken BICD 136 and BIMM121 with Dr. Gustafson. First thing first, shes is a very dynamic and engaging lecturer, probably one of the best I've seen. She makes you want to learn what she presents because she really loves what she's teaching. You will work harder then you have ever worked, but probably won't get above a B-. She's a GPA murderer.

Too much workload! She makes us read 2 book chapters and 1 research paper every week, making it very hard to catch up. It is actually doable if you dont take any other classes that has workload, but considering that most students do, this class is So TIRING. Dr Gus is, despite all that, a nice lady. However, too much information jammed to class

Professor Gustafson-Brown is great as a person. She is very like-able and tries to make lectures fun. BUT, when it comes to material she over complicates things and her exams are very long and she expects you to remember every single detail. I do not recommend taking this class with her.

analysis.name: Emily Clem
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She uses something called skills based grading where instead of getting grades on individual assignments you demonstrate mastery of concepts. If you do well on quizzes and homework you don't have to take the final. She also does flipped classroom style so all the learning is from videos. Personally hated both of these systems but it's a fun class.

Class was simple in the beginning and catches you off guard in an instant. Homework was pretty challenging at times (once spent over 10 hours working on one). Her examples are simple compared to the homework and exams. You will most likely try everything on google with no luck and a bunch PDFs to read through. Lectures are boring and Podcast-ed.

Shes not bad or anything, but I couldnt focus on any of her lectures. This was an issue because syntax almost killed me. I recommend going to office hours or section. The homework is once a week but very hard so PLEASE join a student homework group because if you try to do everything alone there is a chance you might fail. Trust me.

Syntax is a hard class -- HW takes a long time and is not intuitive. But her grading system reduced stress and made it much more manageable; midterm and final were like 'catchup points' not 'if you get a B, you'll never recover'. I didn't think her lectures were boring at all; I think she's one of the best professors I've had.

This was her first quarter at UCSD and I applaud how smooth the course was. I'm not a linguistics major and this class was manageable if you take the time to review the lectures. Weekly homework but most of the answers can be found through the lectures. Final was long/hard but she generously curved the class.

analysis.name: Alexander Cloninger
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Cloninger is passionate about his profession and keeps his lectures very focused on the class itself. Ht goes through the material pretty quickly, but is open to questions and he writes his notes in a way that makes it very easy to take notes. Although I didn't like the class every much he is a great professor that I would recommend to anyone.
This is one of the most densely packed course I've ever taken. The content he goes over in class doesn't nearly prepare you for the homeworks or the exams.

I dont think Ive learned a lot. Possibly since Im just not so interested in the topics. However his exams were pretty easy and I didnt spend much time studying but still ended up with an A-. Some HW assignments took me hours but the TAs were very helpful.

Overall a great professor. Exams were 75% HW / 25% Past exam problems. Very good and informative lectures. Podcasted lectures, which he mentioned he might not do again. Homework load was a little heavy at times, lots of material covered. Skipped around the textbook too much, sometimes I had to go read previous chapter to know what was going on

no midterm and weekly hw assignments every week. Wish more respect was given to the science of teaching. For hearing these things for the first time flow of information feels ironically unoptimized. There were not many visuals time is spent writing on the chalkboard every lecture

analysis.name: Clara Meaders
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: The professor's test were not reasonable. The test felt like they were made to make you fail. The lectures and homework were nothing like the exams. The TAs were often either unhelpful or were unsure of what to do.

Get ready for very challenging exams, difficult lab reports, and two finals in the last week worth almost 50% of your grade. She is not very supportive of students without a strong molecular biology background. Homework questions are extremely hard and you lose points often. I would take this class with anyone but her.

Class is very hard and concept is not easy to follow. She expects student to know a lot of details about molecular biology. Exams are super hard and she does not care about class average and wants to challenge students. TAs are not good and helpful and they do not answer questions. They are very fake.

Dr. Meaders is a blessing of a human! Shes very smart and cares deeply about her students and their learning. Tests are challenging, but she has a lot of failsafes built into her grading policy (i.e. extra credit, dropping assignments). She also asks students for their opinions and feelings about their learning experiences. Cant recommend enough!
The course was challenging, and at times the grading felt unclear due to her vague expectations!! Lectures were very difficult and did not always align closely with exams.

analysis.name: Clinton Tolley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: !) HE IS SO CUTE! 2) He is super helpful. 3) The topic is so interesting. Overall amazing teacher. Best teacher I have had so far.

He is a great professor, only graded by a few things  that are the same every week: Discussion post, Weekly quiz (with three attempts), small writing opinion in class, and reply to discussion post. The class has only one midterm and one final. The final and midterm are only worth 15%, while the weekly quizzes are worth like 21%. Easy class for an A

When you see him writing notes on the board, don't worry, you don't have glaucoma, literally it is unreadable and there are NO lecture slides, 1 midterm, 1 final, both take home papers, i dont know how good of a grader he is because I havent finished the course yet, im only doing this because im procrastinating on one of his papers as we speak

Took phil 181 with him. Lectures were really nice in the beginning but as the course went on I only went once a week. I think it was more the material i didn't care much for. in class assignment once a week, discussion post every week and quiz. But he gave a pdf of quiz on canvas and that helped me get through the readings. Lectures not recorded.

Phil 35: He is not a good lecturer (goes on rants and isn't concise), lecture participation is mandatory and there's extra credit for additional discussion posts. There are 2-4 readings (25+ pages) each week, the midterm guidelines are similar to the final (1 midterm/final), and there are multiple choice quizzes each week.

analysis.name: Clarissa Reese
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
