review_highlights.comment:
- all guest lectures
- one homework assignment per week graded by completion, discussed during section
- midterm & final are free response but pretty easy, just study the discussion slides

The class is mainly guests who come and lecture instead of the professor. Grading really depends on the TA. She allows a cheatsheet only on the front side. My suggestion if you take this class is to pay attention during discussions because most of the midterm questions are from the discussions, but are more in-depth.

super easy class and an amazing professor. there are weekly hws which are based on lectures. reading is given out but no one does it and honestly you don't need to finish hws and tests. hws are graded on completion not accuracy so just make sure to answer all parts of the question. dr. reese is so nice and just wants respect for guest speakers.

Almost ALL guest lecturers & most of the info is useless for exams as it's to see if you're interested in their topic (gets boring). only important info is on the weekly hw. Prof. also yelled at students multiple times abt respect for talking/doing something for another class during lecture, which i thought was unnecessary. readings are optional

This class lives up to its reputation as the most difficult class in the major, but I've never had a class with such real life benefits. It's a research class, but with a big professional component (some classmates even got jobs). Dr. Reese cares a lot about her students and is always there as support, but you need to go to her when you need it.

analysis.name: Claire Edington
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Took her for the "Tropical Disease" class. Love her, she's such a great lecturer. I got an A+ due to the extra credit she gave at the end. Certified mother.

Literally just take the class if you guys are wondering if you should. She is the easiest history teacher you will find and she is so nice. It's clear that she cares about her students and literally she barely gives out any homework. There are group discussions but they're so easy. Take it, its such easy credit!!

"woke"? lmao that comment makes me mad oml. bro doesnt know the meaning of the word. This class is so eye opening, the prof is very passionate and amazing at lecturing, this class talks a lot about decolonization and provides a lot of different perspectives through different mediums to really communicate how decolonization has shaped society. 10/10

I loved this class so much! If you're thinking of taking her class, just do it. She is very engaging when lecturing and sooo easygoing. There isn't a lot of homework AT ALL, the main thing she has students do is read the material before she presents it in class. Even if you don't read it, it's still clear to understand when she's teaching it later.

It was personally difficult to obtain all lecture material as she does not provide recordings. However, she is extremely understanding and caring, as well as willing to help if you put in the effort to reach out. She truly cares about the material she teaches as well.

analysis.name: Claus Sorensen

His proof were not always clear but were fair enough. I believe he could have address the class in better ways. His test are a mixture of fair questions that reflect the material and a few questions that are almost impossible to solve. I went to his office hours and he seemed to always be busy, it would be great if he was more available to students

Definitely don't recommend Professor Claus' class because he is not a good lecturer; especially, in his class, students are forced to keep taking note and don't have time to actually learn; other than that, he does't focus on concept and often only talks about examples. I honestly don't like him, and I regret it so much.

analysis.name: Seth M Cohen

Awful teacher. Absolutely doesn't care about the students. Rude and disrespectful, when I asked him for a makeup on a quiz I missed because I had surgery, he said there was nothing I could do and that I would get a 0.

Completely vague on what he expects to see on a lab report. Insufficient guidelines that are set like traps for losing points. TAs were jokes, they "helped" me changed my own correct answers to wrong ones. And now, three weeks after the grade given, told us grades were all wrong, there's no curve, 94 is A, only 20 As in a 600 ppl class. Amazing.

He seemed like a fair teacher initially. But then, no proper communication or guidelines, and on top of that had no grade adjustments or curve factored into the class. Being a Chemistry course, you wouldn't except a professor to grade that strictly. Furthermore, he dropped all grades by 1/2 a week AFTER grades were finalized and posted to academics

analysis.name: Cory Root
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

He lost himself in those slides made before the lecture day and then skipped all important information. He ruined my last bio class.

Allows cheat sheet (1-sided for midterm & 2-sided for final) which is very helpful. Exam questions are very similar to his practice tests. Easy but boring class.

Really great professor with the reverse classroom thing. He is very kind and willing to help when you ask or attend OH. In his exams, you are allowed 1 sided 8x11sheet and the final both sides. The exams are heavy on the short-answer parts, so you do need to know the material pretty well but he is a great teacher. Iclicker is used for attendance.

Dr. Root is a really kind person. The class is flipped and the material is so dense that people tend to cram their entire cheat sheet. Unfortunately, it feels like the class is more of a "how detailed can you make your cheat sheet and retrieve the information" class rather than a class built on memorization and memorization.

flipped lecture classroom, cheat sheets for midterms and finals, and good feedback is given. he gives a lot of practice material to prepare you for the exams so you know what to expect. the discussion style lectures were lackluster, he lets everyone talk over him and he isn't very engaging. interesting material though.

analysis.name: Michael Coblenz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Faux-structured class: too many assignments & unclear directions. Randomly assigned group + TA is an absolute pain since it affects grade. Refused to let me switch and I lost points due to bad teammates.
Final exam grading was the worst I've ever seen: inaccurate grading and didn't approve regrade solely because I wasn't "close to a grade boundary"

The professor is very supportive and attentive to students. The class project is well-structured and closely reflects real-world SWE internship experiences. Since teams are assigned randomly, the project experience can vary depending on group dynamics. There is an oral exam, where students must explain  their own code. I liked this class a lot.

Amazing professor, this was by far the best class I have taken as a MSCS student. Amazing TA (Jacob) as well. I can't state enough how much I have learned and the group project element was a great way to finish off the course. There are quite a lot of readings and assignments, but both midterms were very chill. Most of the class probably got an A.

Zero clarity/accountability. He only taught Konva - had to self-learn coding for project w/ AI (and be tested on it via oral exam). No project sprints got graded til AFTER EOQ on a rubric he literally NEVER showed before. My project TA (Devanshi) was unhelpful and at one point had bizarrely insisted on joining my team's group chat, which was weird.

Class is not structured very well. Some TAs are good, while others don't provide prompt and constructive feedback. We didn't spend time with React as the previous class did, but instead made games for K-12 students using Konva.js. Lectures are mandatory and not very useful, while labs are busy work.

analysis.name: Joel Conte
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Conte is one of the nicest profs I have ever met. Lectures are clear, not too fast, with good logic, combining theory and examples. He gives clear explanation on your questions. He focus on usage of theories in real life and tests and hwks all require thorough understanding of the material. Tests are hard though, the average is around 70/100.

SE125 really depends on how well you ingest information because there is a lot of it. If you go to lecture every time though the class is rather simple. The final was pretty straight forward and the two TAs, Angshuman and Giovanni, were excellent and if you have them as TAs, take every opportunity to get their help because the class isn't a gimme.

Geniunely top-tier professor. Might even be the greatest of all time. This guy cares for his student & loves what he is teaching. Super fair grading and heavy curve. 

But the course itself is something else. Content-heavy, hard and time-consuming, you gotta put a lot of effort in. Office hours are a must, and the content is a lot to digest.

Anyone who thinks Conte isn't a good professor cannot be trusted. Prof Conte is the greatest and most caring professor I have had. This class was not easy but he has many office hours that are very helpful. He also explains problems really well. He wants every student taking this class to succeed, truly. CONTE ROCKS!

Took SE125 back in Fall 2024. Not too bad for a statistics class, just make sure you go to office hours so you can learn how to do the homework, because the office hours is almost more important than lecture for this class. Love Big Man Conte!

analysis.name: Cory  Smythe
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Easiest class I've ever taken, put absolutely no effort into this class, but I was taking this class to learn about jazz culture and instead was forced to listen to a bunch of experimental music only VERY tangentially related to jazz. I would have much preferred a more difficult class that taught me what I wanted to learn.

10/10 Professor. Class is graded on attendance for lecture and discussion, midterm, and final. He does attendance the first 15 minutes of class and never got mad students left early. He wants the class to be stress free as possible. Midterm and Final are super easy and online. We did not have class week 10  or midterm day. Easy A fr
Super interesting lectures, tests were easy, he's super sweet and wants it to be an easy, fun class.

analysis.name: Matthew Crum
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Crum is genuinely the best professor I've had, and I don't usually like writing/history so this is surprising. He turns what could be a boring class into an exciting one as he finds themes we can relate to. Your grade entirely depends on the TA, so you just have to hope for the best. If you go to lecture and discussions regularly you will succeed.

Crum is a great professor. very approachable and kind, he cares about his students and makes an effort to get to know them. Assignments are not marked by him and it's up to the TA. He doesn't teach much related to the actual assignments in lecture. He does weekly reading reflections and has EC assignments in lecture and outside. 2 essays 1 revision

Crum is my favorite prof I've ever had. His makes it extremely clear what is expected of you in essays and reading responses. Attendance is not mandatory, but a big section of the final is from stuff he says in class that's not on the slides/in the readings. Lots and lots of reading, but I actually enjoyed a lot of it. So caring and kind!

Super nice professor, interacts with students in lecture and makes the class feel really personal. Didn't have any trouble engaging in this class. There are two essays and they are graded sort of harshly but its really easy to find resources to help and the modules in canvas basically outline the essay format. Best HUM prof ever

Matt Crum my GOAT. I took both HUM 2 and 3 with him and his lecture style is super fun and thought provoking.

Lectures aren't strictly mandatory, no in class quick writes or quizzes but he will talk about the definitions of key terms that will appear on finals. I had to miss classes due to other midterms but he's super understanding about it

analysis.name: Meredith Crane
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She's a great professor. Since it's her first time teaching this class, you can tell she's putting in a lot of effort to make it engaging and enjoyable. The homework isn't difficult and is exactly what appears on the exams, which makes it very fair. She also offers a generous test drop policy.

Really good professor and overall really easy class. Lectures are really easy to follow and understand. The homework follows what was taught in the lectures and the test is very similar to questions on the homework. She drops one of your 3 test which is very clutch.
She was the best! I adored going to her class and she was a great lecturer. She drops one of the 3 exams which was clutch after not doing great on midterm 2.

Absolutely goated econ prof. Easiest class I've ever taken in my life, high school included. Three exams is most your grade, bombed the second exam bc I forgot it was happening and came in late and threw the third bc I had another final and still got an A-. Didn't go to many lectures or study for any exams but if you do, you can easily get an A+

CRANE IS THE BEST. The lectures are so easy to follow. Solutions to HWs are literally given in the discussions (which are recorded!). 3 exams, all non-cumulative, with lowest score dropped. I did well in exam 1 and 2 and did nothing in the course (0 in final) and got an A+. She is also very attractive. 10/10 professor, no complaints.

analysis.name: James Cooke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 131 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Avoid if possible. Sure Cooke is charming and funny but do not be fooled by the false sense of security. The worksheets, practice exams, discussion section problems are not at all reflective of what is to come on the tests. The only slightly helpful material were the end of the week problems. Also, hardest final I have ever taken in my life.

Tests are all free response, is very vague on what he wants when it comes to the questions and then expects very specific terms to be present in terms of answer for you to even get partial points. there is no curve. avoid at all costs!!

Pretty good guy and good personality. However, he is vague on what to learn for the course. Test are graded harshly. If you don't specify certain things you wont get the points for it even for effort.  Questions a vague and hard to know what he exactly wants. Could be better if practices were more like the test and given before the end of the week

Great Prof. He is really funny, which will help to keep some people awake through lecture. 2 midterm and 1 final. midterms are okay, you get to redo one question with a group. Final is a killer and worth 45%. Very long and tough. Sections are not mandatory, but they supply worksheets that are really helpful. Class is podcast. Isn't an easy A.

He's a nice guy and all, but I don't think he is a good professor. His lectures are so brief and only touch on the general idea instead of the detailed mechanisms, yet his tests were complete free response and he requires so much details. Tests are vague and I never know what he wants. Worksheets in class are useless. Please don't take him.

analysis.name: Craig Callender
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Funniest professor ever, but his grading and class as a whole were very disorganized. Didn't know what was being expected for the writing assignments besides some broad outlines (no rubrics given). Classes sometimes deviated off track. Finding things in canvas was like finding a needle in a haystack. Still found the course enjoyable though.

Why UCSD would elect a philosophy prof to teach an soc. based environmental class I cannot begin to understand. I like Callender, but his grasp and clarity of environmental issues is not sufficient to be of any use for this class, it's as if he's learning along with us. If you do not have to take ENVR 130 with him don't, stick to phil.

The lectures are very fast, sometimes not posted, only make sense with the actual lecture, not by themselves. They repeat the readings with less full content. The readings are per class and kind of long. Sometimes he has easy class quizzes based on the readings, never pop tho. Midterms are kinda hard, but final not so much, not curved. Mostly Bs.

He's a pretty chill dude, but his lectures were all over the place most of the time, and his Canvas was even more disorganized than his lectures. Lectures are mandatory, and he'll call you out if you go on your phone and do other things on your laptop. Grade is based mostly on midterm, final, and a big project, so it's easy to lose your A.

Funny guy and passionate about his material and brings his dog to class! Assignments are randomly assigned and not too hard. Tests are fair but super weighted and will affect your grade heavily. Lectures are mandatory and a little hard to follow.

analysis.name: Christine Crofts
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: 100% would and will take Professor Crofts again. It is obvious that she cares a lot about her course content, and she encourages students to share their thoughts. She takes students' opinions seriously, and answers questions so clearly and concisely. Assignments are not difficult. Not too much reading. VERY easy to talk to outside of class.

Amazing and sweet professor! Lectures are engaging and she encourages participation in class but doesn't force it. You can choose to have graded attendance or not, she accepts late work with no penalty, assignments and tests are easy and don't require too much. She's an easy grader just as long as you meet all the requirements. Highly recommend!!

WOW! I loved Prof. Crofts' class! Very engaging, invites discussion but is also understanding of every students' circumstances. Fun assignments and discussions; since I took her Food class it was often applicable to daily life. Attendance is mandatory if you want to to be! (you can choose which is cool). Take her classes, you won't regret it.

SHE IS AMAZING! I actually took her for soci 137: sociology of food! She is very caring, flexible and understanding. For the class itself, class is mandatory if you choose it to be (she gives you the choice). There is one group paper and the rest are papers instead of a midterm and final! Very chill easy A class. Take this class with her!

Lectures are actually fun never minded attending. optional occasional group work or solo. grade is mostly homework and a take home final and yeah that's it. the actual content was really good too honestly so it made it even easier to actually learn something without it hurting.

analysis.name: Teddy Cruz
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: A really sweet guy. As days go by, you see more and more people facebooking because no one gets what he's talking about since he uses some extreme terminology to express his mind. Grading totally depends on TAs. Show effort and variety in your projects and attend all lectures and discussions, A guranteed!

This class is definitely one of the WORST classes I've taken at UCSD. DO NOT TAKE CLASS IF YOU HAVE TOMAS AS A TA. He was so pretentious, unwelcoming, and had a personal vendetta on bio majors. Teddy rambled a lot and I was hardly able to understand what projects were for. I lost total interest in class because of the staff's terrible behavior :(

He's super nice and very passionate about what he teaches which is why he is so respectable. Even though the material isn't the MOST interesting, I've found myself intrigued at some of the things he's showed us. You just have to be open minded about things, it's an art class. Overall, really nice guy, the class isn't that bad.

Extremely theory based class, more so poli sci w/sprinkling of vis arts ideas. Prof Cruz is VERY passionate and I respect him for this, though, this class was DISORGANIZED. TAs were awful and aggravating. Everyone I spoke to could not follow along w/lecture as prof would stop class every 30 min to complain about students not giving full attention.

i am currently taking his vis 100 for FA 25. Teddy himself is a nice guy and is extremely passionate about his field, but is not a great teacher. we are in week 8 now and every single person I have spoken to about this class has not learned a single thing. the class lacks proper structure and we aren't provided the tools we need to succeed :(

analysis.name: Sarah Creel
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Hilarious. She doesn't even cover the material that will be on the weekly quiz until the week after. She posts up hilarious lecture slides which are full of blanks so you need to sit through her boring lecture which teaches nothing at all. For her weekly online quizzes, she does not give ANY feedback so you don't even know what you got wrong. RAGEE

You should definitely take Dr. Creel's class. She has an extremely fair and truly excellent grading system, and she uses scientific methods to help you genuinely master what she teaches. Before every exam, the TAs hold a review session—both the review slides and the problems are helpful! Everything she tests you on can be found in the lectures.
The fact that her grading system is fair and well-designed already puts her above many others. I also love her teaching style.
Awesome class! Easy A ! Just study lecture notes and you will be fine ! Great professor !

Very nice professor, knowledgeable in her field. However super test heavy, and tests were a bit too hard to study for (review session didn't even cover half of what was on test). Midterm1 super curved to accommodate, M2 easier. Lecture doesn't really help but still counted towards grade unfortunately.

analysis.name: Cressida Madigan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Madigan's class has been one of my favorites by far. As a non-biology major, the class content was fairly easy to understand and really interesting, especially the historical aspects. She is also very passionate about what she teaches. Discussion is online and there are 5 short quizzes (not cumulative) every 3-5 lectures along with a final.

Professor Madigan and her TAs are so thorough with their explanations I really appreciated all the work they put into the presentation slides and the mandatory discussions. The only thing that stopped me from getting an A+ was I missed a discussion class, but they give you 2 free excused absences so thats on me. 10/10 would take again

She goes fast during lectures, you can tell she is only reading off the slides. I felt like she didn't care if there was a mistake in her syllabus or study guides, outdated. Attendance is required now, I did bad with attendance but still managed to get A. Exams are poorly worded and can get confusing but should be ok w videos and extra studying.

This was the easiest class I have ever taken. The first midterm was very problematic due to the wording on many of the questions. But after many students complained through muddiest points, she changed improved the rest of the midterms which was great!!! All exams are open note, open internet, and could also be done remotely or in class. Would rec!

One of the easiest professors IMO. Class attendance is mandatory through iClicker, and lectures were easy to grasp. There are weekly journals; it's a bit tedious but helpful for me in understanding what we're going to learn in lectures. Bless her soul for making all the exams online b/c it's such a life saver. Would strongly recommend!

analysis.name: Jordan Crandall
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He showed up 60% of the time. He even missed the first lecture. When he was actually there, he would lecture on the same single point for over an hour (the apparatus). Doesn't explain things well at all. He trys to make himself sound intelligent by using unnecessary jargon and he even made up vocabulary which hinders the flow of information.

no no no no. this professor is really full of himself and likes to try to talk really intelligently. so much so that it hinders most of us from understanding what he's talking about. im sure he's a nice person(sometimes), but as a teacher... only take him if you really need to. he grades strangely.

Excellent individuated resource suggestions - really smart in this way. Blunt/tough in email but get over it because he's really caring in person. I said VIS183 but I had an independent study and writing course and none of the above listed.
Hate this guy... He was gone the last half of the quarter and we had practically no lectures during that time period.  I also had a power-hungry TA which doesn't help either.

u discuss readings in class. u have one project. midterm is presenting idea. final is finished project. u can do whatever u want on a chosen topic (video/flash/website)with ur skills(if u learned any from vis program at ucsd). u learn nothing from this class, it's boring, and his remarks at times can make him seem like an ass, but it's an easy A.

analysis.name: brian cross
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lectures are somewhat boring, and can put you to sleep easily.  The projects during the quarter were interesting and somewhat fun.  The midterm and final papers are not too difficult either.  Overall, just meh. TBH I just slept in his class and did the homework.  Oh yeah, mandatory attendance sucks.

Brian Cross was very insightful and had some really interesting films that I would have otherwise would never watch. He is also very chill and just overall pretty easy to talk to, and is pretty much very understanding if there is any problems with assignments and stuff like that

I've had Brian for two quarters now and I genuinely love his class. He is an inspiring artist and truly cares about what he teaches. He is super laid back and only asks that you try your best and show up. He is understanding and actually cares about his students beyond the classroom.Having him as a professor reminded me why I want to be an artist.

I didn't understand his lectures. The gist was social justice issues. He grades tough yet doesn't even do the grading. I felt that he explained the standards of his "tough" grading to the TAs pretty vaguely. One group got an A that didn't even follow directions yet we got a B & followed directions like what. The readings are difficult & don't help.

Excellent professor. Honestly, I slept through the lectures, but that's because they were 3 hours (6pm-9pm). He's really passionate about the course and the TAs are amazing. Only four assignments the entire quarter (two papers and two videos), which weren't too bad. There were a lot of readings, but you can get by without them. Highly recommend.

analysis.name: Thomas Csordas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Csordas is one of the brightest anthropologists out there today and this class is one of the most interesting you will ever find. It's not for everyone, and you must read the material, but if you do, the payoff is great. We were graded on two take-home essays of 8-10 pages. If you come to class and do the reading, you will do fine.

Good professor. Tons of reading, but what he assigns is actually interesting. Attendance is mandatory, but classes are mostly spent discussing the readings, so make sure you get them done. Grade is based only on 2 tests, but he also gave 1 extra-credit assignment and curved a LOT. His TA Ben Merrill is really sweet and understand, loved him!

Professor Csordas is one of the most unique professors, I've been fortunate enough to meet. I was impressed by his research and past educational career. During class, I was frequently engaged and the readings were super interesting. You won't find another class like this at UCSD. Make sure to show up even if you don't finish the reading.

He is a facilitator for the small seminar-style capstone for Global Health. He's kind of quirky and follows the mold of an absent-minded professor sometimes (b/c he's so busy!) He's still very knowledgeable but is not super approachable.

analysis.name: Syrus Csaba Nemat-Nasser
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His class was easy. This course is based on mechanical physics, which is a prereq for this class. Sometimes, his lecture seems too simple and you end up not paying attention. It is okay. I did the same. However, when it is time for you to do your homework, you might be a bit irritated by the difference in difficulty. However, watch some youtube vid

Nemat is a very engaging professor. He is one of the few engineering professors I have had who truly cares to spend time making sure the students understand the material, absolutely. He will tend to spend times on material that seems simple, however, it is with good reason. FUNNY which is great for eng. class. Exams very close to HW & pract. ones.

PROFESSOR IS AWESOME! The class is hard, but he provides every resource to help you. I didn't attend office hours so I don't know how good he is at helping 1 on 1, but the TA's are helpful. Old test and quizzes are posted w/solutions which are useful. Class is clear and straightforward. UNderstand your HW and you'll get an A. Also be fast.

A very knowledgeable and genuine professor. He is a little goofy during lectures but this makes the class much more palatable and even funny. Almost too easy at times (could be difficult if you have a different prof for a later class in the series) but great at reinforcing full comprehension of a topic.

He knows the materials and he knows them well. I don't know if he's helpful in his office or not, but the lecture comes right of his head. Makes small mistakes at times. READ the book at least once before or after the lecture. DO the homework and sample quizzes and tests and you should be fine.

analysis.name: Marisol Cuong
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great great great caring professor. You can tell that her students' well being matters to her. Attendance is absolutely mandatory, but worth it. 2/3 lectures are in person and friday's lecture is asynchronous, which basically means you read on your own. Very progressive and gives her final before the finals week. Love her

Easy class but a LOT reading. Professor goes over the material but she is kind of difficult to follow along with bc she goes on tangents and I got the vibe she expected us to know more than what was discussed, which is why she didn't elaborate much. so maybe don't take this class if youre new to CGS content. Shes very knowledgeable and nice-ish

This class was a lot more work than I expected, especially for an English major. The essay assignments were time-consuming, requiring around 5+ hours of work each. Despite putting in the effort, I've been struggling to get decent grades, mostly C's. Might not be the best fit for those looking for an easy elective.

I took this class to be more informed and aware of sexual violence and I feel like Professor Cuong did an amazing job at lecturing giving the class material to spread awareness. Everyone in the class was very respectful and understanding, which was very heartwarming to see and helped the atmosphere of the class. Highly recommend!!

Professor Cuong was one of the best I've ever had. She gives very passionate lectures and tries to make them as relevant as possible so that the students can understand. Participation is very important in class, not just attendance. Lots of seminar/discussion work and reading. Weekly journals are due on Friday. Everything is fairly graded.

analysis.name: Craig Eberhard
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
Loved this professor this course is very chill. He has lots of anecdotal experience and most have some value. Lectures are easy midterm and final are online. He rambles a bit but explicitly says whats on tests

Just make sure to pay attention in class and take notes. The people giving this lecturer a 1/5 clearly didn't pay attention/go to class lol

This class does not measure your knowledge. It measures your ability to memorize and take verbatim notes of what the professor states, regardless of relevancy to the material. This class with Craig Eberhard is lecture-based and not learning by doing or project-based. If you want to learn anything, avoid taking this class with Craig Eberhard.

I actually don't know why the professor has such low ratings, he wasn't as bad as I thought. He does lectures but I would say the only hard thing about the class was the exam, just study for the math problems and you'll do fine. The concepts he taught was easy to understand too so I would say go for it if you're thinking about it.

He's OK as a professor. It's sometimes hard to tell what will be on the tests. Sometimes even if you attend all the lectures, you will miss a few questions on the tests because it seemed like it didn't matter. Midterm was easy and final was too hard. I got an A- on midterm and B- on the final, and I studied way more for the final.

Like the other comment, I was really worried about this class and the prof but he does care about his students and he does want us to succeed. If you did well on the midterm, he let us use that score for the final so most of the class didn't have to take a final. Attend class, pay attention, take good notes, and study and you'll succeed.

analysis.name: Curtis Marez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I definitely like this class a lot more walking out of it than when I walked in to it. I learned a lot of interesting things. Professor Marez is a pretty cool guy. He's passionate. Some said he stuttered a little but it didn't seem to bother me. Five two page papers to make sure you did the readings. Three pop quizzes to ensure you go to class.

Terrible professor. Says "um" about five times in between each word. lectures have very little to do with readings, and reading is unnecessarily heavy. All he did was spout off against neoliberalism. Doesn't answer emails, and goes through powerpoints way too fast for notetaking. Also, he is against everything electronic. No laptops. DO NOT TAKE.
Great professor, very caring--interested in technology and uses it in class, just asks you to sit in the first few rows if you are using a computer

Assigns way too much reading, some that he never discusses. Gives reading quizzes that ask about ambiguous and insignificant terms that were from reading. Hates all things technological and doesn't let you take notes on your laptop unless you sit in the front two rows.

He is horrible teacher, says um or uh between every word, reads off of slides verbatim, brings nothing useful to class. He won't post lectures, until midterm, otherwise no one would come to class. Never answers question, and gives inaccurate facts about history.

analysis.name: Charles Curtis
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is a cool dude.  The music you listen to throws a lot of people off since it is pretty obscure, but if you try to get into it, the class can be pretty fun.  It's different than any other music class and it really opens up your mind to things you would have never known.
If you make an effort, you can definitely get an a good grade in this class. The class material is also pretty interesting . Would definitely recommend.

Great professor, easy to get a good grade like most humanities classes. Class was actually decently interesting though not super exciting or anything, but I mean what do you expect going into a music class. Overall, I liked it and most of all it was easy.

it's my First class where I really had to know how to BS on everything-hw and tests-to get a good grade.He seems pretty intelligent and knows what he's talking about.  Although he may seem strange/unique, he's nice, approachable & wiling to help/clarify.

I agree with the 5/16/04 review. His voice sounds very educated. He rambles a lot and goes off topic. Still not really sure what this class is about but BS-ing is easy and his grading system is super lenient (he gives two makeup midterms).

analysis.name: Paul Curcio
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: class was set up to have guest lecturers every week. was an interesting class, but it was hard to tell what was course work and what was not. no midterm or final- just a book review and metrics assignment. curious to see if he will be teaching this course again in the winter

Paul is such a gem. He is extremely knowledgable about all aspects of urban studies and planning and has connections in the industry like no one else. Expect guest speakers and group assignments. His teaching style is dependent on you caring about the material. If you aren't passionate about USP don't take the course, but if you are, he's the best!

I absolutely LOVED this class! I was a bio major (now a cog sci/psych major) and I found the public transportation class to be my favorite class I've taken. The small class size gives you lots of opportunity to interact with Paul directly. He's just the sweetest guy and you'll learn *so* much you never even considered about transportation. 10/10

Lectures are pretty structured and you can expect what to come. Learned a lot about public transportation which I would never have known if I didn't take the class. He is approachable and makes lectures casual, like a conversation. He has a lot of practical knowledge many academics don't. Would definitely take another class from him.

Professor is very knowledgeable in the subject, and topics are applicable to current events in the field of transportation. The class structure allows for real discussion alongside guest speakers in the profession every week. To gain the most out of lectures every week, be sure to keep up with readings before class.

analysis.name: Sean Curry
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The professor did not have any passion to teach the class. For him, it seems like teaching is just producing goods in a production line. His lecture basicly repeats what is in the textbook.

I do not recommend this professor. I learned everything from YouTube tutors and nothing from his lectures. Once I understood the concepts I went back to my notes to see what he was trying to teach and still didn't understand his lectures. He knows what he's teaching but he doesn't explain enough to understand. Good luck.

The professor did not give the answers for his practice midterm and finals, which make students feel hard to review. I asked him about answers but he said no. Also, he did not give enough office hours during final week. He combined his MATH142B office hour with another class so I do not have enough time to ask questions.
The lecture is very boring, and it is very hard to get access to the professor after class. Exams are super hard.
The professor talks too fast in the class, so it is hard to follow up. Also, he covers too many chapters for this course, so it is very difficult for me to review.

analysis.name: Julie Cullen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Cullen is my all time favorite professor. Especially at a public school, you won't find many people who are as dedicated to teaching the material and ensuring the success of her students like Professor Cullen. The content is straight-forward, but the tests are designed to assess your understanding of the material rather than memorization.

After taking Machina, I was scared to take 100b. But Cullen is SOOO sweet. She's really enthusiastic so she speaks really fast. Her lectures are clear and concise. Absolutely NO tricks on the midterm or final. Some questions are tricky but these are meant to separate the A and B students. Easy Midterm, Hard final. (at least I thought it was) No HW!

Really great professor.  It's hard only because it's economics but she makes it as easy as she can.  Always available during office hours;  I was scared of econ but now I'm not anymore.  I'm really bad at math but she showed me how I can do the problems with algebra instead of integrals--now that's a teacher instead of just making me feel dumb!

Professor Cullen is awesome! super nice, flexible, and truly cares about her students. lectures are interesting. She lectures off of her slides that are posted on ted. On top of her shtuff! First week of class she already had most of the stuff for the quarter uploaded on ted. responds to questions and emails super fast!

Professor Cullen is a very nice, smart woman who is extremely enthusuastic about economics. Her tests are very difficult compared to the Aplia homework and are sometimes hard to get through. Office hours and inclass experiments were helpful. I recommend Cullen, but Econ100B itself is very difficult.

analysis.name: Curt Schurgers
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 76 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I had taken a circuits class before, but many concepts were still unclear to me. He explained them so well that I finally understand them now. If you start the practice exams early and well before the quizzes, you will do fine on the exams. His lectures are engaging because you actively solve problems and get direct feedback from him.
Yes, this is the man you need. If you want a real authentic engineering experience as you enter the ECE department. This is the man from Belgium you want.

Has a whole discussion section dedicated to improving our studying strategies. Lectures feel like brain teasers sometimes, but useful for learning. Alongside the course, I highly recommend just going through a circuits textbook to fill in the gaps before the quizzes, and just to solidify your mental model of the material, in general. Curt is goated

Conceptually difficult and the tests are hard, but Curt does a great job of giving students all the resources they need to succeed. Whether that be constant tutoring hours, tons of previous exams to study with, or his bootcamps. If you can manage your time well and study effectively, you can do well. If you only try to memorize, expect to fail.

Coming in with previous coding experience certainly helps, however, I think if you work hard you can learn it quick enough. Importantly, he emphasizes how different concepts work together. He provides the textbook which there are online quizzes for but they're easy if you do the reading. Exams are fair and open book/notes. Highly recommend.

analysis.name: John Curington
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing Professor! It was my favorite class of the quarter and I was so happy to finally get an A in a bio class. Definitely take this professor!

A really conscientious, caring professor. Also volunteers at the school free clinic for homeless people. Used humor and clinical stories in lectures. Though BICD100 is a huge class, Dr. John made the extra effort to learn your name if you came to office hours or asked him questions. Taking a class from a real doctor rocks!

One of my favorite lecturers at UCSD and it was his first time teaching BICD 100. His midterm was easy (his first test written) while his final was fair. People eased off thinking that his final was going to be easy as well but he explicitly said that it was going to be harder than the "easy" midterm. These people shouldn't cry about their grades.

This class is my favorite class! Curington is so funny! I just love attending lecture because he stutters and the things he say can be very funny. He has a great sense of humor. Sometimes he may be a bit boring when he just repeats himself like 3 times or even 4 times and when he just reads the slides. But still I love him and his class! :D

The lectures were exciting and the professor had a lot of clinical examples. The exams (mixture of multiple choice and free response) were pretty straightforward if you studied. Mastering Genetics helps to keep you up to speed. The professor is very sweet and animated; he makes genetics interesting. Best upper div bio experience so far!

analysis.name: Cynthia Lee
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She doesn't really teach you anything, it's all on you to read the book and teach yourself. Tests you on how well you write code under pressure. I don't see how that's helpful to beginners but whatever. It's a manageable A. She's super condescending in office hours. Ask the TAs for help!

Great prof! Very flexible and willing to help anyone who puts in the time to succeed. The class is a bit time consuming between the labs and assignments. She also gives participation points using clicker questions so you pretty much have to go to class. The midterms and final are pretty much from the lectures. If you put in the time it is an enjoyable class!  The TAs were also awesome! Very helpful and very accessible!
She's not bad. But it's hard to judge the professors in this course very comprehensively because of the really bad lecture format. But professor Lee was very clear, fun and a good teacher overall.

One of the best professors in the CSE department. I can see how this material would be difficult with another professor but Professor Lee gives so many examples and her homeworks/exams are very much based on the examples. Even the clicker questions really help you learn and when you go back to study those can be very useful. Overall, excellent prof

Great professor!! Lectures were clear and she took the time to explain everything which was really helpful for me as a first-time programmer. Go to class for the clicker points. Both midterms and the final exam were straight from lectures and labs. 1-page cheat sheet for each exam. TAs and tutors were extremely helpful during labs and tutor hours.

analysis.name: Cynthia Truant
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Simply wonderful. She's passionate & dedicated towards her subject and genuninely cares about her students. HIEU 129 had 2 take home midterms + study guide w/ all the possible questions for the finals. HIEU 131 had 1 essay, and study guides for final & midterm. Lots of reading and books to get, but are very interesting. I highly recommend her!!

This class is easy, especially if you choose the section option.  The readings are interesting, if a bit repetitive towards the end. Truant seems to really care about her students, to the point of wanting to get to know everyone in her lecture by name. Her lectures can be slow, but if you attend you don't always have to do the readings.

One of the most enjoyable classes I took for my regional specialization requirement at ERC. Taking a section option instead of the midterm is the best thing you can do. Susanne Hillman was the kindest, sweetest TA. The prof herself is very sweet but her lectures can be boring seeing that she talks so slowly. Regardless take the class!

Even though her lectures are incredibly dry, she is interesting. She assigns a TON of reading, but reviews it all in class, so just focus on the main themes of the class and you can get out of the superfluous reading. Lots of assignments, but overall an easy class. Also, visiting her in OH will almost guarantee you a better grade.

Requirements are straight forward, does give a study guide, but because of that is a bit tougher on grading.Midterm+essay+take-home final.Recommend if you are interested in the subject. If you'll take it for some requirement,you'll be bored. Professor is a real sweetheart and now and than would throw out some really funny jokes

analysis.name: Daniel Kane
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Daniel Kane is a great professor. He is a very clear lecturer, which is good because the material is tough and requires a deep understanding to answer questions of any real substance. If you get distracted and look at your phone for a few minutes, though, you may find yourself very lost. His tests are very hard, but he curves the class heavily.

He's a great lecturer - very enthusiastic, clearly knows what he's talking about, and explains concepts in a way that helps you understand WHY. He goes through a logical progression for how to approach and solve a problem, which is extremely important for figuring out homework/tests. His tests are difficult, but he curves the class VERY generously.

The class has a harsh grading scheme, the grading criteria isnt very clear it is just "justifiable" for proofs. The prof himself is really good but his lectures arent super clear, he writes and moves on fast but he is also open to even fundamental questions so that is good. His grading criteria is tough but he also gives a heavy curve

Sometimes confusing presentation (he needs to use less verbs and just get to the point), but made up for it by being really nice during office hours.  Also, I had a bit of a crush on him (Dr. Kane is pretty darn cute) so helped me focus :)

Prof Kane is a mathematical prodigy. I love his class. I learned so much. Sometimes when I see his handwriting I think his brain thinks way too fast and his hand just cannot catch up with his thoughts so he scribbles. It is kind of intimidating to talk to him because he is so smart. His class is one my fav at UCSD. I wouldnt want it any other way!

analysis.name: Danielle Raudenbush
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This was her first year teaching so she's more than likely to change things up. She has pop clicker questions to get students to attend her 8AM lectures. Sections are mandatory. Midterm and final are both blue book free-response so do the readings. Overall, the class was interesting although her lectures weren't because she just reiterates readings

Easiest class ever. The readings are in Canvas, and the lectures are not long if you simply put them in 2x speed. There are two midterms, a final exam, a response to weekly discussion posts, and a mandatory attendance discussion. The exams were open note, and as long as you write down what each lecture topic was, citing will be very easy.

Professor does not reply to emails. I sent several and did not receive email back. She does not give enough insight into what the midterm is going to look like. Online lectures are quite lengthy + she speaks in a very monotonous tone. She requires us to cite which lecture she discussed something in the midterm answers= this takes a lot of time!!

Professor Raudenbush really cares about the students and she wants you to do well. She did't grade our essays or tests, but they were relatively straightforward. You get more points if you know the names of the authors when you write your midterm and final tests. The class was pretty basic but enjoyable.

This class was both one of the easiest and most interesting courses I've taken. I enrolled in it to fulfill my DEI requirement, and it exceeded my expectations. The midterms were straightforward, and the course requirements were manageable, with weekly participation and discussion attendance.

analysis.name: Matthew Daugherty
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If he hadnt told us that it was his first time teaching the class, I would never have known. Theres a ton of material to learn, no way around it, but his lectures were excellent and his tests are extremely representative of the material he teaches. Plus theres extra credit! Def take his class if you wanna learn virology and actually enjoy it

Professor Daugherty tries to answer questions to the best of his abilities. But his exams are very difficult, especially the finals. He gets so intricate with the concepts that your memory fails you in the exams. 3 quizzes, 3 exams including finals worth 90% of your grade. He does not curve or round up, even when it's 0.05 pts to the next grade.

The entire grade comes from 3 quizzes and the midterm and final. Readings aren't mandatory for success because everything he expects you to known is covered in the lectures. The exams are extremely memorization heavy but fair. There was EC in the past but he doesn't offer it anymore but he does curve each exam.

He made the hardest tests I've ever taken at UCSD no matter how much I studied. Too much to grasp in 10 weeks. He gave vague instructions on what to study for exams. It would've been nice to know what to prioritize while studying. He's a good lecturer but just can't get over his impossible exams with insane detail. Also 90% of your grade = exams.

This class is difficult and heavy on memorization (perhaps excessively so), but Dr. Daugherty's lectures are highly interesting, comprehensive, and engaging. Almost all of your grade comes from exams. "Required" reading from textbook, but not actually necessary to read it to do well. 4% EC offered (+ more for SETs) and tests are *slightly* curved.

analysis.name: Jennifer Deal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor is developing the course and makes it very strict for not having her own stuff in order. Grading is unclear, + 5000-word peer project review that's due at the end, which had no gainful purpose. She was pretty condescending and chose to flex her background. I was left feeling frustrated, uneducated, and annoyed.

Pulls out grades out her ah! You have to participate a lot and of course attend the class every time. The group project will mess you with grading, since she provided no rubric or feedback and pulled grades out her ah crack. Also encourages us to use AI, but changes her mind 50 times about when can you use it or not.

She's an amazing person but the class can be a little work heavy especially if your group for the project is not very involved. However, the final and mt had reasonable Qs (MC+short ans) so if you study the lectures/book you should be good. There's a reading quiz every class 4 Qs, pretty easy but you need to buy the book or go to geisel reserves.

professor genuinely cares for students and loves what she teaches. very short MCQ quiz in the beginning of class and 1 midterm + final that are mostly short answer questions. there's a group project throughout the quarter so make sure to contribute because ur members rate you based on that. + a short 5 minute presentation on week 10

Professor Deal is one of the sweetest people I have met. She cares about her students and it honestly made me sad when people wouldn't participate. I had personal issues while taking her class and she was more than accommodating and considerate. A little unorganized with the assignments but overall funny and caring.

analysis.name: Dennis Trinidad
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 39 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is one of my favorite professors i've taken, his lectures are very engaging and he is a very caring professor. If you talk to him outside or after class he will put in the effort to get to know you, even though class isn't required it is usually pretty engaging. There isn't much homework and the midterm and final were online and very fair.

Class is easy if you're interested in it, I wasn't. All tests are open note and open book, so take good notes. The lectures are long and boring but podcasted. A few homework assignments, pretty easy, go to office hours if you have questions. The professor is genuinely so nice. A little math at the start. Only take if must tho, not elective material

I personally felt that attending lectures wasn't very valuable, since it seemed like Professor Trinidad mostly read off of the slides. The homework is very light. This class was my easiest so far in college. Professor Trinidad is very fair and goes easy on the students, probably just respecting the fact that this course is just an introduction.

He is a wonderful guy. He is truly so genuine, and you can tell he loves his job. He wants students to good in his class. Homework is simple and straightforward, exams are both on canvas on your own time, and they are heavily weighted but relatively easy. I didn't go to the lectures consistently but when I did you could tell how much he cares.10/10

You can tell the professor is passionate about the concepts, but the lectures are often repeating most of the lecture slides. Graded by HW (6 x 5%), midterm (30%), and final (40%) which are all relatively easy. Lectures are not mandatory and the slides are posted before classes, and no discussion sections. I would definitely recommend him.

analysis.name: Deepak Kumar
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great class but very high difficulty. The Programming assignments and exams are very difficult. His lectures are incredibly fast paced. He'll introduce a topic for the first time at the start of class and less than 30 minutes later will use applications of the topic assuming complete mastery but still not enough to do any of the assignments.

professor deepak is really kind, outgoing and lectures are engaging! he is also really funny. the PAs and exams were extremely difficult and lecture slides are usually 100+ pages which can be hard to keep up with. he responds really fast on piazza and I can tell he cares a lot for his students. overall, great professor and person!

This class is hard, but the professor is by far one of the absolute best in the CSE dept. If you loved Niema, you'll love Deepak even more. 5 PAs, about 2 weeks per PA. 2 exams. Curves based on rank. Top X = A, next X= B, both XYZ = c/d/f. Clearly extremely knowledgeable. But he CARES so much. Bro is a national treasure. TAKE HIS CLASSES!

Awesome professor with very engaging lectures!! :DD His tests are challenging but as long as you watch the lectures you will be okay :) Programming assignments are also super fun and he is very active on piazza so if you get confused he will answer pretty quickly. W class would take again!

Deepak is a really cool person and a good professor. He's really funny in class and also the assignments are really fun! Tests tho... are kinda scary

also he writes plays isn't that so cool

analysis.name: Devin Garofalo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely one of the best literature professors. She cares deeply about what each student thinks and wants everyone to improve. She really wants to hear your interpretation/analysis of the texts rather than simply grading you for having the right or wrong answers. For the midterm, she wrote a page of feedback for everyone which was really special.

Really cool professor. Classes are mandatory but grades based off reading completion and comprehension. Classes are just discussion style, talking about the readings seeing everyone's perspective. Teaches things none of my prior lit professors had taught before. For midterm got a whole letter of feedback. Definitely recommend, favorite professor!

If u have the opportunity to take a class w/ this wonderful woman, DON'T HESITATE TO TAKE THE CHANCE. This was my favorite lit class I've ever taken. She gave a page worth of feedback on our midterm in-class essay, I've never had a Prof do that before. Taught literary devices/ideologies that no Prof has bothered. Enthralling discussions/lecturing.
Incredibly nice lady, and her class discussions were unlike any class I have taken before. This class was probably the most intellectually stimulating lit class I have taken at UCSD.
Truly great prof. Graded on attendance, midterm and final. As long as you attend and do the readings you will succeed. Lectures are interesting if you actually engage. She is very cool.

analysis.name: Simrita Dhir
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Dhir is one of my favorite professors that I've ever taken. She is soo kind and you can tell she really wants you to succeed and really does listen to you and your thoughts. I really enjoyed her class. Although there was a lot of reading and having to discuss with others, she made class enjoyable! I recommended her to all my friends!!

She's a caring professor and very interested in students as individuals. Although she does repeat herself often taking up majority of class time, she is interested in what you have to say even it's similar to your peers. Very thorough with her critiques in writing that helps you create work you'll be satisfied with. Would recommend!

Writing is one of my favorite subjects however this teacher made me hate this class. She would repeat herself constantly and treat the class like we were kindergarteners. I have never hated a class so much and it wasn't even the material that was the issue. Sitting in that class was pure torture and there is no other way to put it.

I usually never rate my professor but for her I needed to she is amazing. Best writing Professor at UCSD. She doesn't give out as much work and really cares for her students. I am also taking her for WCWP 10B. That's how good she is. Would suggest picking her out of all the other writing professors.

Enjoyable and relaxing class. Dr Dhir is very kind. She is knowledgeable and passionate about teaching. Class readings, videos and discussions were fun. She gives prompt and detailed feedback on drafts. I was able to develop both projects very well. She makes every student feel special. I definitely recommend.

analysis.name: Dhananjaya Mukku
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Passionate teacher, great lecturer, interesting course. Class consists of 3 quizzes (each worth 30 points) and a cumulative final worth 40 points. One quiz dropped at the end. All quizzes and final taken via canvas (you have a 24 hour window). Extra credit via SONA.

Professor Mukku comes off as intimidating at first but he is really passionate about his studies and research. Attending his lectures and reviewing content after class is a must. Once you see how his first quiz is, you'll get a hang of the rest. This course requires a lot of studying, so if you procrastinate or don't like studying. Drop the course.

You know when people are really intelligent but arent the greatest teachers? Dr. Mukku speaks so fast and expects students to understand what hes talking about. His lectures are SUPER dense. Theres 3 open note tests and a final so its not terrible. Most students stopped showing up synchronously b/c hes not interactive and speaks too quickly.

analysis.name: John Czworkowski
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 153 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's such a nice guy but he isn't the best teacher. His tests aren't curved but they are pretty easy and fair. I hadn't taken ap chem in high school but I still managed to do pretty well in his class thanks to the book. His lectures were pretty useless plus he posts all his slides anyway. Overall the class wasn't bad. His teaching skills however….

Doesn't curve, MC choice tests that make you second guess, useless lectures. I pre-read the text, took notes, and did tutoring to understand what was going on. As a Prof, he's useless. Do not recommend.

Dr. C is a horrible teacher and on top of that doesn't have a curve. His tests are relatively easy, but there are under 20 questions so if you miss one it's like 6%. Sapling is easy and quick. His class has no extra credit or any curve. NOT RECOMMENDED.

I never really went to lecture cause I was taking Chem more as an interest than for a major, but his tests were pretty easy and representative of the book. He gives extra credit and also allows the option to drop one test. Granted, the other two big Chem profs are probably preferred in the sense that they "teach" better, but Dr C was pretty good.

Came to lecture everyday, when it got tough (ch 4, ch 9) I fell behind in the lectures, but if you stick to the book, do all the homework and make sure you understand each one (sapling gives you explanations - use em!) the midterms and the final are pieces of cake. Exactly what I wanted out of a class - I learned the material and gained an interest

analysis.name: Francesco Lanza Di Scalea
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He explained the concepts decently, and his usage of the chalkboard eraser as a beam helped with visualizing the concepts. Sometimes he'd go on tangents though for a while or explain a topic in a non linear manner, confusing the class. Though after lecture you'd look up the topic on YouTube and become even more confused... so it's not really him.

Professor Francesco Lanza Di Scalea is by the best solid mechanics professor I ever had. He's an inspirational and hilarious guy. Tests are straight forward. Do the homework and you will do just fine on the midterm. I highly recommend him.

The overall grade is graded based on 2 midterms and a final only. Study his notes & hw solutions and you'llbe fine. However, his lectures can be confusing sometimes & his written notes & explanations are unclear so definitely come to office hours for helps. Attendance is required and contributed to 10% of overall grade and lectures are not recorded
The lack of access to resources made this class kinda horrible. Lectures always made the content more confusing for me which added hours of relearning the material outside of class.

Lanza is one of the best at UCSD. His accent takes some getting used to, but once you do it's not a problem at all. Likes his students, and does a good job getting to know them. Attendence is mandatory and he takes roll from time to time. He will often put examples that he does in class on midterms and finals, so study what he does in class!

analysis.name: Dillon Chapman
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Take Strom. Hardest lectures I've ever had to sit through because they were so boring and we couldn't use electronics. Never did any of the readings though and still got an A. Grade determined by TA and anti racist grading policy means you can write whatever as long as it follows the prompt.

This review is for all three-quarters of DOC! Overall Professor Chapman is a great lecturer and she has a soothing tone when speaking! She is great at reminding students to do the assignments before the due date and she provides great personal examples of the essays and journals needed to be completed! Definitely would recommend it!

I didn't think she was bad but I do think her lectures were boring just cause of her teaching style and the way she spoke. Not very engaging with the material or with students, but I found the class itself to be really easy! Many of the mandatory lecture responses were difficult if you did not do the readings.

The class itself is not difficult so I'm assuming she has low ratings because of her attitude. She can be passive aggressive at times but it's not horrible. She will give examples of assignments and your grade is essentially determined by your TA. There is a good amount of reading but I've heard you can get away with summaries of the text.

Grade really depends on the TA. Frequent discussion time during class so I received more feedback/insights from peers than the professor herself. She started using worksheets in class at the end of the quarter and expected you to finish them by the end of class, which I personally think caused a mess. She can be insightful sometimes though.

analysis.name: Dixit Rishabh
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Horrible lecturer. Him + the TAs didn't explain the material well at all. I stopped attending lecture after the first few weeks bc there was no point. Exams are way more difficult than the practice he gave us, and I felt like I received little guidance. He gets irritated w questions. If you can't get a different prof just wait til next quarter.

Class felt like Math 20D on hard mode (2.3 GPA in class compared to 2.8 & 3.1 from other classes). Lectures were hard to follow so look up videos. He's new but shows signs of improving. A good reminder to practice self-study. You're not screwed if you take him. Grading scheme is very forgiving but midterms had lots of computation in little time.

First midterm average was 38/60. Lectures in general are confusing, written in cursive, barely even legible, and take a lot of time to take in. Lectures are not podcasted, notes uploaded inconsistent with what's taught. YouTube videos teach this 100x better, but there's only so many you can find for this class. At least practice similar to tests.

Lectures are not recorded, lecture notes are only posted until after the "topic" is finished (not posted after each lecture), very hard to read handwriting, and very low midterm averages. Goodluck to you if you don't go to lecture and actually pay attention. Avoid taking this prof unless you really have to. If not, wait for another quarter.

No recorded lectures. Tests didn't reflect lecture material or homework. Class averaged LOW on midterms and final. Unclear lecture notes. Numerical analysis is a tough subject with lots of studying required outside of class, but I don't think this teacher helped me as much as possible.

analysis.name: Dino Dinco
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Dinco is one of my favorites I've taken at UCSD. Every time we show up to class it just feels like hanging out with friends and laughing the whole time. He's very knowledgeable when working through projects and creating media. Highly recommend.

Do not take this professor. It's as simple as that. Don't let the low volume of reviews confuse you. He is not qualified and proved it with his unprofessionalism and lack of effort. This is a production course- and if you were, let's say, hoping to learn about production, then find another professor. Will fail if you miss class.

If you miss three (3) classes- you will fail the class. not a point reduction, not a letter drop, a fail, no matter what. claims it is to prepare you for the industry. does not teach in order to prepare you industry. outlandish standards with no credibility to back it up. do not take.

Ever heard of STEM classes designed to weed out students from the program? This is the film equivalent class. You're expected to hand in a project each week. It is designed to prepare you for the absolute demanding environment of film production. Giving constructive feedback is necessary, and phoning it in will only get you chewed out by the class.

Outstanding professor who is truly caring and thoughtful about his students, as well as fair, kind-hearted, and humorous. Class was always interesting and 3 hours seemed to go by in a flash (he always let us take a break in the middle). He gives extremely great feedback about everyone's work and I loved participating (and I'm usually not the type!)

analysis.name: Mamadou  Diagne
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Diagne seems to love teaching students. He often engaged with his students during lectures and actively solicits student feedback and questions. He doesn't record lectures and strongly encourages attendance, though it is not required. His homework is fair and allows students to correct their own work. He picks accessible textbooks.

Professor Diagne is an outstanding instructor who genuinely supports student learning. Coursework is fair, exams are reasonable with study, and he is always available for help, including review sessions before exams. His clear and engaging teaching style creates a challenging yet rewarding learning experience.

The professor truly cares about student learning. Homework is fair, and exams are manageable with proper study. He's approachable, offers Saturday review sessions before exams, and is always willing to help. Friendly and supportive, he makes the course both engaging and highly recommended.

I feel like the material could've been taught better. Half the time lectures seemed very unhelpful. But he does explain well if he understands the question. Exams were curved which was life-saving. Homework is not bad at all. If you want to truly understand and learn material, might not be best class.

analysis.name: Dmitri Zurita
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Zurita is so passionate about his job, he is so caring and the material he teaches in class is different from all the film classes I have been taking. a lot of time I fee like I can just learn the stuff professors saying from YouTube video but professor Zurita invite you to have critical view into art and grow as both a person and artist

Professor Zurita is an astounding teacher who inspires students and creates a safe space in the classroom for all types of art to be shared. He provides good critique and grades at the end of the quarter to give students enough time to do the best they can on assignments. He's just a chill guy, grades easily, and brings out the best in students.

Easily one of the best professors at UCSD. His teaching is unorthodox but the results speak for themselves. He made the class feel safe and was always encouraging us to follow our own paths. In his class I found my voice as an artist and made more friends than I have in years here because of the community he creates in class.

WARNING
for the girls or guys who are willing to take this class to learn film - 
he will push you to do naked pictures/films. if you didn't do anything HAM
which is like being naked or actually hurting yourself(I'm serious), he will question you for not taking the class seriously.
doesn't grade till the end of the quarter, but the grades are easy.
