Best professor I've ever had. Always pushes students to care deeply about their work. Would definitely take his class again.

analysis.name: Dominik Wodarz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Do not be fooled by the quizzes. The final is 100x harder. I was talking a walk under a warm, sunny day and then a tornado swept me away at the end of the road.

You need to be good at making and applying connections—like case studies. Otherwise, the Prof is great at teaching and passionate about his work. Material is explained very clearly.

Dude was generous with the curve. I hope he keeps the final exam format, as it was meticulously crafted and a good representation of student understanding. Had he exposed students to problem solving questions through HW and quizzes, I reckon his ratings would be higher. There is a gap between his teaching (great) and student preparation (lack of).

Mostly a memorization heavy class. His midterms are 75% word for word practice problems, and he holds a review session during lecture before every test His final, however, is much more difficult than any of the midterms, and he doesn't really warn you about this. Cram hard and study everything a few days before the final and you will be fine.

You have a couple of quizzes then a final. A large part of the quiz will come from the review questions he gives out, but don't be a fool. For the final, he switched it up on us and put hard questions. The mean score for the final was 69% Def was an uncool move on his part. Had a B+ for most of his class, but will likely end with a C+ now

Not bad, but his slides are a bit disorganized. He does not split them up by lecture, and handwriting can be illegible at times. His explaining makes up for it well enough. I found the content very interesting and quizzes were fair, questions are usually word for word from the practice questions he does in class. Heard the final will be bad tho...

analysis.name: Benjamin Doller
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Doller is very kind and nice. I felt like there was a lot of busy work in this class and they took a long time to grade assignments. It was a pretty easy class, but just a little boring for me.
Lectures can be kind of dry, but he is pretty chill otherwise and gives out easy assignments. Took him for 8B which I found very fun.

I really like Professor Ben Doller! I've had him for two classes and his upper division literature classes are small, close-knit, and very enjoyable. All the projects are very creative and doable, he is also very helpful if you have any question about literature in general; he helped me create a poetry portfolio. I highly recommend taking him!

analysis.name: Janna Dickenson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 65 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Would not reccomend this class, so much busywork and the topics are a lot less interesting than you'd expect.

So, so nice and clearly cares a lot about her students. I've taken her for PSYC 100 and PSYC 172, and both classes deal with some sensitive topics. She takes a lot of care in keeping everyone comfortable and engaged, which I really appreciated. I would take her again and again! Exams are fairly easy (cheat sheet is allowed!)

She's a fine and caring teacher but her lectures are so unclear, she never gets to the main point and rambles on a lot about things that aren't in the exams. The questions are all application based and the answer choices are all technically "correct" but have to choose the best one. 3 in person exams, 1 dropped which is nice.

personally, her lectures and slides were all over the place that i just stopped attending. her exams are application based, so pay close attention to wording. she prob wont implement the online quizzes/exams anymore because of FA25. attendance is extra credit and she drops lowest exam and quiz which are both open note. wouldnt take again ngl

Prof. Dickenson was an ok - a little boring to me but she was nice and loved to answer questions. Grade was made up of 2/3 exams and 8/9 quizzes. Everything was open book but exams were still confusing. Can get extra credit for attendance and requires SONA (about 4% of grade). She's not a bad prof but I knew too much of the material to be engaged.

analysis.name: Doug Nitz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He seems very upbeat but even sitting in the front his lectures just seemed like a bunch of blab. Class was full during the first week but a bunch of people dropped it by the 3rd class. You're graded on two tests. Very monotone so make it's hard to understand

He doesn't post his slides, lectures are a lot of talking in circles or bragging about his work. He seems like those researchers who cares too much about fame/status. 2 exams is your whole grade (wk 6&10), slides are confusing & just copy-pasted research articles, SUPER dense & not helpful. Everyone in class looked confused & most people dropped.

Not tech savvy, doesn't post slideshows, says attendance isn't mandatory but be warned, the podcast does not catch any audio or chalkboard drawings (which he relies on more than slides). His slideshows are compromised of paragraphs. The mean for midterm 1 was 63%, and instead of rethinking his teaching style he told us we need to study harder...

good prof, cares about student understanding. If he writes it on the board its not on the slides and it is on the test, so pay close attention to those and copy his board work down! lots of EC in tests, grade is based on 3 tests (including final) all weighted equally and a mix of multiple choice and fill in the blank, no free response. Solid prof.

Professor Nitz is a very down to earth, hilarious and brilliant teacher.  This class is purely driven by research papers on a very complex subject but he explains them very well in class and has helpful slides.  The entire grade is on 2 tests (about 10 questions total), but he gives the questions out a week before. There's no excuse not to do well!

analysis.name: Noelia Dominguez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Loved her class; she seemed to really care for her students as she created a rapport. Attendance is mandatory yet flexible. Assignments were well thought out, complex and not stressful. I really recommend taking Profe Dominguez's classes

Prof Dominguez really cares about her students and gives plenty opportunities to practice Spanish. Participation and attendance are mandatory, but she cancels Friday classes. Half of the classes are w the TA (covers grammar), the other half with the Prof (goes over textbook). The weekly movie assignments were fun! No tests, just a final project.

Professor Dominguez genuinely cares about her students. Her class was really easy but still worthwhile. Enjoyed talking to her, definitely get the sense that she is fun and kind, it truly matters to her that we do well.

I loveeeeee professor Dominguez. She's so kind, so understanding. She does have weekly writing assignments and some projects, but they're easy. She doesn't judge you regardless if your Spanish is bad. (lol) She's also very inclusive. 
Easy class, love the professor.

If you have to take this spanish course, take this professor ! One of the best i've had at UCSD she is super caring and funny. She won't judge if you can't say certain words in spanish she allows you to say them in english. Assignments are super easy and quick.

analysis.name: Dovi Kacev
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was interesting, but I didn't love how it was split between two profs. The lectures were really interesting, but the tests blindsided me. We don't get any practice tests so I honestly went into it not knowing what to expect, and it focused way too much on species. Other than that, i enjoyed the discussion sections and Dovi is very kind

Great professor! Graded on discussion participation, weekly quizzes, a term paper, & a final exam. Lectures were podcasted. Discussion required a pre-posted question and speaking during the section for credit. The term paper on marine mammals included multiple assignments with feedback. Final exam was in-person, closed-note (mainly short answer)

Unfortunately Dovi is completed inaccessible. He will not respond to emails, an issue that I discussed with many many other students who experienced the same. Setting up a meeting (since he has no designated office hours) was impossible-he did not respond for weeks. Students reach out for help and he isnt there, it makes it difficult to praise him.

amazing, chill prof. one of the best I have had so far, really cares about students. doesn't give too many assignments and the ones he does give is just to make sure you are getting and understanding material. tests were on material learned in class it was more just applying the info. 1000% would recommend and take again.

Great lectures, cool shirts, reasonable grading, a little inaccessible for contact outside of class but he seems to have a lot going on back and forth between SIO campus and main campus classes? Overall would absolutely recommend bc the class was still great and well instructed.

analysis.name: Dontarie Stallings
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 176 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Hilarious, super nice guy. Multiple choice, grade replacement system, definitely take him! In general, chem is hard but seriously he's a great teacher who makes hard topics easy and is all around just a delight. Love him and I will probably get an A. I will be taking him hopefully in the future!

The book wasn't very helpful for this class. Do all of the weekly assigned quizzes, those are most likely to come up on the exams. There are two midterm exams and the first two sections have a replacement option on the final. Lectures are recorded. Overall, Stallings is a great professor!

Honestly, if there were one thing I could do differently, I would go back and attend every lecture, even if it was at 8 am, because as long as you keep up with regular lecture attendance and do not chatGPT every homework, you will do very well. He is very respected in the chemistry department; overall, a fantastic dude. Watch out for bears!

Great in the sense that he's easy to talk to but lectures and hw didn't really reflect the difficulty of the exams. Sometimes he will go off topic during to keep students engaged. I liked the way he graded as exams did not make up most of one's grade. He allows cheat sheets and had a grade improvement plan. Hated how Achieve was required and $$.

He is not the best lecturer but definitely thinks he is. His grading is pretty generous, and the class is curved. I got a D on both midterms and failed the final and still got a B-. I only had to take one chem class so I didn't try. If you but any effort at all you'll be fine. It's an intro class so he really isn't trying to fail anyone.

analysis.name: Drew Hoffman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Writes vague test questions, each test feels like its trying to constantly trick you over minutia unrelated to the content. Classes like this are basically just memorizing the results of previous Psych research, it isn't important enough to be worth the amount of time invested in Hoffman's tests, where each question is worth 1% of your grade.

Almost guaranteed to get her for any COGS GE courses. She is very fair and interested in her content (the content overlaps with COGS101B quiet a bit). However she is mostly graded by her tests, which require a lot of inferring (which leads to a lot of disputes). Study the lecture notes carefully, possible to get a B or C but still hard.

This class had some of the most poorly written tests I have ever seen. Other than the myriad of confusing typos (in spelling and syntax) the answers were frequently contradictory and used terms never mentioned in lecture. This is unfortunate because the 3 embarrassments of multiple choice tests are worth 80% of your grade.

Much more of a philosophy course than a science course which can be misleading, and many figures mentioned in class hold prejudiced views when looked up. It makes the course feel tone deaf at best, eugenicist at worst. Assignments and final project were not well organized with little feedback, course size didn't suit a discussion-based structure.

professor hoffman is super nice and her lectures are very clear (she spends a lot of time explaining in different ways so that it sticks), the class structure and teaching style reminds me of 14a with professor creel. attendance in lectures and discussion arent mandatory and all lectures are recorded

analysis.name: Mark Dresser
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Not a fun class to sit through as it dragged on forever during some lectures. The only bright spots was the sometimes we would have live performances which were really cool. I did not like the concert reports as I do not enjoy having to go far and spend money to turn in what is homework. Grading is really slow in this course.

This man has no concept of what an appropriate workload for already overwhelmed students is. This was a class for non-music majors and he indunated everyone with complex music theory and 20+ pages worth of papers (EXCLUDING MIDTERM AND FINAL). He's kind and passionate but this class was genuinely the worst class I have taken at UCSD.

This is one of the worst classes I've ever taken. There are so many papers and so much reading. If you have no music background you won't stand a chance. This class bored me out of my mind, I learned nothing, and I don't even like jazz anymore. Also, there are kind of a lot of papers, so if you don't like to write, pick an easier UD writing class.

When he taught the basic musicianship class he made it really difficult. He quizzed us every week on melodic and rythmic dictation, sight singing, pulse fields, and interval ear training. I wouldn't take him for basic musicianship, his expectations are way to high and he doesn't seem to understand that other people have other classes to study for.

Although this guy's comments below mine are so thoughtful, I think I'll add some more info.  SUPER EASY for anybody, the profs (there were 3 that quarter) laid out everything on the tests and really short essays.  The foreign guys were a little hard to listen to, but not much to complain about. the class may be totally different next year, though.

analysis.name: Andrew Meyertholen
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 92 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: you can tell that meyertholen truly cares. even though his final and 4 quizzes (where you drop the lowest one) are difficult, he curves the class fairly to keep the class average reasonable. the material for 2b was still very challenging. he has mandatory iclicker (graded for participation not credit), discussion, and pre-lecture questions.

Won't lie - physics is really hard. But there are many opportunities to succeed. The homework is a lot harder than the quizzes, but I don't think a lot of people do it (costs $65 to access). Meyertholen's flipped class format is great practice, but you need to add more as needed. Overall, you have to fight hard for a good grade.

I joined this class feeling very insecure after getting wrecked by physics 2A and I just naturally hated this subject. However, this professor completely changed my mind and made me fall in love with E&M. Not gonna lie, I worked really hard and his exams are pretty challenging, but you will learn a lot. He is just an amazing lecturer no doubt.

Professor Meyertholen is an amazing professor and overall a really caring guy. It was his first quarter at UCSD and he wasnt confused or lost at all and gave great lectures. He posts everything on his course website so it makes it really easy to go back and study. He has mandatory pre class questions (homework) and clicker questions.

One of the best professor's I've ever had! Personally I am not good with physics but this guy made it very easy to understand. He really cares about teaching and knows his material very well. Great feedback when asking questions and quizzes are really fair if you put in the work.

analysis.name: Andrew Huberman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's like the Justin Timberlake of neuroscience; legit though. He is really knowledgeable, down to earth, lectures are attention holding, really good class. No textbook, readings consist of modern research papers. Recommend.

Dr. Huberman is a great lecturer. The material can be intimidating (seems to be taught at a graduate level) but his main goal is to invoke scientific curiosity and teach students how to analyze and understand scientific papers. He assigns papers each week for a group to analyze and present during section. Very good practice for the MT and final.

Dr. Huberman is one of the few exceptional teachers that truly cares about his students' learning. He won't force you to memorize asinine facts -- instead he'll give you the tools to learn neuroscience from research, like an actual neuroscientist does.  He is a gifted, captivating lecturer and great at explaining complex material. Highly recommend!
One of the most student-centric professors at UCSD. Easy class, interesting, you learn some cool material,  overall very enjoyable academic class.   Take him if you can.

He's an entertaining and knowledgeable lecturer if you choose to go to lecture. One group project, a midterm, and a final. Discussion is mandatory but you just go over papers, which you should read because they help you prepare for the exams. Learn the different methods used and you'll do well. Easy A class as long as you do a little work!

analysis.name: Rachel Dudley
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Class consisted most on group work, and attendance was mandatory as there was a quiz at the end of lecture every day. Found her to be VERY picky on her grading criteria. Not the most approachable, so I mostly relied on the TA who I'd recently had as a teacher. She was okay, just not the best.

The professor was okay but not great at explaining concepts and could come off as unapproachable. The class is easy with mostly group work and little outside effort. The final is the main assignment and could've been online. Only take it if you're interested in linguistics.
Probably the worst linguistics professor I've ever had to deal with. Tough grader, won't accommodate to your needs, always dtm.

analysis.name: Andrew Kummel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 255 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: He's a really chill teacher and funny but his tests have no chill. He uploads notes and practice tests online, along with hosting 2 practice exams before every test but its still pretty hard for those who arent good with chem. Half the questions are conceptual and the other half are math based. Good luck if you have his class.

Really entertaining class, Kummel cracks a lot of jokes. He hosts 2 practice exams and gives 2 more takehome exams every time before an actual exam and those help a lot. Funny story, for exo reactions that won't stop and can't stop until a reagent is all used up, he played Miley Cyrus's "We Can't Stop" in lecture. Loved going to his classes.

He's a smart guy but can't communicate his knowledge very well. He goes through the information too quickly and never goes into detail, rarely explaining stuff that's important for the 3 MIDTERMS (and final). You're better off reading the textbook and his slides, not worth getting up at 8 am. Pro: midterms are similar to practice ones

Professor Kummel is extremely knowledgable and intelligent, but sometimes he assumes we are too and doesn't explain certain concepts in enough detail. Nonetheless, he often tries to explain concepts through real-world analogies that can sometimes be helpful. Tests are very tough, but he holds two review sessions before every test.

He's funny, but his teaching style is not my cup of tea. He uses analogies that I couldn't really get, and his exams are extremely difficult. He offers many practice midterms and review sessions, but in the end, it felt like I knew more about taking his tests than knowing the material. Heavily conceptual class.

analysis.name: Songzi Du
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Uncaring, lectures extremely difficult to follow. Feels like he's out to get you, because he is. All I know is he took a break from teaching, and apparently used to be good. Something happened while he was away, and now I consider him one of the worst professors I've had in the ECON department. The only positive is his exams being nearly identical.
A little hard to understand because the microphone would keep on cutting off his speech, but everything is on the slides. Exams matched all of the like 10+ practice exams provided.

A great man. Lectures cover relevant material for exams, practice/past exams he provides are almost identical to the upcoming exams. He extended my due date by three days on an assignment when I switched into his Econ 171 class during week 2. He's awesome.

Now I can say I know a lot about CAPM model and expected utility theory. Professor Du is the perfect pofessor at UCSD. The Lecture is clear and recorded. The tests are fair and he is approachable and caring! My only regret is I took 100C with another professor a quater before he is the instructor.

Professor Du teaches students in a fairly easy and understandable way. The course materials can be hard but he never confuses you with things you don't need to know. That being said, his exams were very fair based on what was taught in class. I would definitely recommend him.

analysis.name: L. Jean Dunn
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you are a student who is genuinely interested in learning about the courses topic, you will be disappointed by this professors inability to lecture, create a presentation with any kind of logical organization, and a total incompetence to clarify topics when he is asked questions. He is simply the worst professor at UCSD. Avoid at all costs.
Homework isn't representative of class material, lectures are boring. It's doable but not fun

Grade consists of 4 HW assignments 20%, midterm 30%, and final 50%. Homework graded on completion, lectures were absolutely boring. Cool professor but man hard to stay awake, usually never went the full 3 hours. Both exams were 50 MCQ each, meaning missing even one question would hurt your final grade a lot. Posts study guides for exams, helpful.

homework assignments were easy, but completely irrelevant to midterm/final. lecture was boring, but if you paid attention, it did help for the exams (heavy studying). asked random questions about what school he attended. also yelled at our TA in front of the class and went on interesting rant where he referred to himself in the 3rd person.
We only had 4 HW assignments and they are all graded as either 100%, 85% or 0. Very fair teacher but if you miss anything you're a little screwed

analysis.name: Dusan Keres
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If this is your first physics class ever DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR'S CLASS. Considering this is an introductory class, the way the prof teaches it, it definitely requires a lot of foundational knowledge/background. The class is very test heavy and weekly exams are pretty difficult, so if you're not a good test taker, this class isn't ideal.

This class is graded very heavily on quizzes which are 51 percent of your grade. 4 quizzes and one gets dropped. Each quiz has 9 points with 5 mcqs (1 point each) and 2 frqs (2 points each). The FRQs are fair and there is generous partial credit, but some of the mcq questions seem to be tricking you; very stressful (1 mcq is 11 percent of your quiz

The lack of effort put into this class by the professor compared to any other physics 2 astounding. All he does is assign homework from the book and give quizzes. The professor adds nothing to the learning and is also hard to understand in lecture. You're better off just self studying, but attendance is also mandatory. 10% attendance 90% quiz+final

I think he is a better 2C professor than other courses. He is more knowledgeable about topics like fluids, thermo, light, and sound, so he was able to answer questions in ways that made logical sense. His lectures are monotone, but understandable. He didn't overcomplicate the topics beyond being able to use the equations to solve the problems.

Sort of a sleepy teacher during the lecture. Quizzes + Final are worth an insane 90% of the grade and each quiz is only 5 MCQ and 2 FRQ. There are no practice quizzes/finals either, and no cheat sheet. Homework is just assigned problems from the textbook.

analysis.name: Nur Duru
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
- amazing professor, nice, caring, passionate
- curriculum is created by muir college, professor has no control over it but she tries her best to help you be successful
- lots of reading and writing but nothing too difficult

Super nice and understanding. The class looking back was not hard pretty similar to AP Lang. Muir Writing just recently changed the grading scale so def not as hard as it was in the past. She has no control of the class but I still think she makes it pretty fair. Very interesting to listen to. Would've loved her for literally any other class.

I really liked this prof. The curriculum created by muir college is rough/hard and not her fault, but she does her best to help you and make sure you're successful despite it. If you think something is unfair its prolly a muir rule not hers. She really nice and gives clear feedback. She's also really accessible through email and office hours.

She seemed like she cared about us doing well and provided good feedback on the writings we had to do. There's 3 paragraphs and a 2000 word essay, but she doesn't have control over the material. Feedback was slow and there was a lot writing at times, but she gave as many points as possible to help. just turn in ur things on time and youll be fine.

Gotta make sure to be on top of the schedule and readings as she won't always remind people and you will be expected to know it in class. She says that a physical version of the textbooks from the bookstore are needed but realistically you can get away without using them. Very caring but won't take bs

analysis.name: Ioana Dumitriu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She genuinely cares about the students and is always available outside of class via Piazza. Her lectures are clear and she always makes sure the students are not getting lost along the way. The lecture material is representative of the exam material, and there aren't any curveballs. 100% would recommend this professor, best in the math department!

Sincerely one of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures are clear, direct, and extremely captivating. She always tries to make sure no one has any unanswered questions, and personally responds to every Piazza post within a few hours at most. Exams and homeworks are fair and instructive. I looked forward to every lecture. Highly recommend!

Dumitriu is a sweetheart, very caring and happy to answer any questions in office hours or during class. Also gives clear lectures that are easy to understand. The HW is reasonable, the lectures should give you all the info you need. The grading is heavily weighted on a midterm and final, but there are lots of practice problems to help you prepare.
The class content is very interesting and she explains everything well. Leture notes are also posted so you can spend more time listening to the lectures rather than writing down notes.

The book is more straightforward and clearer than the lectures and slides in my opinion. midterm and final are not hard but very tricky. You have to pay attention to the examples talked about during lectures. The weekly quizes are not hard if you read the book carefully. No extra credit and curve.

analysis.name: Neal Dykmans
